Exposition rétrospective où elle montre: Retrospective exhibition where she shows the Room Dividers woven. Consequences: Minutiae structure will recall these weavings
Evelyn Bullock costumée pour la fête cos: Evelyn Bullock costumed for the Summer Art Institute costume party of 1949, photographed by Dina Woelffer.
Fuller autorise Larsen à développer les: Fuller allows Larsen to develop the Dymaxion principles, which it will use in particular in its teaching by modeling tenegrity structures. models: tetrahedron, octahedron, icosahedron, vector-equalibrium, compact stacking of spheres Consequences: She will teach “par lesquels la nature se construit elle-même” principles
Exposition personnelle recensée dans le: Personal exhibition recorded in the New York Times, giving him national recognition. review in the New York Times
Fuller invite Emerson Woelffer, enseigna: Fuller invites Emerson Woelffer, a teacher at the ID since 1942, former WPA (1938), then noted nationally (Whitney Annual, first personal exhibition in New York at the Artist's Gallery). His wife Dina, a Harry Callahan photographer, also teaches that summer.
L'intérêt des étudiants et le soutien de: The interest of the students and the support of Charles Olson lead the college to invite the potter Robert Turner, trained at Alfred University, to inaugurate a pottery program. Albers, who resigned earlier in the year, had always opposed it, judging the clay without rigour, from the “art de cendriers”. Consequences: Birth of ceramics to BMC.
L'atelier de poterie est conçu et constr: The pottery shop is designed and built by architect Paul Williams in consultation with Turner, who thinks it as a production pottery. Turner notes having been left alone, kept away from the divisive policies of the college, occupied by the construction of the workshop and the oven. Turner actually lent the college the funds to build the pot shop (note 2)
Voulkos gagne le Ceramic National de 194: Voulkos won the 1949 Ceramic National at the Everson Museum while still undergraduate at Montana State University; The award won him the direction of the Archie Bray Foundation, a newly established residence in Helena. Before Black Mountain, he did functional pottery with rich enamels, brush strokes and incised lines. Consequences: He will meet with Hamada, Leach and Yanagi a few months after they moved to Black Mountain in 1952
Cage rencontre le compositeur français P: Cage meets French composer Pierre Boulez on a trip to Paris; Boulez was inspired by Artaud (notably in his Second Piano Sonata, 1948) to dismantle melodic and thematic conventions. Consequences: first link in the chain leading to Artaud to Black Mountain
Cours d'été d'Olson que l'étudiant Mark: Olson summer class that student Mark Hedden quotes as starting a decisive turn away from the literary drama, towards “un nouveau concept du théâtre” that Theater Piece No. 1 would accomplish three years later. Olson presents “Wagadu”, a mythical story inspired by Soninke legends and taken from African Genesis (1937): reading by Olson, music by Pete Jennerjahn, decorations by Dan Rice; Olson describes it as “jointure of speech-sound-motion, projection-melody-gesture”. Direct Previous of Theater Piece No. 1 Non-linearity Consequences: “The Glyph Exchange” Olson Preparation
Anni Albers devient la première artiste: Anni Albers became the first textile artist to have an individual exhibition at the New York Museum of Modern Art. Consequences: The following year, the Albers moved to New Haven, Connecticut.
Un ballot de momie de Paracas déballé en: A bundle of paracas mummy unsealed in 1949 contained a 11'3" wide fabric; The fabric is now in Lima. 11 feet 3 inches wide fabric
Exposition individuelle au Museum of Mod: Individual exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art, then broadcast across the United States for more than three and a half years. Tour duration: more than three and a half years.
L'ancienne étudiante Hazel Larsen Archer: Former student Hazel Larsen Archer is named first and only full-time photography teacher of the college; photography becomes a more permanent part of the course catalogue. Consequences: Institutionalization of photography at BMC, culminating with the summer institute 1951.
Rauschenberg photographie l'intérieur au: Rauschenberg photographes the austere interior of the Quiet House: white stucco walls, two identical chairs in a corner, diagonal light strip through one of nine square windows light ray tangent to the ear of the left chair, triangular shadow on the seat Consequences: Testimony of the influence of Archer on its attention to light
MoMA et la National Foundation for Infan: MoMA and the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis organise a poster competition for vaccine research; 24 artists and photographers participate for a cash prize; The first prize goes to Herbert Matter (two children jumping to the rope, legend “One of them had polio–skilled teamwork brought recovery”) 24 participants, silver prize; the reproduction of the Archer poster hanging on the same wall as his photos Consequences: Public reminder of the Archer polio itself
Le MoMA acquiert le tableau d'Andrew Wye: The MoMA acquires Andrew Wyeth's painting showing Christina Olson, with polio, lying in a field, back to the viewer, facing the house at the bottom Consequences: Most famous artistic representation of a subject affected by polio
MoMA organise un concours d'affiches pou: MoMA organizes a poster contest for polio research. The first prize goes to Herbert Matter; Archer participates and earns $500 for its bid. Dorothea Lange, guest, declines; Tana Hoban, Esther Bubley and Margaret Bourke-White contribute. Matter winning poster: two children jumping side by side, legend “One of them had polio – skilled teamwork brought recovery”; Archer poster: photo of two young children in the centre, “Don't be afraid” above, “Knowledge is a weapon against polio” below; Archer price: $500 Consequences: A miniaturized version of the Archer poster was glued next to his photographs in the Steichen exhibition, linking the two
MoMA acquiert le tableau de Wyeth (peint: MoMA acquired Wyeth's painting (painted 1948), representing Christina Olson, paraplegic after polio, lying in a field. Wyeth substituted for Christina's body the younger and valid one of his wife Betsy. Remarkable coincidence: this acquisition, the Archer poster and its photographs of Asawa and Quiet House occupy MoMA's orbit the same year. Christina propelled herself with her arms; left hand and wick of black hair directed to the house at the bottom Consequences: the painting makes the body a place of social production
Après le Milwaukee State Teachers Colleg: After Milwaukee State Teachers College then Black Mountain College, Asawa, born in 1926 in southern California, moved to San Francisco in 1949 and resided there until his death in 2013. Consequences: the beginning of her mother-artist community
En visitant le logement temporaire de se: By visiting the temporary accommodation of his parents (a room of the former Japanese language school), Asawa deplores the uniformity of thousands of American houses: one in five “pense pareil” houses because painted in pink, etc. Six people sleep in a room the size of the Peggy living room; “It is terrifying”
Avant son arrivée à San Francisco, Asawa: Prior to his arrival in San Francisco, Asawa collaborates with Tolk-Watkins on a collection of “poemstories”: black line drawings on white paper; for the poem of the six-striped tiger, she imagines vertical rows of postage stamps, the undulations of the postage stamp serving as temporary legs. Black ink drawings on white paper; Postage stamps and postmarks Consequences: Project likely unfinished; Tolk-Watkins publishes Pigs Ate My Roses without Asawa drawings
Tolk-Watkins confie son conflit entre rô: Tolk-Watkins entrusts his conflict between mother and artist role and thanks Asawa for a frog (origami jumping, “elle saute admirablement”); Asawa encourages her to embrace maternity unreservedly. Citations of the two letters reproduced in quotations
Réception de mariage estivale 1949 chez: Summer wedding reception 1949 at Corbett on Wolfback Ridge, facing the ocean and bay. Asawa wears a black dress in fabric offered by Anni Albers, sewn by Johanna Jalowetz (mother of Trude Guermonprez) in short-cut long skirt suit after the ceremony. Charlotte Schlesinger plays the piano. Asawa has difficulty reciting his vows; Baby Ragland Watkins crawls on the floor. Low meal: cold charcuterie and champagne. Black dress in fabric by Anni Albers; dymaxion ring drawn by Fuller; charcuterie and champagne; Ragland baby crawling on the floor; “Ils riaient tous et nous pleurions et nous riions”
Fuller conçoit l'alliance de mariage en: Fuller designs the wedding alliance by describing it in the same terms as its architectural experiences.
Le couple s'installe à San Francisco, at: The couple moved to San Francisco, attracted by low rent and affordable living. Cheap rents; a single income could support a large family. Consequences: Installation in Noe Valley, material condition of future engagement of Asawa in schools.
Asawa écrit à Albert Lanier : « There is: Asawa writes to Albert Lanier: “There is no genius in my hands” (“Il n'y a pas de génie dans mes mains”), a formula that summarizes his rejection of modern artistic engineering. Consequences: Becomes the title sentence of the conclusion of Troeller's book
Rauschenberg étudie dans le programme in: Rauschenberg studies in the Bauhaus program from Josef Albers to Black Mountain College; That's when he starts using the glue. Consequences: Beginning of collage at Rauschenberg, which leads to collages of 1952 and then the combinations.
Étudie au printemps 1949 auprès de Josef: Studyed in the spring of 1949 with Josef Albers and his wife Anni; This is the final year of teaching from Albers to Black Mountain, which his former students consider his best.
Rauschenberg s'engage dans la photograph: Rauschenberg entered photography in the late 1940s during his stay at Black Mountain College; he hesitates a time between painting and photography as a career before choosing both. Consequences: La photography becomes the cornerstone of all his work
Susan Weil fait découvrir à Rauschenberg: Susan Weil makes Rauschenberg discover the method of exposure of photosensitive blueprint paper to light, creating photographs without camera. Silhouettes on 1:1 scale on blue background: hands of Weil gripping branches and twigs, feet, foliage, contorted bodies filling the paper to the edges, evoking the Man of Vitruvius. Consequences: Series of blueprints, many do not survive.
Pendant son premier trimestre à l'Art St: During his first term at the Art Students League (autumn 1949), Rauschenberg made a work today lost consisting of collecting the prints of his comrades' feet on the threshold of the school. Consequences: Anticipe Automobile Tire Print (1953).
Série de gravures sur bois parmi les pre: A series of wood engravings among the first works employing seriality: the board is gradually striated with incised lines, the image passing from black to white in fourteen stages; one of the rare works (excluding photographs) preserved from that year fourteen stadiums, from black to white, incisions on wooden block
Pendant son premier trimestre à l'Art St: During his first term at the Art Students League in the autumn of 1949, Rauschenberg collected the footprints of his student comrades passing the school threshold; work today lost footprints on the threshold of the school Consequences: Anticipe Automobile Tire Print (1953)
Début effectif de sa carrière ; son voca: Effective beginning of career; His artistic vocabulary (sequences, grids, duplications, glimmers, inversions, counterpoint between addition and withdrawal, human scale) was established in the first four years.
Sa préoccupation pour la photographie en: His concern for photography in 1949 arose from an intimate conflict between curiosity and shyness: the camera served as a social shield, a permit to observe.
Passe l'été dans la maison de famille de: Spend the summer in Susan Weil's family home, where she discovers the method of exposure of blueprint paper (cyanotype). Consequences: Blueprint series with Weil
The Club ouvre à la fin de 1949 ; des di: The Club opened at the end of 1949; Discussions are taking place on Zen Buddhism, which according to Valerie Hellstein feeds a rhetoric of literacy and directness. Consequences: This rhetoric joins that of Cage and the critical discourse around Rauschenberg, contradicting the idea of an “inimitié fondatrice” between Cage and abstract expressionism.
Face à la baisse des effectifs GI et des: In the face of declining IM and income numbers, Dreier explores alternative plans (school of art with limited offers), inciting resentment and distrust. When his resignation is requested, Dreier, Albers, Schlesinger and Guermonprez resign at the end of the spring. Consequences: Dreier is the last of the founders to leave; Natasha Goldowski and his colleagues are recruiting former students.
Faute de temps pour recruter, Goldowski: Due to lack of time to recruit, Goldowski and his colleagues call on former students: Fiore (painting), Warren “Pete” Jennerjahn (design), Hazel Larsen Archer (photography), Elizabeth Jennerjahn (dance); Richards and Levi return from sabbatical; Robert Turner, a fresh graduate of Alfred University, launches ceramics. Consequences: Generational renewal of the faculty.
À la démission de Josef Albers en 1949,: Upon the resignation of Josef Albers in 1949, the electrifying presence of Fuller was worth proposing the vacant rectory; He refuses it. Consequences: He returned in the summer of 1949 with a new dome
Été 1949 : Fuller revient avec un dôme p: Summer 1949: Fuller comes back with a newly manufactured, smaller-sized prototype dome made of flexible metal tubes; The dome is mounted successfully and plastic insulating skin is tested. Photographed by Hazel Larsen Archer. Flexible metal tubes; plastic skin Consequences: Experimental validation of tensegrity (“synergetic”)
Josef Albers résistait à un cours de cér: Josef Albers resisted a ceramic class, judging clay too rebellious for students; A workshop was finally built under the auspices of Robert Turner, a young graduate of Alfred University. Studio of 28 by 40 feet (about 8.5 × 12 m) in a flat field, beautiful light, good ovens and equipment. Consequences: Beginning of the teaching of ceramics until closing.
L'achèvement du barrage Solís inonde le: The completion of the Solís dam flooded the site of Chupícuaro; We thought we'd find nothing there, but tradition turns out to be more widespread and discoveries continue. nearly 400 graves with offerings were searched there; dogs sometimes buried separately with offerings Consequences: Dispersion of Chupícuaro objects in the collections
Fin de l'été 1949, Dawson remet à Olson: In late summer 1949, Dawson gave Olson a long, very bad poem on an existential lawn mower crossing the universe. Olson, embarrassed, knows nothing but do it and gives it back to the anxious student who jumps there. Dawson is 19 years old, so anxious that it does not hold in place Consequences: M.C. intervenes
Elle dit à Olson que c'est un poème que: She tells Olson that this is a poem that Fielding wrote for him and asks him if he could not keep it and read it; Olson whispers he will. The poem probably returned quickly to Dawson who threw him into his humiliation. La voice of M.C. takes a hardness; Olson whisper “Yes, of course” Consequences: For Dawson, M.C. was “un pote” that night
Olson parle de Paterson et des Cantos ;: Olson talks about Paterson and Cantos; Dawson, who had never heard of Williams or Pound, laughs aloud: “Bill Bill” and “Ezra Ounces”. Smile scattered around the table, irritated Olson. M.C. asks Olson to see this from the student's perspective: their names are fun.
Dawson décrit Arnold, peintre cubain, me: Dawson describes Arnold, Cuban painter, wonderful, very cultivated (paintings, writers, politics), which reminds him of his brother-in-law Bill by the physics and the way to smooth his hair back; He didn't see his work, but he's sure of his talent. hair smoothed back, same nose as Billy/Bill
Dès le premier jour de Dawson, Hank lui: On the first day of Dawson, Hank exposed his communist ideas to him and did not change his iota; He has read one or two Wolfe books but talks about it as an intimate and dares to tell Olson that he loves Wolfe “par endroits”. Hank believes that believers in the Christian God are crazy or tweezers; Many students share this contempt.
Olson annonce trois pièces de quinze min: Olson announces three pieces of fifteen minutes each: their version of the episode of cyclope and Ulysses in Homer's Odyssey; a selection of Ezra Pound; a free creation. three 15 minute pieces
Dawson suit peinture, sculpture, philoso: Dawson follows painting, sculpture, Hindu and French philosophy (“au-dessus de ma tête mais merveilleux”), works an oil painting, has sketched teachers and students and sends his mother a portrait of Buckminster Fuller. oil, sketch, portrait of Fuller
Lors d'une discussion intitulée « A Desp: In a discussion called “A Desperate View...”, Kooning talks about the “vide” on which God acts in Genesis: one can float, steal, be suspended and, today, tremble there; The idea of integration is a desperate one. He uses the word “tremble”, which has been recurring in his vocabulary since the 1940s.
Septembre-octobre : exposé avec Elaine d: September-October: exposed with Elaine in “Artists: Man and Wife” at Janis; founding member of The Club, artist collective of 8th Street East.
Pour une exposition au Cincinnati Art Mu: For an exhibition at the Cincinnati Art Museum, Albers writes: “Sans comparaison et choix, il n'y a pas de valeur. Et pourquoi craindre que penser et planifier gâtent la peinture d'un tableau ?”
Culmination du « total thinking » de Ful: Fuller “total thinking” culture by successfully erecting a geodetic dome on campus. Consequences: Touchstone of holistic planning for post-war habitat, transportation and communications
Albers affirme que le progrès ne dépend: Albers states that progress does not depend solely on accidents: without order or control, one drowns or stifles in chaos and decomposition.
La poétesse M. C. Richards monte des œuv: La poetess M. C. Richards created works by Jean Cocteau, including Knights of the Round Table in 1949.
Masato Nakagawa photographie Buckminster: Masato Nakagawa photography Buckminster Fuller with a model in the summer of 1949. photograph kept at the State Archives of North Carolina
De retour au campus en 1949, Fuller érig: De returned to campus in 1949, Fuller successfully erected a self-supporting geodetic structure; it argues the assembly of the dome as essentially utopian project of “design science complet et anticipatoire” Masato Nakagawa photography showing Fuller with the model, summer 1949 (State Archives of North Carolina) Consequences: The dome becomes the emblem of its design revolution
Fuller écrit au magnat des médias que la: Fuller writes to the media magnate that the “reinspiration de l'individu” requires artists to become the “patrons capitalistes” of the original company.
L'été suivant, Snelson montre à Fuller u: The following summer, Snelson showed Fuller a column of about one foot high made of wood and plastic: two cross of equal wood perpendicularly oriented, the upper shape suspended in the air by tensioned nylon threads, the lower one serving as a shelf — a principle of “compression flottante” (discontinuous compression, continuous tension). Two crosses of wood of equal size; nylon yarn; outer wires now the exact right angle; 111⁄2 × 53⁄8 × 53⁄8 inches according to legend. Consequences: Fuller sees it as a new and effective engineering principle.
Fuller demande à Snelson une version mod: Fuller asks Snelson for a modified version of X-Piece and later names the “tensegrity” principle for tensional integrity; He says he will transform the building industry (very high towers without foothills or deep foundations). Each then patents its version of the principle. “tensional integrity” contract. Consequences: Patents separated from Fuller and Snelson; Implicit paternity dispute.
La peau plastique transparente, double,: La transparent, double, thermosealed and pneumatic plastic skin of a dome with a structure of thirty-one large circles (tube beads and continuous internal cable), designed and built at the Chicago Institute of Design in 1948-49, was tested at Black Mountain during the summer of 1949. 31 large circles; tubular beads; continuous internal cable; Double skin heat sealed.
Fuller revient au collège en 1949 comme: Fuller returned to college in 1949 as director of the summer institute, accompanied by a dozen students from the Chicago Institute of Design, bringing a new prototype dome influenced by X-Piece Snelson. about a dozen ID students; flexible aluminium tube dome with internal wiring, more modest than the venetian blind model Consequences: Continuation of Fuller “exploratory work” with enthusiastic students like Snelson and Ruth Asawa.
Le second dôme, préparé des mois plus tô: The second dome, prepared months earlier for a demonstration at the Pentagon at Washington, is successfully erected at BMC and a new transparent insulating plastic skin, heat-welded double and pneumatic, is tested. flexible aluminium tube structure with internal wiring; Double plastic skin, heat-welded, pneumatic, transparent, insulating Consequences: Experimental validation of tensectory theory and “synergetic” process.
Fuller soumet à ses étudiants un problèm: Fuller submits to its students a problem of apocalypse as a matter of duty: the city is evacuated, all residential and industrial concentrations of 50,000 or more people are in immediate danger of annihilation, consumer goods will be diverted to small decentralized communities, everything that is not decentralized will be destroyed. Consignee: “The city is to be evacuated… Everything not decentralized will be destroyed.”; threshold of 50,000 people. Consequences: For Fuller, suburban dispersion was the optimal response to the nuclear threat.
Hazel Larsen Archer photographie Buckmin: Hazel Larsen Archer photography Buckminster Fuller with its dome at Black Mountain College in the summer of 1949 (fig. 3.17). Photograph preserved by the Estate of Hazel Larsen Archer and the Black Mountain College Museum + Arts Center.
Lors de l'été 1949, Fuller fait venir sa: In the summer of 1949, Fuller brought his secretary from the Institute of Design to transcribe his essay “Total Thinking” (edited 1949).
Les Albers déménagent à New York ; Anni: Albers move to New York; Anni became the first weaver to have a personal exhibition at MoMA. She creates several blinds with open slats, light visually and really, texture contrasts and playful invention. The exhibition, well received, coincides with a newspaper strike and lacks full public recognition. It includes wall tapestries and fabric samples. open slat blinds; press strike
Quitte Black Mountain pour New York ; pr: Black Mountain exit for New York; first weaver to have a personal exhibition at the Museum of Modern Art First personal exhibition of a weaver at MoMA
Face à un énorme déficit, le recteur Alb: Faced with a huge deficit, Rector Albers and Treasurer Dreier proposed the unimaginable: a board of directors. La rumor of an affair of the still married Ted Dreier with a teacher fueled discord. At the end of 1948-1949, the faculty demanded Ted Dreier's resignation and saw the resignations of Albers and others. Ray Trayer and Natasha Goldowski, acting president and secretary, proposed to consider the return of John Andrew Rice, which had held the community longer than anyone since. Frank Aydelotte wrote to his sister that nothing would be more disastrous. Rice never pursued the track seriously. Letter from Aydelotte of June 16, 1949 Consequences: Rice will say of the suggestion: “For a moment the clouds seemed to open.”
Un an après le suicide de Gorky, il reje: One year after Gorky's suicide, he firmly rejects the idea that Gorky would have suffered his influence: he is happy not to escape Gorky's powerful influence. final formula : "Sweet Arshile, bless your dear heart"
Un an après le suicide de Gorky, de Koon: One year after Gorky's suicide, Kooning rejects in an open letter to ARTnews the idea that Gorky would have suffered his influence; He takes over Gorky's.
Lors d'une table ronde sur la significat: At a round table on the meaning and titration of works, Kooning argues that if an artist can still title his paintings, it is not always very clear.
Deux mille personnes assistent aux événe: Two thousand people attend events celebrating the 200th anniversary of Goethe, a pantheist admired at the Bauhaus and long resident of Weimar; Four years after the war, the celebrants claim that nationality counts less than the contribution to human progress 2000 participants Consequences: birth of the annual summer conference of the Aspen Institute
Après sa rétrospective personnelle au Mo: After his personal retrospective at MoMA (first of the genre for a textile designer), Anni hopes that the museum will buy tapestry at low prices; The museum is declining. The Busch-Reisinger acquired it shortly afterwards thanks to a bold conservative. The tapestry had survived the war only because Anni had given it to his parents, who had placed it on their grand piano as a piano blanket, with a vase of flowers on it; the ring left by the water is still visible and passes for a calculated compositional element Consequences: work become classical perpetually demanded but that Harvard rarely lets travel (fragility, institutional whim)
Pendant son exposition au MoMA en 1949,: During his exhibition at MoMA in 1949, Anni taught the principles of weaving; It asks students to imagine themselves on the coast of Peru centuries ago, without any machine, and to think about how to weave. primitive craft: parallel twigs spaced regularly, connected by perpendicular strips in leaf strips; Possible materials: animal skins, bird feathers, shredded tree bark, wildflower petals, algae Consequences: The student who most impressed her built a miniature craft with matches from an ordinary notebook.
Lors de son exposition à Paris l'année p: During his exhibition in Paris the year before the article (1950), Hofmann bought recent Dubuffet, hung in his home among primitive French and his own paintings. Paintings hung in his home in Provincetown and his New York studio.
Kline rend visite à un ami qui agrandit: Kline visits a friend who expands his own sketches at the Bell-Opticon; the friend asks him if he has any small drawings in his pocket — Franz still has some. They see “bodilessly” magnified sketches against the wall: a 4 by 5" rocking chair drawing becomes gigantic black brush strokes where the image is erased by the features themselves. 4×5 inches sketch (about 10×13 cm); he continues the drawings one after the other in the projector Consequences: total and instantaneous conversion of his style: large canvases, painter's brushes to building, hardware enamels
Le jour du retour de Dreier au campus, N: On the day Dreier returned to campus, Nell Rice, the group's spokesperson (a narrow majority of the faculty), asked him to cut off all ties with the college: it must live, but not with it in an administrative or political role. Dreier, astonished, requests that the application be put in writing. Consequences: The beginning of the final crisis.
Une majorité d'étudiants signe une pétit: A majority of students sign a petition asking Dreier to bow to the majority of the faculty — among them students of Albers itself. Against all odds, Dreier proposes to assign its responsibilities to N. O. Pittenger, who had just arrived to discuss the position of administrator. Consequences: Dreier agrees to leave.
Pittenger, mécontent de la gestion antér: Pittenger, dissatisfied with the previous management of the annuities, refuses to commit until the issue is clarified; accusations of misappropriation arise because Dreier had put the bonds in the name of Albers alone and Albers had just requested that Dreier be included in the fund. Professor Cole, a long-time auditor, comes to the college and reassures everyone about the legality of the device; For lack of immediate money, Dreier only protects 80% of the funds, the college promising the remaining 20% later. $300 per year in government bonds since 1944 for Albers, Jalowetz and Straus (fifty years and five years of teaching); 80/20%. Consequences: Pittenger accepts an advisory role; resignations become final.
Au nom d'un groupe de collègues, la secr: On behalf of a group of colleagues, Secretary Mangold writes a long typed letter: Dreier mentioned taking over the rectorate; objections: confusion over the management of the college, inability to conduct a meeting, autocracy, exclusion of others from its deliberations, demoralizing economic pessimism. Manuscript note added: “I think he is largely unconscious of these things. That he is psychically unbalanced.” She pleads for Albers to deter Dreier to avoid open, explosive and unnecessary controversy. Typed letter with handwritten note; “he is psychically unbalanced” Consequences: Albers is not being persuaded
Moins d'une semaine après la lettre de M: Less than a week after Mangold's letter, during a meeting at New York with potential Black Mountain trustees, Albers announces that Dreier has decided not to leave college. Consequences: Two weeks of uncertainty
En post-scriptum manuscrit, Albers deman: In post-scriptum manuscript, Albers insists that Dreier be released as soon as possible from the burden of treasurer in the current entourage where his friends are of little help; He proposes that Pittenger suggest someone else if he cannot come himself, while at the same time ensuring their trust. Handwritten note, “a PS.... close to my heart”
Pittenger qualifie ses quatre jours d'«: Pittenger describes its four days as “expérience des plus intéressantes”: Albers “exceptionnellement bon professeur d'art” is “aussi impossible comme exécutant qu'il est grand comme artiste”; Dreier has done a good job with the students and the builder but does not remember his promises from one day to the next and has lost everyone's confidence — largely, according to Pittenger, because of her relationship with an art school teacher: the students do not blame the mistress as much as the fact that she is on the payroll. “teacher in the Art School”; employee mistress; Judgment on Albers Consequences: Reveals college tolerance to open relationships
Tolk-Watkins envoie à Asawa une brochure: Tolk-Watkins sends Asawa an advertising brochure to buy a home in Sausalito, registered to show the location of the Tin Angel and their cottage, with a sarcastic “ha !” next to the word “homes”. Letter dated 28 January 1949; Sausalito Billing: “city of homes [and] gateway to the redwood empire” Consequences: Confront Asawa to Postwar Domesticity Expectations
Dans une lettre à Peggy Tolk-Watkins, As: In a letter to Peggy Tolk-Watkins, Asawa says it's getting to understand Trude Guermonprez and his multiple desires.
Après la conférence et ses dénonciations: After the conference and its inflamed denunciations, beautiful women circulate baskets to collect dollar bills; the money buys alcohol in paper cups, then dances on polkas for hours Words: Elaine: “un demi-pouce dans un gobelet en papier … très, très festif” Atmosphere: smoke, coffee, voice, polkas Issue: the community of artists finances itself
Bill et un artiste inconnu, ivres de xér: Bill and an unknown artist, drunk of sherry, descend to the beach despite hurricane warnings; man faints; Sanders and Bill wear it to the water and undress for lack of jerseys; a state police officer arrests them; cell down, five-dollar fine. Atmosphere: hurricane wind, burlesque drama Issue: Elaine's concern for Bill; The grotesque way of life.
À la fin de l'été, gueule de bois généra: At the end of the summer, general hangover and ill-treatment; the roommate ends up asking Elaine how she keeps her calm; dry response. Words: “Jamais.” She wouldn't allow it. Issue: The vital bet of Elaine against melancholy.
Dîner entre artistes ; Grillo sert un pl: Dinner between artists; Grillo serves a meat-tasting dish that he later admitted to be local whiting; Freilicher brings Basie discs and tomatoes from the garden; Elaine monopolizes conversation with verve. Words: Elaine speaks “de tout, du dessin à la peine de mort” (Rivers). Atmosphere: “heureusement assiégée” community
Gropius propose un mural ; Albers d'abor: Gropius offers a wall; Albers first little interested, decides to make “un mural de vérité”: choose the Flemish apparatus, refuse colors and reliefs, keep gray, dig calibrated voids (brick lengths, half, quarters) to deal with shadows, aim for lightness and a growth effect; he calls the Americana wall. Words: “un mural de verdad, en el que se respetara y preservara el murus” — a true wall respecting the Atmosphere wall: Light diffuses distant windows on the grey brick Issue: Affirming a North American conception of the wall against the Mexican school
Schauffler propose à Rondthaler deux qua: Schauffler offers Rondthaler two quarters of beer if it does not move to Oregon; Rondthaler takes on the challenge, part, finds a job at the Forest Service, between Reed College and spends a lifetime there. Words: “In 1949 Manvel Schauffler bet me two quarts of beer I would not move to Oregon” — “En 1949, Schauffler m'a parié deux quarts de bière que je n'irais pas en Oregon” Atmosphere: complicity of former students, postwar carelessness Issue: a bet of friend decides a lifetime
Fuller copote un étudiant dont la voix l: Fuller copots a student whose voice impresses him to read one of his 200-page poems; guests sleep after the first hours; Fuller, joyful, demands that reading go to the end Atmosphere: Interminable evening, vaguely comic solemnity, radiant obstinacy of Fuller Issue: The egocentric genius faced with an exhausted community
Croyant à une offre ferme, Wolpert a dém: Believed in a firm offer, Wolpert resigned from his position; Natasha's letter cancels everything; it responds with a diatribe (“collège frauduleux”, “double combine dégoûtante”); Natasha talks about misunderstanding; A few days later, he died of polio Words: “I want to hear nothing further from your fraudulent college… you have sunk to your true level” Atmosphere: Rage, betrayal, tragic irony of death Issue: The power relations of a college on the brink of the abyss even crush his children
Deux semaines après le lancement, premiè: Two weeks after launch, first critical session; the reviews go from team to team; Albers speaks with students from 13:30 to 17:30 with Switzerland; almost all offer monumental decoration without thinking about plastic; In the evening, Albers wrote his exasperation to Anni, noting Kahn's absence. Words: Albers to Anni: “Quite soon struggle as almost all propose a tremendous 'setting' for plastics. But without thinking of plastics. And Kahn the coordinator, though here, did not show up. We are wondering.” Atmosphere: Long afternoon, student confusion, Albers disappointment contained. Issue: Silent confrontation between the two pedagogies: the hand against the concept; the absent person who was to lead.
Fin septembre ou début octobre, avant le: Late September or early October, before departure for Cincinnati, Kahn visits Albers to discuss the plastic problem; Albers shows him for the first time his geometric drawings on the line — future Structural Constellations; Undocumented conversation. Atmosphere: Two men discovering each other; the authors invite to imagine the exchange. Issue: Crossing of two major trajectories of modernism around impossible spatial structures.
Après leur été à Asheville, les Woelffer: After their summer at Asheville, Woelffer passes through New York; Pollock, sharing their passions, the press to stay there and look for a permanent gallery. Words: Pollock begs them to stay (paraphrased). Issue: Choice between New York career and traveling life.
L'architecte Williams conçoit le bâtimen: The architect Williams designs the building in consultation with Turner, which partly finances a loan to the college, has built workshop and oven, without engaging in the internal struggles of the college in full transition after the resignation of Albers. Words: Turner: It was not a time of discovery but of consolidation of what he had learned to Alfred Atmosphere: working loneliness, out in a field Issue: A traditional craftsman left in America's most experimental college
Eleanor pose dos tourné dans le ballroom: Eleanor poses back turned in the ballroom to walls painted by Weber; Open flash of room 8x10; Four variations retained at the draw: the chignon unwinds, the arms fold out of field, fall, spread over the radiator. Words: Callahan: Eleanor didn't know what Weber was talking about with her painting, otherwise she wouldn't have let it. Atmosphere : Relaxed, spontaneous, day and night. Issue: Intimacy of the couple as an artistic laboratory.
Asawa en robe noire cousue par Johanna J: Asawa in black dress sewn by Johanna Jalowetz in a fabric of Anni Albers; Schlesinger on piano; Asawa shoots at his wishes, everyone laughs, the baby Ragland crawls on the ground; then a sober reception of cold charcuterie and champagne in front of the ocean/baie double view Words: Lanier later: “Ils riaient tous et nous pleurions et nous riions et nous nous en sommes sortis” Atmosphere: Warm, messy, burlesque and moved Issue: Union of two Black Mountain elders around college friends, alliance of Fuller dymaxion as symbol
La faculté, à une voix de majorité court: La faculty, with a short majority vote, imposes the departure of the interim treasurer Theodore Dreier, co-founder, with the consent of a significant part of the students; Josef and Anni Albers and several other teachers resigned in solidarity. Atmosphere: Governance crisis within a community supposed to live by consensus Issue: Out of 16 years of college life; end of the Albers era
Dans la dépendance bâtie à la mémoire de: In the Mark Dreier memory dependency, Rauschenberg photographes a chair under a diagonal light shaving a white plaster wall — purity and precision that Albers could not pull away from it elsewhere. Atmosphere: Silence, immobility, dust, aural superimposed on visual Issue: La photography as a premonition of White Paintings and 4'33"
Lors du Mardi Gras de 1949, Ingeborg Lau: On the 1949 Mardi Gras, Ingeborg Lauterstein wore a unicorn costume designed by Rauschenberg; Trude Guermonp the photograph. La photo is stored in the Black Mountain College Papers of the North Carolina State Archives. Atmosphere: Festival, extravagant costume Issue: The festive and creative spirit of the college, collaboration between artists
Weil et Rauschenberg livrent un groupe d: Weil and Rauschenberg deliver a group of Albers paintings; Egan lights the gallery and reveals an exhibition by Franz Kline Words: Weil: “I felt like I had been socked in the stomach” — I felt struck in the stomach; what they had learned in art school seemed suddenly invalid Atmosphere: Shock and exaltation Issue: Switching from Albers pedagogy towards freedom of abstract expressionism
L'étudiant frémissant tend son long poèm: The shivering student extends his long very bad poem on an existential lawn mower; Olson, visibly outdated, returns it to him; M.C., the hardened voice, demands that he keep it and read it; Olson whispers his accord Words: M.C.: “It's a poem… Fielding wrote it for you… Don't you think you might keep it, and read it?”; Olson : “Yes, of course” Atmosphere : Anxiety of the 19-year-old, embarrassment of the master Issue : A humbled young poet saved by an ally
Dawson s'assied près d'Olson après le dé: Dawson sits near Olson after leaving the others; Olson talks to a student, face 15 centimetres from hers; he breaks a hot dog in half, dips half in the mustard, rips a bread in quarters, then crumbs, grabs a tomato through the table, bites it, picks up chips full of fingers, all talking about Howard Fast, Saroyan, Pound, Eliot, Wolfe, cigarette in the beak and milk glass in the hand; At the end, only a few lettuce leaves remain. Words : He talks about Howard Fast, Saroyan, Ezra Pound, T.S. Eliot, Thomas Wolfe Atmosphere : fascination of the young Dawson in front of this giant Titan esque Issue : introduction of the narrator to the character-Olson
Questionnaire en règle : Wolfe ? « No go: Questionnaire in good standing: Wolfe? “No good, bad on public morals.” Saroyan? “No good.” Scholem Asch? “No good.” In front of Dawson's deconfite mine, Olson puts his elbow on his shoulder, sucks a huge puff, blinks from the eye and throws the sentence, then moves away from a huge laugh. Words: “Every dog has his own fleas” (each dog's fleas) Atmosphere: comic, affectionate, overwhelming Issue: literary taste as a lesson in authority
Après le test de prototype de l'été 1948: After the summer 1948 prototype test, Fuller returned in 1949 and succeeded in erecting a self-supporting geodetic structure; Nakagawa photography Fuller with the Atmosphere model: Belief euphoria of the proselyte of geodesy Issue: La redemption of the inventor of Dymaxion chess by tangible success
L'étudiant présente une colonne d'enviro: The student presents a column of about one foot: two cross of perpendicular wood, the upper suspended in the air by tensioned nylon threads, rigid balance maintained by external wires; Fuller immediately reads a new engineering principle and requests a modified version. Atmosphere: Declic decisive — a student inspires the master. Issue: Paternity of a discovery (tensegrity) that will also be played in front of patent offices.
Étudiants d'ID débarqués de Chicago avec: ID students landed from Chicago with Fuller, the dome is mounted in aluminum tubes prepared for the Pentagon; the lattice rising becomes stronger than its parts; The transparent, thermo-welded plastic skin is then tested. Atmosphere: Triumph of a “synergetic” process after the previous year's failure. Issue: Validation of the Tensegrity and All “pensée totale” of Fuller.
Fuller distribue à ses étudiants un prob: Fuller distributes to its students a problem of apocalypse: the city is evacuated, all concentrations of 50,000 or more people are in immediate danger of annihilation, consumer goods are diverted to decentralized communities, everything that is not decentralized will be destroyed. Words: “The city is to be evacuated… Everything not decentralized will be destroyed.” (“La ville est à évacuer… Tout ce qui n'est pas décentralisé sera détruit.”) Atmosphere: Eschatological emergency; nuclear fear turned into a design exercise. Issue: La from nuclear terror to technocratic planning.
Après la demande de démission de Dreier: After Dreier's request for resignation and Albers's resignation from protest, Trayer and Goldowski, acting, propose to return Rice — the one who held the community longer than anyone else; Aydelotte opposed it; Rice is not pursuing. Words: Aydelotte: “Nothing would be more disastrous for the college.”; Rice : “For a moment the clouds seemed to open.” Atmosphere : Cracked community, fleeting hope. Issue: The founder's failed return.
Las des cafétérias, un groupe de peintre: Las des cafeterias, a group of painters decides one evening to rent a loft; 20 founding members each pay ten dollars; unable to find a name, they simply call it “the Club”; We drink coffee, some drinks, talk at night. Words: De Kooning: Greeks and Italians have their social clubs along Eight Avenue; “nous ne voulions rien avoir à faire avec l'art”. Atmosphere: Conviviality of emigrants, rejection of institutional seriousness. Issue: Underground institutionalization of the New York avant-garde.
Kline passe voir un ami qui agrandit ses: Kline visits a friend who enlarges his own sketches in a Bell-Opticon; the friend asks him if he has any small drawings on him — Franz pulls out a handle; projection on the wall; the 4×5 inches rocking chair becomes gigantic black blows that erases the image; It enchains the drawings, the image always swallowed by the traits that delimit it. Words: Friend: “As-tu de ces petits dessins dans ta poche ?” Atmosphere: astonishment shared by both men in the face of scale change Issue: instant conversion that founded all the later art of Kline
Le jour même du retour de Dreier, Nell R: On the very day of Dreier's return, Nell Rice, spokesperson for the five dissidents (acute majority), explains to him that the college must continue but not with him in any administrative or decision-making function; Dreier, astonished, asks that this be written. Words: Rice: College cannot succeed as long as Dreier serves in administrative capacity; Dreier: Let us put the request in writing. Atmosphere: Shock, frontal, tense Issue: Referral of the co-founder by his own faculty
Après l'acceptation de Pittenger pour la: After the acceptance of Pittenger for the transition, the Albers, Schlesinger and Guermonprez release their resignations, joined by Dreier; Albers announces to his colleagues that he continues his courses until the end of the semester but ceases to belong to the college. Words: “I will continue my classes, but do not consider me tomorrow a member of this place.” Atmosphere: Bitter but dignified routture, after crisis on crisis. Issue: La end of 16 years of total involvement of Albers in the community.
Intimidée à l'idée d'écrire sur celui qu: Intimidated at the idea of writing about the one who was her teacher months earlier, she filled a third of the article of quotes of Albers, then elegantly refuted her formula “My work is study, not revelation” by declaring that the revelation dwells in “the austere expressions of his spaces and colors”; the same number contains 19 of his criticisms 19 in a number; it will affirm a record 38 reviews per month Consequences: first text of Elaine on Albers
Elaine publie dans ARTnews des comptes r: Elaine publishes in ARTnews reports of the Albers exhibition presented in two galleries, then article “Albers Paints a Picture”. Consequences: Transforms the admiration born of Black Mountain into critical writing.
Williams découvre Lou Harrison lors de l: Williams discovers Lou Harrison during the creation of the First Sonata of Ives, played by William Masselos on score edited and reconstructed by Harrison from an old manuscript and sketches. Riegger and Varesis very moved in the public ; Williams imagines Thomson, Copland, Cowell and Bernstein present without having seen them. Consequences: One of the greatest piano moments ever heard by Williams, felt 53 years later.
Démission en février. Voyage d'été « pou: Resignation in February. Summer trip “pour oublier un temps l'enseignement, l'administration et la vie en communauté” (letter to Grote, March 31, 1949). Josef gives four design seminars at the University of Mexico (10 June-15 August); housed avenida Veracruz 102 C, Colonia Roma. The Moellenhoff visit them and travel together three weeks; Visit to Diego Rivera's Anahuacalli Museum with Rivera and Clara Porset. Consequences: Final departure of BMC
Étudiants de l'automne 1948 trouvent une: Fall 1948 students found a decimated faculty; Frank, exhausted by hijacking meetings, finds a better position in Quogue; Ann follows him shortly afterwards. Frank and Nell return late and exhausted from endless faculty meetings. Consequences: Exchange of mountains against the ocean.
En février 1949, elle rejoint la petite: In February 1949, she joined the small choir led by Bimbus, which drew more musicality from them than they thought they had. Invited to sing a Sunday at the black YMCA of Asheville: they give fragments of a Bach cantata; The local choir responds with a rich and deep black sound, including “I Been 'Buked and I Been Scorned”, which touches their bones; then shared refreshments. Sunday; Bach cantata (which is forgotten); Spiritual “I Been 'Buked and I Been Scorned” Consequences: An outstanding experience of encounter and black music
Une pétition d'enseignants demande à Alb: A teacher petition asks Albers for a faculty meeting “en vue de demander la démission de T. Dreier”; Dreier advances by resigning; the resignations of Albers and others, dated February 18, 1949, are in the archives, but the student petition described by several witnesses is not found. Consequences: Reverse direction
Mel Mitchell Kelly affirme que les Rondt: Mel Mitchell Kelly claims that the Rondthaler and Levi, still officially members of the faculty, sent their power of attorneys against Dreier via cable; Mary Caroline Richards has absolutely no memory of it.
Les Albers démissionnent début février 1: The Albers resigned in early February 1949; the rupture, prepared since at least 1947 perhaps 1945, is attributed to their solidarity with Ted Dreier, while all the pathologies of the college had crystallized around him. Consequences: End of Albers presence after almost 16 years
Des enseignants dissidents pétitionnent: Dissident teachers petition for a meeting to request the resignation of Dreier; the latter advance by resigning; Albers and others also resigned on February 18, 1949. Atmosphere: a tense coup de force, then memorized in an adversarial way Issue: the taking of power and selective blindness of memory
Pendant des jours, Bill parle, Elaine no: For days Bill talks, Elaine notes his ideas, they iron the text again and again, she makes suggestions; At the end, Bill states something “totalement juste” without room for argument. Words: Elaine: “Bill never liked to write. He talked and I took down his ideas for him.” Atmosphere: Literary workshop with two, creative complicity of the couple. Issue: Bill's La glory is built in the shadow of Elaine, not recognized as its equal.
Elle notifie à Albers qu'elle quitte ART: She informs Albers that she leaves ARTnews to travel to Tangier with her sister Marjorie: “l'idée de ne rien faire que peindre au bord de la Méditerranée” seduces her; the project remains a fleeting fantasy, but it ceases the short criticisms, fearing of losing the “rough edges” necessary to the artist, because “un critique doit regarder tout avec équité” letter to Albers, March 1949 Consequences: it passes to the background items paid up to $75 coin
Correspondance Pittenger-Trayer (25 et 3: Pittenger-Trayer correspondence (25 and 30 March 1949) documents the sale of gravel and the Forbes case; Fuller left an “remarque sur la plomberie” in a three-page note dated 1 June 1949; Dreier-Pittenger letters of September 1949. Note of 3 pages of Fuller; site gravel Consequences : Financial Fragility of 1949
Après son travail photographique remarqu: After his photographic work noticed in the summer of 1948, the Board of Fellows invited him to become a photography reader for the coming year. Consequences: First position of official photography education
Elaine écrit à Albers : elle évoque son: Elaine writes to Albers: she evokes her imminent departure from Black Mountain (announced in March 1949), reports of her double exhibition in February, and thanks him for a birthday present (March 12). Atmosphere: Disturbance and gratitude at a distance, between college and New York. Issue: The Elaine-Albers link survives at the start of the master and at the end of summer 1948.
Invitée pour un camping de cinq jours le: Invited to a five-day campsite along the ridges, cut short by one day because of frozen toes (it only wears sneakers); rain the first three days, snow the fourth, fog almost continuously, no view; bag of sixty-five pounds, painful muscles but dazzled mind by virgin trees, spongy moss, streams; Last night under a rock overhanging, waking up under the snow, violets frozen like perfect glass; One night, the moon pierces the clouds and they sing while walking “Sleepers Awake” and other Bach choirs. 65 pounds (~29 kg) of bag; sneakers; rain 3 days, snow 4th ; violets frozen in glass ; Back to high school in the sun with snow still on the packs Consequences: She learns survival and that physical pain can be separated from joy, wonder and friendship
Les quatre démissionnaires restent jusqu: The four resignations remain until June to honour their teaching commitments; Dreier, without class, leaves Black Mountain permanently in mid-April, going to Florida with his wife then camping west. Consequences: End of the Albers-Dreier era.
Ayant accepté un rôle consultatif auprès: Having accepted an advisory role with Pittenger, Dreier, without current courses, leaves the college permanently in mid-April; the Albers, Trude Guermonprez and Charlotte Schlesinger stay until June to finish their teachings Travel to Florida then camping in the West — first real rest in 25 years Consequences: End of the presence of the founding group of 1933 (except Nell Rice)
Article non signé (en réalité écrit par: Unsigned article (actually written by Lanier) about Black Mountain College's Student Minimum House project, illustrated with Hazel Archer photographs; John Entenza had contacted Lanier and Asawa for this publication on the recommendation of Anni and Josef Albers. Arts and Architecture, April 1949, p. 30-31 Consequences: National Dissemination of the College's Work in Architecture
Lanier offre un vase à sa cousine Laurie: Lanier offers a vase to her cousin Laurie Pearson, who replies at the end of April that she will never dare to put flowers in it. Letter from Laurie Pearson of 30 April 1949: “my pond-farm-piece is wonderful. I fear I'll never put flowers in it—it is too beautiful without them”
Breton prononce une diatribe anti-améric: Breton pronounced an anti-American diatribe (racism against blacks and Indians, sexual hypocrisy, Coca-Cola, control over Latin America) at a meeting against the dictatorship and war of the Revolutionary Democratic Rally. RDR, anticapitalist and anti-Stalinist movement. Consequences: Index of French anxiety against the post-war American power.
Une nuit du camping, la lune perce les n: One night from the campsite, the moon pierces the clouds; Walking on the forest road, they sing “Sleepers Awake” and other Bach Atmosphere choirs: magic, detached from physical pain
Insatisfaite de sa critique après un jou: Dissatisfied with her criticism after a whole day in the Nakian workshop, she stayed at the office after everyone left, towards the 5 p.m. deadline; Hess arrives at nine o'clock in the morning when she leaves and asks suspiciously: “You haven't been here all night, have you?”; It laughs weakly and runs away without answering 17h; Full night at the office Consequences: illustration of his ruthless self-requirement
Après la dissolution de Subjects of the: After the dissolution of Subjects of the Artist in May 1949, Tony Smith and a few artists took over the loft lease at 35 East Eight Street and continued the Friday evening lecture cycle, known as Studio 35 from the address. (Note the inconsistency of the source: it dates from Bill's February 1949 conference, prior to this dissolution.) loft at 35 East Eight Street; Friday evening conferences Consequences: Continuity of the avant-garde's place of speech.
Deadline de 17 h approchant, elle dépose: Deadline at 5 p.m. approaching, she deposits her other critics, announces some retouches to the article Nakian, starts there ; suddenly realize that everyone is gone; works all night; At nine o'clock in the morning, cross Hess entering Words: Hess, suspicious: “Vous n'avez pas passé la nuit ici, quand même ?”; she laughs weakly “à cette suggestion grotesque” and flees without answering Atmosphere: night solitude of the office, dawn, comedy Issue: self-requirement until exhaustion
Six mois après la brochure, Asawa s'inst: Six months after the brochure, Asawa moved to San Francisco and tangentially crossed the bohemian circles. Consequences: Beginning of Californian Life
Après avoir accepté d'être conseiller gé: After accepting to be a general adviser, Pittenger became rector in July 1949, the faculty granting him “toutes les prérogatives administratives” to act without hindrance, while the search for a permanent holder continued
Premier voyage en wagon-lit (Pullman), v: First trip in a sleeping car (Pullman), car almost empty, well padded, air slowed, lukewarm; In a kind of mist a voice said to him, 'You go to a place and you will change'; He panics but desires it; Later reading 'What does not change is the will to change', he knows that he found his man (Olson). Wagon Pullman almost empty, serene, warm
Premier article de la série « X Paints a: First article in the “X Paints a Picture” series: Dickinson, 57, “étonnamment méconnu et sous-apprécié”; It compares in detail three states of The Ruin; a year earlier she had painted The Music Party showing him on violin with Daniel Brustlein in cello series documented by photographer Rudy Burckhardt; Dickinson, 57 years old Consequences: launch of the series that will make his reputation
Le cours de composition pré-architectura: The course of pre-architectural composition takes the name of Composición Pura: intuitive and abstract character of the composition of the three-dimensional space from material, form and color, as a prior habit to architectural realization. Sequence: plans, model, criticism, lifting of the model from the plans, group criticism. Difference with Albers course: exercises in predetermined spaces. Publication in Arquitectura y Construcción n° 16, September 1949
Wyeth voit Ben Loper devant sa cabane en: Wyeth sees Ben Loper in front of his cabin driving home, returns two days later, discovers the scene: Loper sitting alone in the dark room, a triangle of yellow light around an eye. Five months of work, including eleven weeks of execution. a month before Loper, a greenhouse worker, agreed to pose on the weekend; Gesso panel of about 27 x 17 inches Consequences: title found during a pose session
Deux jours après leur rencontre sur la r: Two days after their meeting on the road, Wyeth knocks at the door of the cabin; invited to enter, he opens on Loper sitting alone in the darkness, leaning forward, a triangle of light around an eye; Loper gets up and vision dissipates — Wyeth will never see that light spot again. Atmosphere: afternoon heat, golden dust, dark room, desolation Issue: the instant birth of a painting that will require five months of memory reconstruction
Six anciens étudiants (dont Steinau et H: Six former students (including Steinau and Howard), plus Pittenger and Corkran, meet two days at Forbes to propose a reorganization: an Board of Overseass sharing the power to choose a rector (and only authorized to revoke it), wage manager, tenure, budget, hiring with the rector, and interested in funding; property and educational policy would remain at the faculty. group of six former students + Pittenger + Corkran, two days of meeting Consequences: One-year start of community debates
Forbes propose de financer la constructi: Forbes proposes to finance the construction of a new science building up to $6,000 and stops at the college during its holidays to help resolve the debates; he supported the idea of Levi adding five or six non-residents to the current Board and agreed to sit there. $6,000; five to six non-residents; Possible meetings once or twice a year Consequences: Demonstrates that an interest without official authority is possible
En voyage de vacances, Forbes s'arrête a: On a holiday trip, Forbes stops at the college, offers to finance the science building, says he is in favour of the plan of Levi, proposes to look for a rector in parallel of the faculty Words: it says “enclin à favoriser” the idea of Levi Atmosphere: calm, conciliator Issue: demonstrate that one can serve without dominating
Dans l'exposition de Steichen, deux œuvr: In Steichen's exhibition, two works of Archer hung near each other: on the left Asawa profile in front of the doors of the Quiet House, on the right a smaller close-up of a door handle whose screws form a face Atmosphere: The intimate world of the North Caroline transported into the New York rooms Issue: The “amateur” Hazel-Frieda Larsen displayed alongside Lange and Levitt
Pendant une séance de croquis, un garçon: During a sketch session, a simple minded boy visits Loper; In one hour he will open the door and look outside about twenty times; Wyeth ends up asking him what he's looking for; his delayed answer becomes the title of the table: A Crow Flew By. Words: Wyeth asks the boy what he is looking for; unconnected answer that becomes the title Atmosphere: absurd, at the limit of the supportable for the concentrated painter Issue: the chance of a word provides the title and the meaning of the work
À deux heures du matin, Wyeth se souvien: At two o'clock in the morning, Wyeth suddenly remembers the beam of light falling upon the eye and quickly makes a sketch highlighting the shadow passing through the face; it fixes the final size of the head and decides to reduce the figure in the composition. Atmosphere: night solitude of a painter who works only by day Issue: the return of the founding vision
Exposition collective organisée par Edwa: Collective exhibition organized by Edward Steichen; Archer, presented as “young amateur” as Hazel-Frieda Larsen, contributes seven portrait studies; Two photos of Quiet House hanging side by side: Asawa profile in front of the doors, and a close-up on a door handle 7 portraits; the photo on the right slightly smaller; the screws of the handle feature a face with two eyes and a mouth Consequences: New York recognition of the work of Archer
Exposition collective de photographies s: Collective exhibition of photographs under the direction of Steichen: Bourke-White, Levitt, Lange, Hoban, Bubley and Hazel-Frieda Larsen (Archer). The press release describes it as an “young amateur” with “portrait studies”. Press release: “She is a polio patient, and during her convalescence has done some of her photography from a wheelchair”; she teaches Black Mountain College and makes herself known for her close-ups revealing faces
Excédé par la lenteur de la faculté (il: Excessed by the slowness of the faculty (it took two-thirds of the votes to change the statutes), and having led the college during the six months of crisis after the resignations Albers-Dreier, Pittenger resigned, although the Board proposed to extend it by one year. two-thirds majority required to amend the statutes Consequences: Start of a double rector search (Forbes and faculty committee)
Exposition groupée associant artistes lo: Group exhibition involving local artists, sponsoring companies and institutions to identify talent transferable to industry; the price included an order from the sponsoring company. Asawa submits five wallpaper projects; Guermonprez also participates. Five designs of wallpaper.
Parmi les biens qu'Albers laisse en part: Among the goods that Albers leaves when leaving are 2,000 feet of yellow pine floors he wants the college to sell as his agent; the college refuses this responsibility. 2000 feet (linear) of yellow pine floor; letters Warrington to Albers (2 Dec. 1949) and Albers to treasurer (3 Jul. 1950) Consequences: Durable litigation on the property of Albers
Invité à parler à Studio 35, Bill exige: Invited to talk to Studio 35, Bill requires Motherwell, then in Boston, to give the lecture, which Elaine co-wrote; Bill and Elaine, like other members of the Club, do not resist listening to it Consequences: symptom of feuds between surreal factions and downtown
Elle dit à Albers vouloir inclure ses th: She tells Albers to include her color theories; he replied that he was going to make the Homage to the Square “based on color” series; two weeks later he completed about one hundred tables of the same format; it describes the “simplicité aseptique, presque militante” born from calculations on milled paper and oil sketches, and perceives the “sensibilité inavouée” of the “peculiarly gentle and tentative” lines and the translucent atmosphere of matte colors about 100 paintings in two weeks, all of the same dimension Consequences: it writes on works for which Albers remains known
Elaine entreprend un long article sur Al: Elaine undertakes a long article on Albers and wants to include its color theories; Albers replies that it will make a series, Homage to the Square, based on color. Two weeks later he completed a hundred canvases of the same format. about 100 paintings, all of the same size, produced in two weeks; calculations on milled paper, oil sketches Consequences: Elaine writes on works for which Albers remains the best known; it describes their “simplicité aseptique, presque militante” and their “sensibilité non avouée”
Après avoir prolongé son été à Provincet: After extending his summer in Provincetown until autumn (working without heating, then streptococcal infection and back to New York), Elaine squatte successively the apartment of Edwin Denby Street West 21st, then the studio of painter Bill Brown Street 100e, awakened each morning by “dirty ditties” sung by kids on the stairs. She claims to have held eight workshops in 1950. West 21st Street; 100th Street; eight studios in one year; Streptococcal infection
À la quatrième expo personnelle de Pollo: At Pollock's fourth personal exhibition at Betty Parsons, Elaine denigrates all canvases except one — out of loyalty to Bill or sincere scepticism — within reach of voices of Greenberg and Krasner, his most fervent defenders.
L'été précédent, Excavation partant vers: The previous summer, Excavation going to Venice, Elaine tells Bill that she reminds him of the Triumph of Death of Brueghel; He then showed her the magazine whose cover reproduced this painting — she was right, as usual. magazine cover reproducing Brueghel
Matter, qui loue une chambre pour août,: Matter, who rents a room for August, invites Elaine; the invitation the charm because the frame sounds “fantastiquement incivilisé” and promises “créer des ennuis” with “certaines harpies délirantes” (unidentified women that Matter had complained about).
Deux ans après l'été de Black Mountain,: Two years after the summer of Black Mountain, now Dean of the Design Department at Yale, Albers invites Bill to animate bi-weekly writings for painter students; Bill quits after two semesters. Elaine, a lecturer invited to Yale in 1967, will love teaching much more than he did. Crits twice a week; stop after two semesters; Elaine invited to Yale in 1967 Consequences: Durable contrast between the taste of Elaine for teaching and Bill's rejection.
Josef accepte la présidence du départeme: Josef accepts the chairmanship of the Yale Design Department; The Albers is moving to New Haven. Nick Cernovich, Student Moderator, organ: Nick Cernovich, Student Moderator, organizes a student survey: a large majority voted for the re-engagement of M.C., but also of Levi and Fiore. Consequences: Contradicts Board purging
La faculté établit un compromis : recteu: La faculty establishes a compromise: rector guaranteed three years, sharing with the Board the powers of appointment and re-engagement, responsible with the treasurer of the annual budget (subject to approval of the Board), non-teaching and dedicated to administration. Three-year term Consequences: Allows offers to Ballou and Huss
Fin juin, la faculté offre le poste de r: At the end of June, the faculty offered the position of Rector to Richard Ballou, Director of Education of the Ethical Culture Schools; and the position of Business Manager (and Professor of Drama) to Wesley Huss, a Quaker friend of Don Warrington, passed through the Friends Service Committee and the Hedgerow Theater.
Après leur voyage à La Nouvelle-Orléans,: After their trip to New Orleans, Tom and Michael came back on their way to college on a Sunday late in the afternoon, hungry and exhausted. There was nothing left to eat in their kitchen at the Meadows Inn except a box of Quaker Oats, which Tom prepared on an Coleman stove. Consequences: Reunion with Charles Olson that welcomes them with relief.
Un jeune auto-stoppeur/chaffeur blond au: A young hitchhiker/blond driver in the face of a choir child takes care of them, invites them to eat a hamburger, claims to check a tire, and disappears with their suitcases while they order. Tom had offered to pay burger, coffee and pie. Hamburger of the thief remained cold on the counter. Consequences: Rumaker loses a week of clothes, razor, toothbrush, and the only new thing he had: a suitcase given by his mother. He's coming home with less than nothing.
Charles passe devant Meadows Inn, grimpa: Charles passes in front of Meadows Inn, climbing carefully on the pine roots of the way, comes to talk to Tom and Michael through the mosquito window to welcome them, insisting on his joy of seeing them again. He seemed to be watching their return. Tom tells about the journey and the flight; Charles, fond of good stories, listen avidly. Consequences: Rumaker feels an overwhelming sense of security when returning to the earth of Black Mountain.
Tom achète avec sa solde GI une Buick 19: Tom buys with his GI balance a grey Buick 1950 in good condition, with three decorative “hublots” chromes on either side of the hood. “portholes” chromes are what sold the model to Tom (and millions of others). Car parked on grass in front of Meadows Inn. Consequences: Allows shopping in the city, beer trips to Ma Peak's, and film sessions at Asheville.
Après le voyage, Tom achète une Buick 19: After the trip, Tom buys a grey 1950 Buick with its GI demobilization balance, attracted by the three small decorative chrome windows on either side of the hood. Car parked on grass in front of Meadows Inn. Allows ice races, supplies in town, beer at Ma Peak's, cinema at Asheville. Consequences: Tom “file” on every occasion in his new toy.
Quelques jours après le retour de La Nou: A few days after the return of New Orleans, Rumaker discovers that he caught some crabs, a memory of his Cajun. He will eventually laugh at this episode as part of his education, as the entire journey — “on and off campus”.
Richards traduit Knights of the Round Ta: Richards translated Knights of the Round Table by Cocteau (1937), translated and staged his surreal comedy Marriage on the Eiffel Tower (1923) in June, and directed Yeats' The Death of Cuchulain the same month. printed program of The Death of Cuchulain dated 4 June 1950
Le Board vote par bulletin secret la non: The Board shall vote by secret ballot on M.C.'s non-recommitment; the faculty is stunned, M.C. madroyed; it “soulève une terrible tempête” Words: “un absolute thunderbolt”; “mon amour du lieu... était si incontesté que je ne pouvais imaginer être renvoyée” Atmosphere: shock, indignation Issue: political purge disguised as an administrative measure
Ils montent l'escalier extérieur en cat-: They climb the outside staircase in Cat-bourgeois; Cajun protects its new lime green sheets with a blanket; he spends a long time in the toilet (washing); he returns naked, full tanned, lying on his belly; after the act, it appears to rinse; He discovers a stain of K-Y on a sheet and rubs it with a soapy sponge slammed with tongue; He tries to ejaculate but fails; He confesses his blockage with self-destructiveness. Words: “They're new and I don' want 'em to git stained” (They're new, I don't want them to stain). “Ahm all greased and ready, baby” (I'm lubricated and ready, baby). “Maybe Ahm just an assman like Miz Peppah and not a cocksman” (Maybe I'm just an ass like Miz Pepper, not a dick). Atmosphere: Moon clear through flaps, scent of tropical flowers, slow ceiling fans, feline nervousness, tenderness mixed with anxiety. Issue: The sexual humiliation of Cajun, the permanent fear of the 1950s, the loneliness of two men in a sensual and dangerous city.
Le matin du départ (samedi), le Cajun em: On the morning of departure (Saturday), Cajun takes Michael to the Cree pharmacy where he works; chicory coffee for Michael, Coca for him; He presents Michael to his colleagues who look at them ironically. Words: The Cajun, with a challenge point: “Yeah, Ah slept with 'im” (Yeah, I slept with him). Atmosphere: Fluorescent light without romance, nervousness in the eyes of Cajun, this “vieille peur des années 1950 même à La Nouvelle-Orléans”. Issue: The gap between the night of desire and the day of social fear.
Le jeune chauffeur blond au visage d'enf: The young blonde driver with the face of a choir child offers them a burger in a small alley café; he claims to check a tire; They order three burgers; they use toilets; driver's burger cools; Tom goes out to check and comes back scared: the man and their suitcases have disappeared; They're waiting unnecessarily. Words: “Ahm so famished ma' belly's kissin' ma' backbone” (I am so hungry that my belly embraces my column). “That's mighty white a' ya” (It's very white on your part — thank you). “Maybe he'll be back” (Maybe he'll come back) — Tom, weak. Atmosphere: Dark alley, grinning screenendoor, slow realization of deception, shame. Issue: Loss of property, injury of pride of Rumaker, crack in the complicity of the two friends.
Dimanche fin d'après-midi, affamés, ils: Sunday late afternoon, hungry, they find only Quaker Oats only Tom cooked on the Coleman; Charles passes past, jumping on pine roots, comes to talk to them through the mosquito net window, happy to see them again; Tom tells the journey and the flight, Charles listens avidly. Words: Charles insists on his joy of seeing them again. Atmosphere: Heat of return, security recovered, shame of Rumaker at the idea that Charles knows they were fooled. Issue: The contrast between the deceptive outside world and the college shelter.
Mi-juillet, Ballou refuse le rectorat, i: In mid-July, Ballou refused the rectorate, invoking the “confusion” between “communauté et éducation” at Black Mountain and the faculty's indecision on the role of the rector, except raising funds. Wes Huss accepts the position of business manager. Consequences: Conservatives give up hope for “responsable” reorganization
Pendant les longs après-midi paresseux d: During the long lazy afternoons of summer, Tom and Michael swim in the swirl of Snake River and take the sun on the rocks. The sons of hostile farmers sometimes throw stones at them from the bushes. The water is full of tritons that Tom calls “newts” to reassure Michael, but that look like snakes. Consequences: They become “noirs comme la terre” sun.
Après le déjeuner, un gros plombage tomb: After lunch, a big filling falls and the tooth starts to hurt horribly. Rumaker panics and will knock on the back door of Charles, the only one with a car at that time. Charles is lying on her bed (dressed this time), perhaps after her own breakfast. He is annoyed, finds it a nuisance, a tax. Rumaker must beg twice. Consequences: Charles reluctantly accepts to take him to his old convertible, silent and heavy-duty Ford during the ride.
Sur le chemin, ils passent devant des bl: On the way, they pass in front of black bleachers sweating behind a rusty mosquito net door. The dentist, a bald little man in white blouse, is direct and effective. Office on the second floor of a brick building, narrow staircase. Cost: “quelques dollars”. Charles remains silent on return. Consequences: La pain stops. Rumaker is grateful despite the silence of Charles.
Un dramaturge brun banal d'une trentaine: A typical thirty-year-old brown playwright reads a pacifist play during a Sunday evening program. Charles starts to sneeze, first in a low voice and then loud enough for the author to hear it, driving the audience. The playwright, first sure of himself, casts alarmed glances, reads at all speed, and then escapes into the night. Wes Huss, the only real pacifist on board, keeps silence and his face controlled. Consequences: The playwright was never seen again. Charles again expresses its rejection of pacifism in the following course.
Fauché après le voyage et le vol, Rumake: Failed after travel and flight, Rumaker entrusts its concern to Charles. Charles insists: you need to tighten the belt even further, and suggests applying to Swannanoa's blanket spinning, a job rumor for the night shift.
