Consequences: Rumaker refuses internally (experience from past factories, shipyard with his father). Charles, feeling his refusal, then proposes to wash his windows and dust his books for $5.
Charles revient furieux d'une course en: Charles returns furiously from a race in town with Kate, two years old, because a shopkeeper was too hard with the kid who was searching in candy or something. Kate didn't understand the woman's anger. Consequences: Charles informs the entire community of its anger.
Un dramaturge pacifiste de passage (brun: A pacifist playwright (brown, banal, early thirties) reads one of his plays during a Sunday evening program in the basement of the Studies. Charles sneezes first slowly and then gets stronger, driving the audience. The author, first sure of himself, accelerates his reading and escapes in the night, never seen again. Wes Huss, the only real pacifist on board, keeps silence and his face controlled. Rumaker joins the laughs, which he believes to be an “thug Black Mountain régulier”. Consequences: Charles repeats its rejection of pacifism and rests the question of “maraudeurs sur la colline” and marauders per se.
Fauché après La Nouvelle-Orléans et le v: Failed after New Orleans and the theft, Rumaker entrusts its money worries to Charles, who again recommends applying to Swannanoa's blanket spinning (night shift hiring rust), in order to be able to follow its day courses, including “Reading the Newspaper”. A bus would pass on the county road near the VA hospital, but Rumaker doubts it's driving at night. Work from 8 to 10 hours night. Rumaker has already done factory jobs (including the shipyard with his father) and refuses internally. Consequences: Charles, seeing his refusal, offers him $5 to wash his windows and dust the books from the living room library.
Rumaker, paniqué par un plombage tombé,: Rumaker, panicked by a fallen filling, knocks on the mosquito door; Charles is lying on her bed, dressed, annoying; Rumaker must beg twice; Charles reluctantly accepts; Silent ride in Ford convertible; Consultation with a direct and effective dentist; Silent return. Atmosphere: Pulsative pain, timidity broken by urgency, massade silence of Charles, shame of Rumaker. Issue: La Dependence of poor student on rectorate, asymmetry of power, generosity under conditions.
Dimanche soir ; le dramaturge commence s: Sunday evening; The playwright begins his reading, confident; Charles sneezes gently and then louder, driving the audience; Rumaker joins the laughs; The author precipitates his reading, looks panicked over his pages, ends in gallop and disappears in the night. Atmosphere: Pack laughs, reader panic, Wes Huss frozen and silent. Issue: La social cruelty of the college, the power of Olson over the group, the cowardice accomplice of Rumaker.
Après le refus poli de Rumaker aux filat: After Rumaker's polite refusal to shoot, Charles, as if he had just thought about it (but he probably read the refusal in his face), proposes $5 to wash his windows and dust the books in the living room. Words: Rumaker thinks: “Cinq dollars, une petite fortune, me permettrait de manger encore quelques semaines.” Atmosphere: Fun, gratitude, fragile dignity. Issue: La charity disguised as work, the student's in extremis rescue at the start.
Olson et Connie étant partis en visite,: Olson and Connie having gone on a visit, Dawson and LaFarge occupy the small brick house two days, sleeping in sleeping bags in the lobby, exploring the library, taking showers in the basement, eating what they bought at the neighborhood market. Sleeping bag or blankets in the lobby; shower without curtain in the basement, cement floor; dishes made in a tiny sink Consequences: When they return, Olson wakes them up and tells them that they must leave; Dawson stays in D.C. at Ken and Neil Noland.
Au retour inopiné du couple, Olson entre: When the couple returns unexpectedly, Olson enters while the two young people are still sleeping on the floor of the hall; Dawson wakes up sitting, sees the bathroom door open; Olson naked, hairy, huge, crashes on the landing three steps higher, the kitchen bias behind it, announces to them that they have to leave, seeds with bright eyes in front of their shimmering, then disappears in the next room; They fold sheets and blankets and pack their bags. Words: It means they have to leave — “okay, get out”. Atmosphere: Dawn, fun, redness and laughter of the two young people Issue: The carnal and childish authority of Olson on its former students
Les deux descendent l'étroit escalier ca: The two descend the narrow staircase hidden behind a tiny door, folded in half to laugh at the idea of the giant Olson on these steps; Everyone takes the shower without curtain, on the cement, thinking that not showering in the shower of Olson would have been unthinkable; They had to bend and twist like him. Atmosphere : Fool laughter accomplice, robber intimacy of the master's house
Josef est invité à présider le Départeme: Josef is invited to chair Yale University's Design Department; Albers leaves BMC for Connecticut. Consequences: End of their BMC period
Après l'offre de Sawyer et Howe au print: After Sawyer and Howe's offer in the spring of 1950 at New York, Albers began in September 1950 and settled with Anni on the outskirts of New Haven. Letter from Osborn to Albers (April 1950) pushing him to Sawyer; William Huff reports that Kahn, consulted, was “vendu” at Albers and “enchanté par Anni, straight from the Old Testament”; Switzerland had proposed a department of Basic Design and Sculpture under Albers. Consequences: Beginning of the period Yale (1950-1958).
Alvin Eisenman, aussi typographe de Yale: Alvin Eisenman, also typographer of Yale University Press, launched the program in the fall of 1950, with an undergraduate component added to the insistence of Albers. Renamed “Graphic Design” in 1959, he placed Yale at the forefront of the domain; His graduates spread Albers ideas across the country. Eisenman describes Albers “very interested in the program, very, very helpful, and kindly”
Les deux programmes accèdent au statut d: Both programs became degree programs in September 1950.
Twombly rencontre Rauschenberg à l'Art S: Twombly meets Rauschenberg at the Art Students League of New York in autumn 1950; they quickly become friends and Twombly follows Rauschenberg to Black Mountain the following summer. Consequences: arrival of Twombly at BMC, summer 1951
De Kooning fait la navette vers New Have: De Kooning commuted to New Haven to teach Yale in the fall of 1950. Weekly shuttle New York–New Haven.
Le dîner de Thanksgiving 1950 a lieu sur: Thanksgiving 1950 dinner takes place on a stage setting on the first floor of the Eiffel Tower terrace. After the meal, the community attended the ballet play by Jean Cocteau Les mariages de la tour Eiffel (1921), translated by M.C. Richards. The absurd plot: a photographer tries to photograph a wedding; an ostrich saizes from its apparatus and runs away; A rifle hunter hunts the bird in the lattice of the tower; A lion devours a guest, a cyclist asks for his way to Chatou, a swimmer from Trouville appears; telegrams fall from the sky (one shot in flight); a General tells of a hunting expedition to Africa with a pie covered with wasps; finally the brides and their guests disappear in the plane, swallowed all round, and the camera exits from the scene followed by its bellows like a tank. Decorate: terrace on the first floor of the Eiffel Tower; giant camera on stage large enough to hold the wedding under its pleated skirt; June Rice Christensen in a large jacket and wig, on a ladder behind the shutter; by the openings of the bellows one sees the guests shaking handkerchiefs and, below, walking feet; the device leaves the scene followed by its bellows “comme un char”. Consequences: Hazel Larsen Archer photographes the representation, image that opens the study: a camera photographing a camera.
Elaine de Kooning publie dans Art News (: Elaine of Kooning publishes in Art News (November 1950, pp. 40-43, 57-58) an article dedicated to Josef Albers, former master of Bauhaus at the time teaching Yale, which she had alongside Black Mountain. Art News, November 1950, pages 40-43 and 57-58. Consequences: The article is included in his combined writings; he documents his gaze on the pedagogy of Albers.
Richards met en scène sa traduction du M: Richards features its translation of Cocteau's Marriage on the Eiffel Tower; the refectory becomes a total environment with the Eiffel Tower platform overlooking a skyline in Paris; actors and public have Thanksgiving dinner before the play. Atmosphere: Reconstituted Paris in the North Caroline Mountains Issue: fusion of community meal and total theatre
Après le repas servi sur un décor en ter: After the meal served on a terraced décor of the Eiffel Tower, Cocteau's room begins: the photographer (June Rice Christensen, checked jacket and swollen wig, on a ladder behind the shutter of the giant camera) tries to photograph the wedding; an ostrich spring from the aircraft, a hunter chases it into the lattice, a lion devours a guest, a cyclist asks Chatou, telegrams fall from the sky, a General tells his pie to wasps; finally the brides and all their guests disappear into the camera, and the camera exits the stage followed by its bellows “comme un char”. Hazel Larsen Archer, in the room, photograph: by the openings of the bellows one sees the guests shaking handkerchiefs and feet that walk. Words : The decor was on the first floor of the Eiffel Tower terrace; The bellows follow the “like a wagon” device. Atmosphere: Absurd, burlesque, carnivoresque — joyful chaos in the blurred light of the movement captured by Archer. Issue: A camera that devours its subjects, photographed by a camera that dialogues with them: the scene bases the whole study on Archer.
La désintégration du mariage de Levi sur: La disintegration of the marriage of Levi over the next six months pushed him out of the community in December 1950; Corkran decided to leave in the fall of 1950, with Trayer, Quakers and Goldowski abandoning any “responsable” reorganization. Consequences: Consolidation of “nouveau” Black Mountain
Levi quitte la communauté ; Richards déc: Levi leaves the community; Richards decides to stay, making their separation final. Consequences: Richards then played a decisive role in 1951 recruitment
Sa mère, qui après le renvoi par le père: His mother, who after the father's dismissal had sought blindly in the streets of Philadelphia, wrote to him to know whether he was coming back to Christmas; Rumaker refuses, writes a lie; he does not want to leave Merrill or face his family, and wants to be there at the imminent return of Olson hundreds of miles of autostop to the parents, then the return
Pour les fêtes, la voisine Cissy Oppenhe: For the holidays, the neighbour Cissy Oppenheimer offers everyone an orange with cloves; the couple breathes them under the duvet by the first large snows (which melt in large part the next noon in this climate that quickly softens) aromatic oranges nailed with cloves, heavy snow melting at noon, hills of Seven Sisters with bare trees smoking in the lively air
Lettres écrites à Robert Creeley, qui le: Written letters to Robert Creeley, which edited and published them in 1953 in Palma, Mallorca (Miscellaneous Press). Maximus Poems Epigraph: “All my life I've heard / one makes many”
Elaine figure comme personne à charge su: Elaine is listed as a dependant on Bill's 1951 tax return. Bill's income was $7,610, including 4,000 first prize from the Chicago Art Institute for Excavation (1950); $1,750 in medical expenses for broken leg of Elaine; The Sidney Janis Gallery advances her supplies money. income of $7,610; price $4,000; medical expenses $1,750 Consequences: gradual improvement in sales over the decade
Dord Fitz, artiste, enseignant et marcha: Dord Fitz, artist, teacher and merchant in Amarillo, Texas, is arrested on an “morals charge” following a homosexual meeting and dismissed from the University of Kentucky; He will remain a man of family secrecy. Kentucky University Dismissal Consequences: Fitz now wears an “moi masqué”, secret that he fears that a portrait of Elaine will reveal
Williams revoit Lou Harrison, qu'il avai: Williams saw Lou Harrison again, which he had seen at Town Hall in 1949, and became his friend during the summer at the college. Consequences: Sustainable friendship between the two men.
Quand Williams conduit jusqu'à Asheville: When Williams drives up to Asheville for the ABC store, Harrison asks for a bottle of Rock and Rye. Rock and Rye: aromatized rye whisky liqueur with candi sugar syrup and fruit, with a disgusting sweetness; only person known to Williams to like this; missing product from ABC blinds.
Tudor vient comme accompagnateur de la d: Tudor comes as an escort to the dancer Katherine Litz; concerts of works by Webern, Schönberg, Cage, Lou Harrison, Stefan Wolpe and student composers. He is preparing the New York creation of the Second Boulez Sonata for autumn; Richards accompanies him to New York and translates Artaud, preparing the climate of Cage “premier happening” played at the college. Concert program, creation of Boulez at NY Consequences: Translation of the Theatre and its double, atmosphere of happening
Mildred et Branwen explorent le site en: Mildred and Branwen explore the site by looking through the windows and find a huge rusty kerosene stove; the driver of the college's old pick-up helps her get down to their rusty kerosene stove kitchen, only a kettle provided, neither pots nor food Consequences: a step out of the “âge de pierre”; possible tea and coffee
En tutoriel, après avoir lu ses nouvelle: As a tutorial, after reading his news (male adults, including a mature alcoholic actor seeking salvation in a church in the Bowery), Olson thundered that it was pure shit and ordered him to keep only one newspaper, one hour a day minimum, and to return the following summer to show him. one hour of newspaper per day minimum, one year Consequences: Gray obeyed, kept his journal during his senior year, changed his thesis to “Kierkegaard's View on the Demise of Christianity”, and returned in the summer of 1952 — at the threshold of his vocation as a writer
Premier été de la témoin : poses superco: First summer of the witness: supercool silent poses, bare feet, long hair and black glasses in men, easy nudism and bisexuality — fads of the nascent Beat Generation, precursors of the 1960s style. She cuts her hair short and in battle “comme une punk”. hair cut very short and irregular ; Generalized imitation of phonetic spellings of Olson (waz, egg, luv, kulchur, Yrsself, ga-wan, Ru-man-tick, egg-zack-tly), second hand borrowed from Pound of the 1920s
Une jeune femme danse devant le miroir d: A young woman dances in front of the mirror of the main hall from 7am until dinner, stopping only to feed the baby who brailles in a basket near the exercise bar. She doesn't take any classes and talks to anyone: ten hours in a row to look at herself in the ice. 7 a.m. at dinner, about 10 a.m.; basket; exercise bar; mirror
Au dîner, Olson torse nu sous une serape: At dinner, Olson bare torso under a beep thrown on the shoulders, sitting next to Cage always very formal in black urban costume, tie and pointed black shoes very bright; Cage punctuates the cultivated laconism of the table of his zen monk laughter while meditating on his next Happening. will; black suit; crystalline laughter; pointed varnished shoes
Elle accompagne le poète Jonathan Willia: She accompanied poet Jonathan Williams to the recruitment office when he refused to be incorporated into the US Army for conscientious objection. Consequences: She sees it as a political education as important as that received from her family or college.
Rauschenberg aide l'auteur du témoignage: Rauschenberg helps the witness author unload his old Ford 39; he discovers a pack of small toles which the author intended to be reused, covered with zinc white, suggesting the original compositions; Rauschenberg is excited about these bleached canvases. old Ford model 1939; small canvases covered with a layer of zinc white; original shapes vaguely visible below Consequences: The author, disappointed, feels less sure of what he will paint on these paintings
Quelques jours après son arrivée, l'aute: A few days after his arrival, the author sees Twombly sitting on the steps of South Lodge, helping Rauschenberg apply matt white paint to a series of canvases mounted on chassis — the same ones that will become the White Paintings. brushed white paint on stretched canvases, on the steps Consequences: These paintings will be exhibited at the Betty Parsons Gallery
Début 1951, le collège envoie quelques d: In early 1951, the college sent a few requests to attract black students; The only result is a severe reprimand of a black educator for writing “Negro” with a tiny one.
Des rumeurs filtrent vers Black Mountain: Rumors filter into Black Mountain: some members do “font pas leur part”, financial instability, everyday mechanics leave little time for interpersonal exploration. La community dissolves after three years — orderly dissolution, stresses Wallen, not bursting discord. The members, about fifty with children and grandchildren scattered on the Pacific coast, still meet each Thanksgiving for five days. three years; ~50 people; five-day annual Thanksgiving meeting Consequences: secret satisfaction of some at Black Mountain
Au début des années cinquante, quand Cag: In the early 1950s, when Cage took the path of chance and “indéterminacy”, Albers told him that he had “renoncé à sa responsabilité d'artiste”; sympathy and friendship break.
Le mariage, connu pour être fragile, se: The marriage, known to be fragile, ended in a separation in 1951.
Au printemps 1951, après une nouvelle ro: In spring 1951, after a new round of factionalism, a very different Black Mountain emerged — almost the opposite of what Natasha, Quakers, Pittenger, Trayer and Corkran had worked to build; all leave college with disgust, for different reasons and at different times; Duberman notes the darkness of the alignments: each major participant assures him that all his other sources are incorrect Natasha and Bill Levi, fountainheads of the conflict, their personalities often having more than educational policy issues Consequences: Natasha moves from discreet member to periphery (before 1948-49) to real leader of the power after the departure of the Albers-Dreier
Olson propose de titrer cette période «: Olson proposes to title this period “The Afterwards, or the Original Damsel Re'deemed”, starting in 1951, without end date. For him, Black Mountain returns to the “cœur de la vieille pomme”: what Rice said in the first catalogue, that the arts share the curriculum center with ordinary studies. Like Rice, Olson believes in renting, not becoming an “institution”: inheriting from an institution, he disassembles it and sells it in pieces so that live something else — people, life in them. Title proposed by Olson: “The Afterwards, or the Original Damsel Re'deemed — you might call 1951 on — with no end date known or in sight!” Consequences: Radical individualization of experience, “chief glory of Black Mountain” according to Duberman
Départs plus ou moins amicaux : les Jenn: More or less friendly departures: the Jennerjahns leave to finish the GI Bill by a year in France; Turner opens a full-time pottery in New York state; the Trayer are going to grow the land in Earlham; Paul Leser joins Hartford Seminary for salary; Natasha leaves for Paris for a year, with less comfort. Consequences: Multiple vacancies
Sur de nombreux candidats, seuls Victor: Of many candidates, only Victor Sprague (biology) and John Adams (anthropology) receive and accept an offer. Consequences: Very small resident faculty
Olson revient pour rester, droit de Lerm: Olson returns to stay, right of Lerma (Yucatán), with its collection y & x. Richards, gone for the summer, offers her her apartment and her place “room and board”; Fitton and Oppenheimer raise a hundred dollars among students as front pay — that's enough to convince him. 100 dollars collected from students Consequences: Olson becomes the heart of the college for its last five years

Pendant l'été 1951, Tudor joue la Deuxiè: During the summer of 1951, Tudor played the Second Boulez Sonata; Olson says something like 'this is the only piece of music since Bach'. Consequences: Williams comments that Olson has only heard three plays since Bach, but likes people who say "worse" things.
Williams écrit des pastiches « cummings/: Williams writes “cummings/Patchen” pastiches full of gilded singing mist and snakes; Olson, which doesn't like Patchen or cummings, “très lourd” with him, puts them into pieces with an “vaste dégoût de hibou”; It takes about two months before they become friends. “fog and gold singing snakes”; “vast owlish distaste” Consequences: initial blur and friendship
Premier numéro au printemps 1951 ; la re: First issue in spring 1951; the magazine becomes the meeting place for many authors who will later appear in The Black Mountain Review and will be called “École poétique de Black Mountain”. Consequences: Black Mountain Review Prefiguration
Origin publie son premier numéro au prin: Origin published its first issue in the spring of 1951; It became the meeting place for many future contributors to The Black Mountain Review, later known as “Black Mountain School of Poets”. Consequences: Prepare the ground for the 1954 review.
Pour sa photo du catalogue BMC de l'auto: For his picture of the fall 1951 BMC catalogue, Olson chose the currency “For use, now” — “Pour l'usage, maintenant”. Catalogue BMC autumn 1951
Shahn, qui y a enseigné la peinture l'ét: Shahn, who taught painting there the previous summer, boasts the unconventional virtues of Black Mountain College and enthusiasm for Charles Olson, the giant poet who teaches writing there. Consequences: Rumaker writes to the college; It's the origin of the whole story.
Interrogée sur Black Mountain, la peintr: When asked about Black Mountain, the painter Mary Reed says she heard about it as an “nid de communistes et d'homosexuels” — which, in the McCarthy era, seduces Rumaker all the more. Consequences: Strengthens the decision to go
Connie évoque Rauschenberg, étudiant en: Connie evokes Rauschenberg, a painting student who left in the spring, of which “Black on Black” and then “White on White” made some noise in New York's avant-garde circles. Consequences: Radiation from college outside.
Achat du n° 2 d'Origin (été 1951) chez C: Purchase of the No.2 of Origin (Summer 1951) from Carroll Williams; The poem “A Po-sy, A Po-sy” leaves him totally confused (“aw, piss, and sing, be / robert burns...”), to the point of doubting his intuition. Slim review purchased at the college store Consequences: Doubt on Olson, quickly dissipated by its personal magnetism
Après le retour d'Olson, qui presse de l: After the return of Olson, who urged Dostoevski to read, Rumaker devoured the library romels and adapted the chapter of the Grand Inquisitor in one piece for the course of Wes: Spanish prison cell at night, two characters, Christ in second advent threatening the benevolent tyranny of the Church; pure transcription without dramaturgy; Wes reads all “adaptation” aloud in class, he and Duck Daley react with a compassionate tolerance Consequences: Learning failure; Rumaker too naive to see its shortcomings
Deux ans plus tôt, Rumaker annonce à sa: Two years earlier, Rumaker announced to his mother that he would no longer go to church; She yells at him to go to a psychiatrist, to stop blackmailing him; After their only explosive fight, she curls silently near the window. The father then puts him out. The priest advises her: “Ce n'est qu'une phase, il reviendra au bercail.” He passes in front of the speaker to catch the bus to his factory work without one more word; then received from a sister-in-law. Consequences: First separation; The second is BMC itself.
Rumaker découvre l'écriture de Creeley d: Rumaker discovers the writing of Creeley in the summer issue 1951 of Origin, a journal published by Cid Corman in Boston dedicated to Creeley. new “In the Summer”, “3 Fate Tales”, “Mr. Blue”; poems “Love” and “Hart Crane (2)”; text largely unpublished elsewhere, even at Various Press Consequences: beginning of a sustainable fascination
À l'automne 1951, avant l'article de Ros: In the fall of 1951, before Rosenberg's article on Action Painting, Elaine describes the way Smith works and draws an aesthetic from it: the artist's moral integrity stems from his honest collaboration with materials and his willingness to find, not repeat, an image; the final work is the sum of the gestures made in matter. industrial workshop: concrete floors, glass windows to the north, round belly stove, tools powered by a Ford engine; radio broadcasting classical music; Workwear Consequences: It establishes the critical approach that others will use and draw the archetype of the existentialist American-hero artist; she becomes a starmaker in the eyes of the Club
Venue du New Jersey, Hartigan voit les p: Coming from New Jersey, Hartigan sees Pollock's first spout paintings; experience changes his life. She remembers “bowled over, really confused and moved in an extraordinary way”. Consequences: She decides to learn from Pollock.
Pollock se saoule brutalement, hurle des: Pollock gets drunk brutally, screams obscenities, approaches violence; Lee reasons him as a child until the alcoholic stupor, then sells Pollock as a genius to Hartigan. Pollock sober is almost silent; drunk, he talks about art and says: “There are only two guys in town… Pollock and de Kooning”. Pollock recommends going to the second Kooning show at Charles Egan and telling Bill that he's sending it. Consequences: Hartigan goes to the Egan Gallery and then to the Kooning studio.
Grand dessins à l'émail noir : Hartigan: Great black enamel drawings: Hartigan finds them “magnifiques”, Pollock's parents by energy, rebellion, gesture, power. Large black enamel designs (“black enamel drawings”). Consequences: She will immediately visit Kooning.
Hartigan frappe en bas ; Bill sort la tê: Hartigan knocks down; Bill pulls his head out of the window with his Dutch accent (“Who's dat?” “Come on up, den”); She finds him compact, beautiful, movie star. Elaine emerges, ostensibly flirts with Bill and claims money for a winter coat, having already spent the given amount. Hartigan first appreciates him badly, then the intelligent and serious judge on one thing: Bill's genius. Bill says of Jackson: “Yah, Jackson is something”; Money fight for a winter coat. Consequences: Hartigan became a witness to the couple and the rivalry of Pollock/Kooning.
Un groupe d'artistes encouragés par Leo: A group of artists encouraged by Leo Castelli invests a vast vacant commercial space; the exhibition, extended at the Stable Gallery, publicly defines the core of Abstract Expressionism. Consequences: The absent ones become second knives.
Bill montre de grands dessins à l'émail: Bill shows great black enamel drawings and vivid abstract painters; praise criticism but very few sales. Consequences: Nevertheless, his reputation grew despite the absence of collectors.
Bill participe au symposium du MoMA, lié: Bill participates in the MoMA symposium, linked to Abstract Expressionist Painting and Sculpture; his statement is published in the Bulletin of the MoMA of 1951. Consequences: His ideas on art affect a wide audience
Parution du livre issu d'un manuscrit in: Publication of the book from an initial manuscript of Perls, developed by Goodman (Volume II) and implemented by Hefferline (Volume I); The three also declare themselves responsible, having solved their differences by confronting them rather than by hiding them politely. copyright 1951 ; map Library of Congress 51-14876 ; Dell Publishing, 750 Third Avenue, New York 17; David Passalaqua's cover; reference “Nineteenth Printing” Consequences: The book becomes the founding text of Gestalt therapy.
Publication du livre contenant le chapit: Publication of the book containing the chapter on retrotlexion, with experiments intended to be practiced by readers/students. Experience 13: “Mobilizing the Muscles” Consequences: The text becomes a source of theoretical material and exercises for possible workshops.
Elle réalise ses premiers dessins-poèmes: She makes her first poem drawings while waiting for the birth of her son Consequences: Initiation of her work mixing words and images
Chaet, venue de Boston pour l'entretien,: Chaet, coming from Boston for the interview, receives from Albers instruction to bring the canvases rather than slides; Albers criticizes him for his work, asks him how he would teach, and hire him immediately, without a committee, in an hour and a half. Maintenance of approximately 1h30; Chaet and Robert Scott are the only external hirings of Albers Consequences: Chaet joins the department; admissions are made on the same model
Albers présente un texte sans titre à la: Albers presents a titleless text at the International Design Conference in the summer of 1951. JAAF Archives.
Session d'été 1951 centrée sur un seul m: Summer 1951 session focused on a single medium, photography, with Harry Callahan, Arthur Siegel and Aaron Siskind combined. Consequences: inspires the Pottery Seminar of autumn 1952
Larsen organise une session d'été consac: Larsen organizes a summer session dedicated to photography and invites Callahan, Siskind and Siegel to become major figures in the history of photography. Callahan and Siegel then taught at the Chicago Institute of Design; Siskind will join the faculty the following year. Consequences: La creative photography as a subject of study was at the time in the United States
Williams, refusé au cours de Callahan à: Williams, refused during Callahan at the Chicago Institute of Design, follows Callahan's advice to register for Black Mountain; There, he fell under the charm of Charles Olson and his interest went from photography to writing and publishing. Consequences: Foundation (just before its arrival, in a Chinese restaurant in San Francisco with David Ruffin) of the Jargon Society, small press become project of the BMC Museum
Oates, étudiant dévoué de Larsen, devien: Oates, a dedicated student of Larsen, becomes the first graduate of photography college; his work is evaluated by external examiner Edward Steichen, director of the photographic department of MoMA.
Nomination comme directeur musical ; il: Appointment as musical director; He composed “Gamelan” (Suite for violin, piano and small orchestra, 1952) and Glyph's music (1951).
Œuvre multimédia : musique de Harrison p: Multimedia work: music by Harrison for eccentric amateur ensemble (piano, bells, harps, more gong and tuning as an option), choreography by Katherine Litz that is entangled in a body slipper, curtain painted by Ben Shahn inspired by Mayan glyphs and Chinese calligraphy, poetry by Olson on race, slavery and community in the modern South. piano, bells, harps, gong, tuning, body sock
Photographie de Katherine Litz dansant T: Photograph by Katherine Litz Dancing The Glyph at the Photo College at Jerome Robbins Dance Division, New York Public Library for the Performing Arts
Au printemps 1951, Turner démissionne po: In the spring of 1951, Turner resigned for family reasons and for lack of predictable time in the pot shop. He had not grasped the experimental ethos of BMC on site, but will later say that the artistic philosophy of the college affected his perception the following years. Consequences: Search for a successor.
Karnes et Weinrib passent une année de t: Karnes and Weinrib spend a year working at Sesto Fiorentino; Karnes meets the industrial architect Gio Ponti and produces Double Vase, published in Domus and awarded at the Sixteenth Ceramic Annual of the Everson Museum in Syracuse.
Pour la solvabilité, Richards restructur: For solvency, Richards restructures the program with year-round thematic institutes and renowned guest artists under contract of two months. flyer of the Summer Session in the Arts from July 9 to August 31, 1951; letter to the faculty: about four artists invited in a two-month contract feeding the whole year — “une pédagogie de l'abondance”
Jonathan Williams publie sous le nom de: Jonathan Williams publishes as Jargon Press The Dancer, marrying a poem by Oppenheimer with an ink drawing by Rauschenberg, commemorating a dance from Katherine Litz to New York.
Siegel enseigne un atelier de deux semai: Siegel teaches a two-week workshop in summer 1951; His practice is then mainly turned to colour photography. Two weeks.
Siskind, rétif à la pédagogie Bauhaus st: Siskind, a resistor to the strict design-oriented Bauhaus pedagogy, discovers at BMC an open and experimental approach where affect and expression are encouraged; he photographed in North Caroline and Kentucky (North Carolina 11). Themes: torn posters, surfaces damaged by water, scratched letters. Consequences: He accepted the position at the ID for the fall of 1951.
À son retour, Albers est parti et l'atmo: Upon his return, Albers left and the atmosphere went from intensive to individual experimentation. Rauschenberg arrives with Twombly, met at the Art Students League of New York. Anecdote: A jealous student tells Jack Tworkov not to understand why he spends so much time with Bob who never goes to class; Tworkov replied that he was interested in students when they stopped going to school. Twombly then painted abstract black and white canvases very gestures, close to the biomorph and plant Consequences: Beginning of Black Paintings
Olson passe cinq mois à Lerma, au Mexiqu: Olson spends five months in Lerma, Mexico, studying the remains of Mayan culture; he reports a renewal of his report to the letter, as an epistolary unit and as a concrete form. five months Consequences: Renewal of his art around the glyph; echo of the Albers stay in Mexico
Shahn dessine directement sur le corps d: Shahn draws directly on the student's body Nicholas Cernovich a pattern for a dance performance; This design is the basis for “A Glyph for Charles” and two large drawings, Down Fall and Nicolas C (1951). two major derived drawings: Down Fall and Nicolas C
Harrison compose The Glyph pour piano pr: Harrison composes The Glyph for prepared piano, two bells, harps, a farm fork and “peut-être” a gong; Six movements ranging from standard notation to improvisation instructions. score ink on music paper, 81⁄2 × 11 inches each; “follow dance” instruction scattered in the score Consequences: musical element of the exchange
Solo de neuf minutes : Litz apparaît et: Nine-minute solo: Litz appears and disappears six times behind a 4 × 8 foot panel painted in an enlarged version of the Shahn drawing, transforming a jersey tube costume into a succession of characters (siren → tree → stone sculpture → animal). nine minutes; 4 × 8 feet panel; jersey tube costume; the panel painted by Charles Oscar, then husband of Litz; David Tudor accompanied Litz as pianist
Conférence sur le réalisme donnée pendan: Conference on realism given during the summer session 1951; transcript retained.
En 1951, Archer organise un institut d'é: In 1951, Archer organized a summer photography institute, inviting Aaron Siskind, Arthur Siegel and Harry Callahan as guest speakers, and mounted photography exhibitions on campus. Consequences: A peak of photography at BMC under the influence of Archer.
Archer organise un institut d'été consac: Archer organizes a summer institute dedicated to photography, invites Siskind, Siegel and Callahan as guest lecturers and mounts photography exhibitions on campus Consequences: Student exhibition in the history of photography and a range of styles
Rauschenberg peint de grandes toiles à l: Rauschenberg paints large oil canvases and presses them directly into the land of Caroline from the North in the moonlight Consequences: Series read by Molesworth as an auctorial abandonment, close to index photography
Archer invite deux professeurs de l'Inst: Archer invited two professors from the Chicago Institute of Design to teach at BMC in the summer of 1951, establishing institutional links between BMC and the offspring of Bauhaus in the United States. Consequences: BMC / New Bauhaus-Institute of Design by Photography
Les objets en fil d'Asawa sont montrés a: Asawa wired objects are shown with Calder mobiles; Ray Johnson, a friend of BMC, describes a suspended room as locking “forms within forms within forms”. The most complex piece to date: Untitled (S.535), 2.20 m high, five lobes, photographed by Cunningham for the cover of Arts and Architecture and in Domus Consequences: First major visibility of Asawa
Une sculpture de cuivre de huit pieds (2: An eight-foot (2.40 m) copper sculpture suspended from the ceiling, weighing twenty pounds, first accepted and then rejected: the jurors doubted it was sculpture. “It wasn't stone, it wasn't welded steel… They thought it was craft, or something else, but not art”, say Asawa Consequences: Illustrating the exclusion of coded domestic mediums from the field of fine arts
Asawa travaille sur un revêtement mural: Asawa works on a folded paper wall covering, the same one then exposed to the Laverne showroom in San Francisco; Renk finds the solution to the unresolved problem of his design school. Wall covering; Laverne showroom. Consequences: Triggers the transmission of folding to Renk.
Après les exercices expliqués par Asawa: After the exercises explained by Asawa (derived from Albers), Renk learns the rules of folding and then spends two days and two nights drawing and folding a shape similar to an eggboard. Two days and two nights of work. Consequences: Series of folded pendants, including Folded (1953).
Publié par le Black Mountain Graphics Wo: Published by Black Mountain Graphics Workshop in 1951.
Participe à l'exposition annuelle avec d: Participates in the annual exhibition with two White Paintings.
Passe la fin de l'été et l'automne au co: Spend late summer and fall at college. Consequences: Collaboration with Cage, illustration for Jargon Press
Réalise avec Cage l'empreinte Automobile: Makes the Automobile Tire Print with Cage.
Illustre le poème « The Dancer » de Joel: Illustrating Joel Oppenheimer's poem “The Dancer”, published in Black Mountain College by Jonathan Williams as the second publication of the Jargon Press series.
Rauschenberg participe à l'exposition an: Rauschenberg participates in the annual exhibition and shows two “White Paintings”. two White Paintings
Après la publicité de Life, Sue et Bob s: After Life's publicity, Sue and Bob solicit their friends Liberman and Brodovich for work: many provocative promises, no jobs.
Rauschenberg passe la fin de l'été et l': Rauschenberg spends late summer and fall in college.
Rauschenberg et Cage réalisent ensemble: Rauschenberg and Cage together produce the auto tire print.
Rauschenberg illustre le poème publié au: Rauschenberg illustrates the poem published in the college by Jonathan Williams, the second publication of the Jargon Press series. second title of the Jargon Press
Monotype réalisé avec John Cage : des fe: Monotype made with John Cage: sheets of paper glued in a long ribbon are spread on the floor of Fulton Street; Rauschenberg ink a section of the street, Cage drives its Ford Model A through ink and then on paper. According to the interview account of Rauschenberg, Cage was the only one to own a car and declared itself ready to participate; He just had to stay on paper and “fit un travail excellent”. English version of the catalogue: twenty glued sheets; German interview version: fifty pieces, six metres long; Ford model A; Cage only motorist Consequences: The only one with blueprints to lay the foundation of the suite: direct trace of the object on the support, role of chance in an organized action
Rauschenberg peint la série des monochro: Rauschenberg paints the series of white monochromes to wall paint applied to the roll on identical canvas panels assembled in triptych. He knows right away that they will have to be painted when the color yellows; he wrote to Betty Parsons in October 1951 to say that the author of these paintings is “l'aujourd'hui”. Ordinary mural, roll, identical panels; letter to Betty Parsons, October 1951; repainted later with the help of Brice Marden Consequences: White canvases will be reused for other works when the canvas is missing, for example Trophy II
Groupe de portraits de Susan Weil, femme: Portrait group of Susan Weil, wife of Rauschenberg, pregnant with their son Christopher, posing and lying in Central Park
Betty Parsons vient sélectionner les pei: Betty Parsons comes to select the paintings, accompanied by Clyfford Still who says almost nothing and does not participate in the choice; Rauschenberg cannot help but rework much of the selection to improve it. apartment at West 96th Street; Still's silence
Début d'une amitié fondée sur admiration: Beginning of friendship based on mutual admiration and sympathy; It strengthens Rauschenberg's anti-expressionist attitude. Consequences: conscious elimination of symbolism, depth and expression in its art
Les commissaires citent les White Painti: The commissioners cite the White Paintings (1951), painted just after its transition to Black Mountain, as an iconoclastic origin of the minimalist sensitivity examined by the exposure.
Rauschenberg réalise des peintures multi: Rauschenberg makes multipanel paintings entirely white that reject the heroism of Abstract Expressionism; their blank surfaces are designed to record the shadows of the spectators and the temporality of the experience of vision multipanel paintings, bare white surfaces Consequences: They influence a generation of sculptors and painters and directly inspire 4'33" of John Cage
Depuis le Mexique, Olson laisse entendre: From Mexico, Olson suggests to his favorite students, including the painter Fielding Dawson, that he wants to return; Students organize a collection to pay for their trip. Student collection Consequences: Return of Olson, future head of the college
Pour célébrer le retour d'Olson, Shahn (: To celebrate the return of Olson, Shahn (glyphic paintings), the dancer Katherine Litz (moving interpretation of the poem) and Lou Harrison (prepared piano score) create a performance around a poem by Olson fustigating the materialistic basis of American life. partition: someone strongly presses against all the serious strings a heavy wood piece of about 2 x 2 inches placed on songs to a “angle nodal” Consequences: Ideal celebration of the vision of Olson
Photographie de Jonathan Williams montra: Jonathan Williams photograph showing Olson at the college in 1951 writing The Maximus Poems; Olson, last rector and leading influence of the 1950s. Photo of Jonathan Williams
Olson, en ville avec Alvin Lipsey, jeune: Olson, in town with Alvin Lipsey, a young nephew of the college's black stove, comes across a local auction. The boy exclaims: “C'est comme une course” (It's like a race). Olson, struck by the allusion to slave sales, writes a short poem supposed to be spontaneous, dedicated “à Alvin et aux Shahn”, and the offer to Ben Shahn, present for the summer. Exclaim by the child; “Alvin and the Shahns” dedication Consequences: Triggers glyph exchange
Shahn répond au poème d'Olson par A Glyp: Shahn responds to the poem of Olson by A Glyph for Charles, painted in “palimpseste” style without erasure. Lou Harrison (a partner of Cage, engaged in his absence) composes The Glyph for prepared piano, 2 bells, harps, tuning and perhaps a gong, offered to Katherine Litz, which choreographs a dance on this score with an enlarged version of the Shahn painting as main decor. Instrumentation: “prepared piano, 2 bells, claves, pitch fork, & perhaps, gong”; Each contribution produced separately but quickly Consequences: Interdisciplinary spontaneous collaboration model
Après deux ans de Turner, deux autres di: After two years of Turner, two other graduates of Alfred, Karnes and her husband Weinrib, take over; They have few serious students, including M.C. Richards. Karnes work deemed too functional by some; Weinrib more experimental, built from clay plates.
Dans une conférence célèbre, de Kooning: In a famous lecture, by Kooning expresses his fatigue of all the orthodoxyes of modern art and declares “I do not need a movement”, echo of the discomfort of some students of Black Mountain against the research promoted by Albers.
Pièce pour deux acteurs (le danseur : Ap: Piece for two actors (the dancer: Apollonius; The voice: Tyana, or the place), illustrated with a map of Stan VanDerBeek (“map of moves”), printed and linked to the college in the summer of 1951, in original two-coloured dishes. 8vo, two-coloured dishes, map of VanDerBeek
Ses premiers poèmes-images datent de 195: Her first poem-images date back to 1951, made while waiting for the birth of her son Christopher.
Après la naissance de Christopher, Weil: After Christopher's birth, Weil briefly returns to join Rauschenberg at Black Mountain; Motherwell and Shahn teach there this summer. She takes part in campus life without being a student, with a marriage that is untiring and a angry baby — she produces almost nothing. Consequences: End of direct link of Weil with college
Après la dernière dévastatrice querelle: After the last devastating faculty dispute, around 1951, Bill Levi left for Washington University taking their young daughter Estelle; Perhaps the lowest period for M.C., of which no one talks, probably to his relief. Washington University Consequences: Very difficult situation for M.C.
Un après-midi, elle confesse être jalous: One afternoon, she confesses to be jealous that Dawson has not yet read Moby Dick and can read it for the first time; confession of honesty, the value of which is equal to that of the book. Office with lake view Consequences: Dawson discovers what she meant: initial experience without equal after Don Quixote
Au début des années cinquante, une publi: In the early 1950s, an advertisement by the Container Corporation of America showed a brilliant watercolour by Philip Guston, which amazed them: proof that creative art could penetrate the advertising world — hope immediately denied. Consequences: Lucid illusion: their art had an effect, but still inside the system
Les deux jeunes artistes, sous l'œil de: The two young artists, under the eye of Motherwell coming to teach this summer, threw handles of pebbles on a large canvas widely covered with tar; Motherwell, between them, was: “Encore.” They were throwing. “Encore.” They were throwing. “Encore.” Large canvas mostly covered with tar; pebbles handles; Gravel patio
Le modèle ne s'étant pas présenté, Bob e: The model did not appear, so Bob and Cy rose from their drawing boards, walked in front of the class and began to undress.
Dawson découvre The Confidence-Man de Me: Dawson discovered Melville's The Confidence-Man in 1951, found it arid and then adored it; On winter days and nights, on his mattress in his study, he constantly read it — chapter 33 (p. 215, ed. Grove Press) shows him what he wanted: fiction must present another world to which one nevertheless feels the link. Chapter 33, page 215, Grove Press paper edition. Consequences: The book becomes a major influence of Dawson.
Pour ses quarante ans, Goodman écrit un: For his 40th birthday, Goodman wrote an essay in which he judged his literary career failed: no conquered audience, it's time to do something else. Consequences: He starts receiving patients as a Gestalt therapist
Goodman, qui a aidé Fritz et Lore Perls: Goodman, which helped Fritz and Lore Perls to theorize Gestalt therapy (mix of psychoanalysis and existentialism), takes patients. Session at one or two dollars; $1,000 earned in the year, in addition to his wife's secretary's salary; Decent poverty still possible at New York in 1951
Goodman doute de ses forces et entre dan: Goodman doubts his strength and enters a decade that he calls “a useless time” (unnecessary time); He challenged himself to have “une once de force en plus” and finished the fourth volume of The Empire City with no hope of finding a publisher. Personal challenge: “une once de force en plus”; Manuscript completed without publisher pressenti Consequences : Completion of The Empire City
À l'occasion de sa deuxième exposition,: On the occasion of his second exhibition, he declared that he had not felt ready for the exhibitions, that he was not particularly happy with it and that he was still working from doubt.
L'été 1951, M. C. Richards et la chorégr: In the summer of 1951, M. C. Richards and choreographer Katherine Litz revived the circus/round theatre events inherited from the Jennerjahn.
Partition tournante : lors de la composi: Rotating sheet music: during composition, Cage “pose des questions” on the characteristics of the partition, then launches coins or pulls traditional achilla sticks to assemble the hexagrams required by the I Ching; “réponses” determines duration, tempo and other compositional dynamics. He uses only the randomization structure, not the divinatory aspect. Coins of money, achille sticks, hexagrams of the I Ching (Book of Changes) Consequences: Turning in the compositional method of Cage, then applied to Theater Piece No. 1
Cage s'attend au silence total mais ente: Cage expects total silence but hears two sounds, one high and one low; the engineer explains to him that the top is his nervous system, the bottom his blood circulation. room without echo, soundproof Consequences : Cage places there the possibility to compose 4'33"
David Tudor arrive pour la première fois: David Tudor arrives for the first time at Black Mountain in 1951 as an accompaniment to the piano of the dancer Katherine Litz; It was also in the summer of 1952.
Fuller forge l'expression « Spaceship Ea: Fuller forged the expression “Spaceship Earth” in 1951; it will then appear on the cover of Operating Manual for Spaceship Earth (1963)
À l'automne, Excavation reçoit le prix d: In the fall, Excavation received the Logan purchase price at the Chicago Art Institute's Annual Exhibition. Purchase price Frank G. Logan Prize Fund Consequences: A little money and visibility for the group
Plus d'un quart de siècle après son arri: More than a quarter of a century after his arrival at the Bauhaus (circa 1951, i.e. “environ vingt-six ans” after 1922-1923), Anni wrote the story of his arrival and the welcome speech of Gropius to the new students. It evokes white clothes “vestaux”, baggy ups and tracks defrayed, touched “fait maison”; Gropius's speech lasted an hour; it compares with the opening speech of Gropius to Harvard the previous year, reported by young friends
Vénérant Gorky, Elaine écrit une analyse: Coming to Gorky, Elaine writes a superb analysis of his work and life; few critics had then searched with so much penetration the meaning of his painting and the dark and obscure aspects of his life. In her notes, she wrote in particular that Gorky, unlike Mondrian, loved the history of painting, saw Walt Disney, the coldness of lavender neon, the flashing tones of Technicolor, the tricolor lights, the neon signs — he could “voir les plantes pousser”. Notes to the article retained; sentence: “he could see plants grow”. Consequences: According to Elaine, Harold Rosenberg will draw the idea of the artist using his own life, one year before his article on Action Painters.
Un soir de printemps, l'autrice croise u: One spring evening, the author meets a young woman in black, black lace shawl on red-dorbed hair, huge eyes, bright white skin, bright red lips, walking fast without seeing her, carried to what was probably a party. black outfit, black lace shawl, golden red hair, red lips Consequences: the friend who accompanies him identifies him: “That must be Elaine de Kooning”
Fraîchement arrivée à New York, Elise As: Freshly arrived at New York, Elise Asher is crushed by both women: “si savantes, si fortes, si absolument sûres d'elles, si centrales” — she cannot say a word in front of them.
Le Whitney donne à Gorky une exposition: The Whitney gives Gorky a retrospective exhibition covering two decades of his work. Consequences: Despite Greenberg's praiseworthy article in The Nation, Gorky remains unacceptably accepted by the general public.
Peintre de cinquante-six ans, largement: Fifty-six-year-old painter, largely self-taught, graceful still lifes and serene classic figures; former commercial artist (theatrical signs from fourteen years old, “au temps de Mae Murray”), military press cartoonist during the First World War, posterist for Warner Brothers. Six-storey whale for Moby Dick repainted in zeppelin the following week; first patron Jules Mastbaum, founder of the Rodin Museum in Philadelphia, who paid for his first trip to Paris
Davis écrit qu'il divise tout art, passé: Davis writes that it divides all art, past and present, into two major categories: objective (absolute art, which sees the perception of the real world as an immediate event) and subjective (illustration by symbols and emotional detours). Davis formula on subjective art: “the character of a Universal Bellyache” and “a Perverse Passion for the Detour”.
Dix ans après l'achat, Graham propose le: Ten years after the purchase, Graham offered Bill the painting for five hundred dollars; Bill buys it back. $500 compared to $50 in 1940
Une dispute à la rétrospective conduit E: A retrospective dispute leads Elaine to recommend Porter to Thomas Hess for ARTnews; Porter writes to a friend that she told him about the quality of his texts and him about their mediocrity; he gets the critical position that Elaine held. Consequences: Porter takes the Elaine review niche when switching to background items
Avant de partir conduire jusqu'à Ashevil: Before driving to Asheville, Harrison asks for its Rock and Rye bottle; Williams runs, bleak that someone likes this syrupy liquor. Words: Harrison asks for a bottle of Rock and Rye; Williams comments on the disgusting sweetness of drinking. Atmosphere: Summer friendship, car Sunday, taste comice Issue: Little friendship ritual that sets a character
Quand une auto-révélation intense le sat: When he is satisfied with intense self-revelation, Olson slowly rises from his chair, dominates the author, shouts his enthusiasm and fixes the new elected one with a fierce affection. Victor, author of the “I finger my innards for the truth” line, becomes the workshop hero for the week, until the next raw metaphor. Words: “Si, Victor, si ! You have it, Victor !” Atmosphere: adoration, competition for the master's ear Issue: Making disciples; favour economy
Après lecture des nouvelles de Gray (per: After reading the news of Gray (old-aged alcoholic actor persona seeking salvation in a church in Bowery), Olson ton: pure shit; not to write anything other than a newspaper, one hour per day minimum, for a year; return the following summer. Yet he spares the public humiliation of these atrocious texts. Words: “Girl, this is pure shit! You're going to do nothing but keep a journal for a year, an hour a day minimum...” Atmosphere: Healthy violence of mentor Issue: Birth of a writer by destroying her models
Olson en serape sur le torse nu s'assoit: Olson will sit on the bare torso near Cage in black suit and tie; laconic conversation, punctuated by the zen laughter of Cage meditating on his next Happening Atmosphere: striking contrast of outfits; “laconisme cultivé” Issue: emblematic figure of the college: two aesthetics side by side
Déchargement d'une vieille Ford ; Rausch: Unloading an old Ford; Rauschenberg notes a pack of small sheets covered with zinc white; he holds one at the end of his arm and exclaims with enthusiasm that it is “vraiment une peinture intéressante”; the original forms guess under the white Words: “What's this! … This is really an interesting painting.” (“Qu'est-ce que c'est ! … C'est vraiment une peinture intéressante.”) Atmosphere: Immediate enthusiasm of the painter, perplexity of the arrival who saw there only material to recycle Issue: The accident of recovery becomes art: Inaugural lesson for the newcomer
Assis sur les marches, Twombly aide Raus: Sitting on the steps, Twombly helps Rauschenberg to brush white a series of tense canvases Atmosphere: Quiet work in the open air, a few days after the arrival of the witness Issue: Birth of the future White Paintings in front of a witness who doesn't know yet
La soirée de cours va de 19 h à 23 h ; t: La class night runs from 7pm to 11pm; everyone goes to Ma Peak's tavern charging in beer; return to college for a session that lasts all night and the following day; Then back to Peak's the second night Atmosphere: exuberance, beer, inexhaustible speech Issue: teaching Olson as a collective fever
Wes lit à voix haute toute l'adaptation,: Wes reads aloud all adaptation, “gamely”; he and Duck exchange gazes of compassionate tolerance in front of a transcription without dramaturgy Atmosphere: Room scattered around the large table; Lesson received with gentleness Issue: Apprentice writer failure, before teaching Olson
Pollock se saoule, hurle, frôle la viole: Pollock gets drunk, screams, approaches violence; Lee thinks him like a child in crisis until the stupor; Then she shows the works to Hartigan and sells her husband as a genius; Pollock, loosened by alcohol, says there are only two guys in town: Pollock and Kooning, and sends Hartigan to see the Egan exhibition. Words: Pollock: “There are only two guys in town… Pollock and de Kooning”; “Tell him I sent you.” Atmosphere: Deaf violence and maternal appeasement; the admiration of the young painter. Issue: Transmission of the torch and seed of rivalry.
Hartigan frappe à la porte ; Bill sort l: Hartigan knocks on the door; Bill pulls his head out of the window (“Who's dat?” “Come on up, den”); They look at the canvases, Bill says good of Jackson; Elaine arises, flirts with Bill, asks him for money for a coat, he objects that he has already given him, she has spent everything; Hartigan leaves without knowing how the crisis resolves. Words: Bill: “Yah, Jackson is something”; exchange on the coat money. Atmosphere: Charmer, accomplice, suddenly domestic and embarrassed. Issue: Portrait of the Kooning couple and the place of Elaine.
L'enfant, ayant appris « toutou » et éta: The child, having learned “toutou” and being rewarded for this word, applies it to any quadruped; to designate a horse to his mother he exclaims that he sees a big toy; it corrects and shows it the distinctive features; he gradually acquires a precise vocabulary for everything that strikes simultaneously his exteroceptors and those of the tutor. Words: “Oh maman, regarde le gros toutou !” — “Non chéri, c'est un cheval.” Issue: How is the accuracy of public language born — and why private language cannot be born like this.
Marchant avec sa mère sur un trottoir br: Walking with his mother on a burning sidewalk, the child says he prefers shadows, in a metaphor that the convention has not yet emasculated. Words: “I like the shadows better. The sun makes a noise in my stomach.” Atmosphere: Crushing heat, sought-after shadows, child's voice free of cliché. Issue: La child perception before conventional language.
Des électrodes collées au front suivent: Electrodes glued to the forehead follow the potentials of the frontal muscle; The tone drops, the proprioception passes below the critical threshold, sleep comes; The relay starts, the buzzer buzzes, the man jumps and wakes up — he woke up sleeping. Issue: External control of the body up to the threshold of sleep.
Premier essai (~15 minutes) interrompu p: First test (~15 minutes) interrupted by increasing impatience; the word “now” gives the feeling of immediacy, accompanied by fear (deep breathing, breast constriction); he suddenly sees objects that he only touched from his eyes, feels a desire to store, “se tiennent autour de lui” objects without continuity with him; Second essay: same fear, tendency to qualify objects as adjectives instead of experiencing the act of observing; Third try on the metro: less fear because of others, vision “multipliée par cent”, great fun, then fun but expensive energy game. Words : Report written by the student, reported at length by the authors Atmosphere: Isolation of the room, objects seen as for the first time; métro crowd that soothes and stimulates Issue: La afraid to be really alive and present
On renonce à la lecture habituelle ; on: We renounce the usual reading; We look around and we say to each other: the train swings, people go out, this man looks at me, I care about the effect I make. Words: “At this moment I am riding in the subway. Now the train is swaying…” Atmosphere: Rhythm rocking the car, anonymous crowd Issue: Maintain contact with here-now
Après l'exercice d'inversion, un étudian: After the inversion exercise, a student writes that after years of informed opinions where he felt “âme perdue”, he finally forged opinions through experience and preferred to be rigid rather than amibe; the accuracy of a decision counts more than a chronic state of analysis; One cannot deviate too publicly from the consensus without ending up in a state hospital. Words: He concludes that there is a limit to the odd behavior that you can afford “avant de se retrouver interné”. Atmosphere: Defensive, ironic; The fear of the asylum comes out. Issue: La resistance to exercise accurately reveals the inner conflict the exercise was seeking.
Inverser les letres (« p » en « q ») tro: Reverse lettering (“p” in “q”) troubles this student as much as seeing someone open a box of cans or cigarettes upside down; it cannot fall asleep if a drawer is opened or the door of the closet is not closed. Words: “Les choses doivent être précisément comme elles doivent être — c'est-à-dire la bonne façon.” Atmosphere: Malaise obsessive, need order. Issue: Exercise affects the neurotic node of order.
En essayant d'imaginer des mots retourné: Trying to imagine words turned around, the student becomes nervous: heart that gets bogged down, eyes that wash; She then tries to write the letters backwards, but the eyes burn to the point that she can no longer look. Words: “C'est fou ! Qu'est-ce que vous nous faites avec ces expériences ?” Atmosphere: Actual physiological angosis: tachycardia, tears. Issue: The harmless visual exercise triggers a body reaction of panic — proof that the “résistant” is there.
Sa fiancée revient d'Europe après près d: His fiancée returns from Europe after almost nine months; They're getting married and he's “ne tient plus en place”. He is asked to imagine opposing wishes: he writes not wanting to return, not loving him, preferring to run other girls for a few more years — and recognizes “un peu de vérité” in this last point. He then became angry with the authors, attacked their algebraic exposure from scratch, then, his aggression expressed directly, concedes that his objections were perhaps very personal. Words: He blames: the truth of a situation is spread throughout the continuum, one side is not all positive or all negative. Atmosphere: Official euphoria, then disappointed, aggressive, finally appeased. Issue: Exercise brings out a rejected truth; Anger against the experimenter is the logical continuation of the insight.
Il attend avec impatience l'enfant que s: He looks forward to the child that he and his wife have planned; invited to imagine not supporting this perspective, he lists with an ease that surprises him: loss of liberty, awakenings in the middle of the night, medical expenses and other disadvantages. Words: He concludes: “Il n'y a pas de crédits sans débits.” Atmosphere: Lucid Eagerness, self-surprise. Issue: Anticipate the flow of expected happiness.
Une étudiante inverse des situations où: A student in reverse of situations where she got mad at people. Words: “Certaines m'ont fait rire aux éclats. Il y avait un soulagement, comme si j'en avais fini avec elles.” Atmosphere: Release, laugh, discharge. Issue: Inversion as the completion of a blocked emotion.
Elles suggèrent tour à tour des situatio: They alternately suggest situations to be reversed and everything goes well, until the mother proposes to reverse the mother-daughter relationship; The student's imagination is completely silent: the mother suggests the mother-daughter inversion; the student: 'my imagination dried up completely' Atmosphere: complicit game then sudden cut Issue: show the border where imagination touches the family taboo
Elle imagine être une serveuse attablée: She imagines being a waitress while a client serves her; Although aware of the unreality, she feels the muscles of her legs tender to inhibit the desire to rise and correct the situation Words: her account of the muscle tension of her legs Atmosphere: body that reacts to fiction Issue: imagination alive enough to trigger motor behavior
En attendant quelqu'un ou un bus, laisse: While waiting for someone or a bus, let each other freely see each other and agree figures and backgrounds, then, without forcing, let themselves be invaded by the feeling of chaos meaningless of the environment and note the resistances Words: 'I am now impatient' — I am now impatient Atmosphere: rising anxiety of the expectation, environment that is untied Issue: converting sterile impatience into creative pre-engagement in the real situation
Ne réussissant pas à verbaliser émotions: Not succeeding in verbalizing emotions and tastes in front of inert objects, she begins to attribute to them emotions at random; These are gradually becoming real, to the point that they almost forget their arbitrary character. Words: “It sort of scared me to see how easily I could fool myself”, it scared me a bit to see how easy I could be wrong myself. Atmosphere: Initial doubt about neutral objects; then a lucid concern. Issue: La fragile boundary between feigned emotion and true emotion.
L'étudiant fait l'exercice de différenci: The student performs the exercise of emotional differentiation in a crowded metro and discovers considerable aggression towards other passengers; Instead of being ashamed of it, he enjoys it and wishes to tell them what he thinks of them; Later, in a less irritating setting, he reviewed the scene and then experienced the blocked (honest, desire to dilute) expected but absent at the moment. Words: He had rather enjoyed this aggressiveness. Atmosphere: Encumbrance, irritation, then fresher retrospection. Issue: True emotion arises when it can; shame comes after all.
Assis près de son beau-père avec qui il: Sitting near his stepfather with whom he is always in excellent terms, the man verbalizes “je l'aime” and feels a vague anxiety, “je déteste quelque chose dans cette figure”; He interrupts the experience, then understands that it is a reaction of fear, nourished by the accounts of his wife and sister-in-law about the paternal hardness of their childhood — a fear “sans rien de concret”. Words: Anxiety put into words: “je déteste quelque chose dans cette figure”. Atmosphere: Frontal disorder, underground anxiety. Issue: The emotion inherited by yes-saying against the real relationship.
Le mari exige qu'elle l'écoute quand il: The husband demands that she listens to him when he develops a theory, even when the children simmer something potentially serious; torn between the pride of responding intelligently and the protection of children, she felt anger and frustration, then the conflict became intolerable and resolved by the postponement of her attention to children. Words: La “chaos of divided attention”, chaos of divided attention. Atmosphere: Domestic tension, pulling. Issue: The impossible choice between theoretic husband and children at risk.
Toujours un peu méprisant de la fierté d: Always a little disrespectful of the property pride of his friend — Cadillac possessed and cherished for more than a year, in which he has often driven — the man focuses his attention on the car and for the first time really notices the beautiful lines, curves and functional abilities; he gets an unexpected aesthetic emotion, and his pleasure is overtaken by that of the friend when he sincerely and spontaneously compliments the beauty of the car. Words: “A small incident, perhaps” — a small incident, perhaps, but indicative of the new areas of experience that the real consciousness opens. Atmosphere: Initial mischief melted into admiration; shared pleasure. Issue: Ceder to an admiration that was rejected in principle.
Allongé sur un canapé, le sujet énonce c: Lying on a sofa, the subject states every awareness: he is lying down, he wants to experience, he hesitates on what to start, the radio plays in the neighbouring room — it reminds him of the program he wanted to listen to — he gets back, feels lost, remembers the advice to stay on the surface, feels his legs crossed, a pain in the back, the desire to change position, then changes position Words: “Now I am aware that I am lying on the couch… the radio is playing in the next room.” — “Maintenant je prends conscience que je suis couché sur le canapé… que la radio joue dans la pièce voisine.” Atmosphere: Fluid interiority, interruptions, self-resumption Issue: Show the method in action, with his failures
Assis dans un train, un sujet explore se: Sitting on a train, a subject explores his internal sensations, reaches the rectum region and discovers his tight muscles to the maximum, without wanting to go to the saddle — “comme s'il retenait son souffle avec le bas du colon”; it also finds a tension band at the navel; Since then, he mechanically checks this tension by walking, standing, elongating, and always finds it, wondering if its concentration does not create it Words: The subject judges this tension “sotte” and wonders: how do I know if it is not my concentration that calls it? Atmosphere: Intimate amazement, embarrassed curiosity Issue: The body reveals what the will did not know
Pendant l'expérience, un homme se découv: During the experiment, a man suddenly finds himself unemployed for his arms: he crosses them clumsyly on his chest, puts them in his pockets, feels uncomfortable, crooked, feels confused, rises almost immediately and walks; his wife calls him for dinner and he is happy to give up the Atmosphere experience: Growing boredom, relieved escape Issue: La resistance disguised as agitation; domestic life as a way out
Après trois semaines sans résultat, un s: After three weeks without results, a subject suddenly becomes aware of his muscular tensions and feels “une masse de muscles noués” — hollow kidneys, back of neck, upper legs; His mind sets itself on a little irritation until it darkens all the rest of the body; he concludes that resistances and tensions are one and the same thing, understands verbally his tension without being able to release it Words: “I was a mass of knotted muscle” — “j'étais une masse de muscles noués” Atmosphere: Fear and fascination Issue: The threshold where the body turns out to be foreign
Pendant l'expérience de conscience corpo: During the experience of body consciousness, he does not know what to do with his arms, crosses them on his chest, puts them in his pockets, twists, feels confused, rises, walks in the room; His wife calls him for dinner and he's relieved to give up. Words: “I am glad to leave the experiment” — I'm happy to leave the experience. Atmosphere: Domestic malaise, febrile agitation, escape relief. Issue: The body reveals a desire that consciousness refuses to see.
Pendant l'exercice, ses pensées s'arrête: During the exercise, his thoughts stop, he tightens his fists, his chest swells as if to scream something he cannot identify; A month later, he sent a real warning to the overinterventionist parents of his fiancée. Atmosphere: Silence and delayed release. Issue: The blocked emotion finds its real address in life.
En relisant ses notes avant de les taper: By rereading his notes before typing them, the subject feels his stiff neck, his lower lip strained and his heavy breathing — the pattern of resentment restraint; At the very moment when he smiled widely, he realized that he felt exploited and martyred to have to do these experiments, and that his anger against the experimenter had finally arrived. Words: “The resentment toward you had finally arrived!” Atmosphere: Discovery both comic and liberating; Since then, the exercise leaves him refreshed and gathered. Issue: The transfer of anger on the experienced master finally confesses.
Lors de l'expérience sur les habitudes,: During the experience of habits, a man finds that he can only innovate in his behaviour at the cost of feeling very “malchanceux”; He hides his superstition, and discovers that he is mad at anyone who forces him to take another path. Words: He confesses that by following the path of the other he feels miserable, furious against himself, and realizes only now that he resents the other and finds that this one owes him a lot. Atmosphere: Astonished confession tone, hot discovery. Issue: The moment you see your own secret mechanics for the first time.
Un homme regarde sa femme repasser l'une: A man watches his wife iron one of his shirts with a care he does not have; His system favored speed, and he became irritated as if he himself pushed iron faster. Words: He said he felt “tendre” pushing iron, annoyed by its slowness. Atmosphere: Domestic, microscopic, revealing. Issue: La confluence between two styles of doing, even in a tiny gesture.
Un sujet est contraint de fermer les por: One subject is forced to close the doors that others leave open; If he tries to ignore an open door, he sits in anguish until it is closed. Words: He says getting up to close the door is less uncomfortable than waiting for someone else to do it. Atmosphere: Deaf tension, physical discomfort. Issue: La compulsion that governs the most common gestures.
Un homme décrit une vie entière réduite: A man describes an entire life reduced into systems of habit — combing before shaving so that moisture does not flow on the talc — to save time for the “sérieux” of thought; He has eliminated certain rituals, but changing even an effective habit creates anxiety, and he cannot help coaching anyone else. Words: He jokes about his “surmoi” that bothers his “moi” until “nous” does something. Atmosphere: Lucid irony on oneself. Issue: The intellectual who systematizes his life and monitors that of others.
Un étudiant isolé, incapable de lier con: An isolated student, unable to link contact with his dormitory comrades, hears from his room others being called out by their friends; One night we discover it under his own window, calling his own name repeatedly Words: He is called himself as someone outside the Atmosphere: Night, pathetic loneliness tinted with absurdity Issue: Perfect image of retroflexion: giving oneself what we wanted to receive from others
Au moment où le patient devrait formuler: When the patient should make a complaint, he feels the attack, dare not, turn it against himself, feel injured and burst into sobbing — sometimes several times in a session. Words: Tears seem to say: “voyez comme je suis inoffensif et maltraité”. Atmosphere: Wet heat of repeated crises, chronic resentment. Issue: The aggression cannot be reorganized outwards as long as the circuit remains closed on itself.
Tapant son compte rendu, elle ressent un: Typeing her report, she feels a nervous irritation that leaves her legs and wins the whole body; She scratches, hammers the keys, her left arm stiffens to the bone; a letter from his parents tie his throat; She admits to crying easily before a film but never in her personal relationships; Aggression returns, pain in the left arm returns Words: “Dans une vie on joue beaucoup de rôles. Lequel est le vrai qui représente le soi ?”; she refuses to agree “le luxe de pleurer” Atmosphere: Martelated typewriter, body tearing apart, anger and tears retained Issue: Unsolved conflict with parents who do not accept her way of life; guilt of returning home refused
Allongé, il prend contact avec son corps: Lying, he gets in touch with his body, breathes deeply, feels excitement ascending and retreating; he restrains his breathing, so he deliberately haletes: the excitement crosses him in bowls of electricity, the body twists in all directions, burning, sweating, tears, shouting “Ohh...” for several minutes; Then he looks at his hands to see if they're grilled; shivering for half an hour, feeling strong Words: “J'ai regardé mes mains pour voir si elles étaient brûlées. Je n'aurais pas été surpris de le trouver.” Atmosphere: Heat of fire, hands and feet blazing, sobs and rales Issue: La promise and fear that these experiences will release; “la phase de lune de miel ne durera peut-être pas”
Lassitude envers le « simili-crime surco: Wearyness towards the “simili-crime surcoté”: he declares not to be disturbed by any of his impulses, not to fear his desire for murder, to cry loudly but to spare the neighbors, then accuses himself: “je suis sans doute une personnalité psychopathique — j'ai volé des voitures, pris de la drogue, vécu avec des femmes. Essayez de le prouver !” Words: “Je n'ai honte de rien — absolument rien — à mon sujet.” Atmosphere: Provocation, challenge narquois Issue: La resistance under cover of total transparency
seul à la maison pour une fois, il pouss: alone at home for once, he pushes the table, first lie down dressed — embarrassed — then undresses entirely on a blanket; rapid soothing breathing; erection he involuntarily seeks to refresh, back pain immediately — “je commence à mettre deux et deux ensemble”; comparison of both sides: right shoulder raised, weight on shoulder and left buttocks; irresistible urge to stretch, then “pont” wrestler on feet and neck; Back to the ground, strange relief, lumbar hollow closer to the floor Words: this old man acquired: this pain “is an old acquaintance”; general sense: “je ne me sens plus aussi confus” Atmosphere: excitement, intimacy, discovery Issue: the body reveals the link between sexual defense and chronic pain
allongée, elle prend conscience de sa ho: lying down, she becomes aware of her shame of her genitals and the strong desire to cover herself with her hand; memory of her mother: “nice girls never expose themselves”; education on moral virtue, warnings and sermons; It concludes with many “unfinished business” but a good start Words: The Mother: “les filles bien ne s'exposent jamais” Atmosphere: shame, lucidity, emerging Issue: conflict between natural desire and prohibitions implanted in childhood
le père le reprend vertement alors qu'il: the father takes him greenly while he knows himself in his right; jaws and throat tied, screamed; He feels that he must not hurt his father — and that is precisely what he does when he moves after the blow; Resolution: Next time, say his Words fact: the father demands what the “ronge”; the son can't let anything out of it Atmosphere: tension contained Issue: moving from injuring silence to direct speech
tension du diaphragme, envie subtile de: Diaphragm tension, subtle urge to vomit, convulsive hiccups; hands are almost spontaneously tightened, the head shakes “non”, the word comes out strong and charged with emotion; he goes so far as to strangle the pillow and sees intimate visual images that he refuses to describe; The tensions of the diaphragm no longer return Words: “no” said aloud, “quite loudly and with much emotion” Atmosphere: Cathartic discharge Issue: the body succeeds what the word dared not
