Pendant une expérience de tension muscul: During an experience of muscle tension, pain in the arm spreads throughout the body; the man trembles with fear, wants to reach out to someone — his mother — and remembers, at four years old, a journey where his mother threatened to abandon him to the manager of the hotel; He runs to her crying, arms stretched; She consoles him by swearing she was joking, while the manager laughs and calls him 'mama's baby'. Words: La mother: If you don't stand well, I'll leave you to the manager. The manager: 'mama's baby' ('ma's baby') Atmosphere: Persistent pain in the arm during the strike of the report; memory rising 'as if it were yesterday'; the experimenter himself says skeptical: 'All this may be cooked up' Issue: Body as archive: a physical pain of today restores a decades-old scene never recalled since
Lors d'une expérience de tension muscula: During an experience of muscle tension, the muscles of the corner of the mouth twist upwards; ten minutes during he believes in a smile, then understands that it is the prelude to a tears crisis; he is crying, for the first time since childhood; embarrassment interrupts the process; he connects the episode to the death of his mother two years earlier, where he had wanted to cry without power Atmosphere: Happily faced with his own behavior; then, after the experience, feeling well-being and 'extreme joy' for making this action available Issue: The tears contained at the mother's funeral are released by a simple facial twitch two years later
L'étudiant, goberge notoire et lecteur à: The student, a well-known goblet and table reader, observes that he bit partially and then rips out the rest; Focus on the bite sending her to dream and the bite is swallowed before he realizes it. He chews, chews: the tongue hurts him in the back, he lacks air, holds his breath, has to push back the food on the sides, make empty swallowing movements, breathe thoroughly, and then take back the rest. At the end of two bites, the taste becomes detestable, it deliberately desensitizes itself, feels a strong desire to vomit, tipping into the dreamery, saying that one must not spoil an entire meal — and stops, twice. Words: It says: “Ne gâchons pas un repas entier en tombant malade ; il y a une limite.” He notes that it's “évidemment une résistance”. Atmosphere: Mouth in disorder, sore tongue, breath cut, rising nausea, stupor of dreaming as a leak Issue: The body defends itself against the experience that would free it; resistance triumph, lucidly seen
Elle essaie une robe vue dans Vogue ou H: She tries a dress seen in Vogue or Harper's Bazaar; the mirror does not return its long, supple and blond ideal; furious and disgusted with herself, she swears to make a diet; Then, feeling sorry for herself, she sits down and eats candy or a piece of cake. Atmosphere: Circle of self-hate and sweet consolation Issue: The introject of the ideal silhouette ingested since magazines dominates its relationship to food
L'étudiant, étendu sur sol et banc, cher: The student, lying on the floor and bench, looks for what introjects he is wearing: he thinks about tolerance, then “How I hate her!” comes up — tight fists, contracted biceps, compressed lips, tight teeth, frowned eyebrows, pulsating temples, ears stretched back, the whole body pressing the floor and bench; tension and heartburn rise to nausea; then comes the name “Aunt Agnes” and all tensions disappear, remaining only a few minutes acid taste. Words: “How I hate her!” then “Aunt Agnes!” — spoken words with a violent insistence Atmosphere: concentrated muscle violence, inner burn, then sudden relaxation Issue: the ejection of an introject embodied by an authoritarian aunt, male, who was in charge at three years of age
Les expériences alimentaires ramènent sa: Food experiments constantly bring the father back to the mind of the student: a dominating man who wants to prevent his children from growing up, for whom “être parent” is his work more than his profession and of which he never intends to retire. The student starts with “vomir” the deep-seated ideas, discovering how many views his father took for himself; He feels immense relief from it. Words: He says analyzing the fatherly ideas “en termes de vues sociales et morales d'aujourd'hui” and feeling “a tremendous relief in sloughing off some of them” Issue: the disassimilation of an introjected father
Cherchant les introjects logés en lui co: Seeking the introjects housed in him like foreign bodies, the subject re-thinks the work on confluence (traits, speech, hold imities of whom?), comes to the problem of tolerance. Then comes “How I hate her!” — the words “je” and “elle” hammered, tight fists, contracted biceps, compressed lips, tight teeth, frowned eyebrows, swinging temples, ears stretched back, the whole body crushed against the ground and bench. Simultaneously, stomach tension and mild burn worsen until nausea. Then come the words “Aunt Agnes!” — and all tensions, burns, pressures, and pulses disappear; only remains, for a few minutes, an acidic taste in the mouth. Words: “How I hate her!” then “Aunt Agnes!” Atmosphere: Growing somatic violence, nausea, and then instant release Issue: A childhood hatred swallowed twenty years earlier returned to the body and named: the past dislodged by a character trait
Exemple construit : on mange un steak ;: Example built: one eats a steak; If one thinks that it looks like last week's, it raises disgust; What's interesting is that he's steak in general and he's getting his own new smell. Atmosphere: didactic, sensory Issue: illustrating the difference between neurotic repetition and healthy appetite oriented towards novelty
Un homme est frappé par un visage de pas: A man is struck by a passing face; suddenly he experiences an emotion “étrangère”, a strange attraction, an unnamed grief — immediately stopped by the present inhibition that continues. Atmosphere: brief, vertigo, cut Issue: show that an image first arrived, without relaxation of inhibition, remains empty and evanescent
Le patient « puissant » achevant un exer: The “puissant” patient completing an exercise becomes anxious when getting something out of it; When asked about his self-problem, he admits that he wants to bite the therapist; He then accuses the therapist of exploiting the session, admits to wanting to be admired by him, disgusts himself of boring experiences and silent; in silence he feels his jaw crunched and painful, remembers that his voice passed between his teeth, clasps them, then smiles seeing his own dependence; As he goes up the chain, he thinks about other women, blames his education, recognizes his mother's censorous face, ironically concludes that “ce que les gens ne savent pas ne peut pas leur nuire”, and decides to re-experience. Words: “Au lieu de vous reprocher, qui voudriez-vous reprocher ?”; “Suis-je vraiment attirant pour vous ?”; “Qui est en train de jouer à un jeu ?” Atmosphere: Increasing tension, therapist silence, tight jaw, anger and final smile. Issue: Show step-by-step dissolution of defence layers until contact is recovered.
Chaet arrive de Boston, toiles sous le b: Chaet arrives from Boston, canvases under the arm on instruction from Albers; Albers examines the paintings and makes them a remarkable criticism; He insists on how Chaet would teach; After an hour and a half, he hires him immediately Words: Albers: “bring the paintings”; then about the criticism: “je n'avais jamais entendu parler ainsi” (Chaet); “no committees” Atmosphere: Direct, without intermediary, dazzling for the young painter Issue: The absolute power of Albers and its way of exercising it
Œuvre mariant un poème d'Oppenheimer à u: Work marrying a poem from Oppenheimer with an ink drawing from Rauschenberg, commemorating a dance of Katherine Litz given to New York.
Rauschenberg sort la toile encore mouill: Rauschenberg pulls out the still wet canvas, the layer on the floor outside, treats it like an adhesive surface or a sensitive photo paper: dust, earth and gravel attach to it, black on black. Atmosphere : Tactile, nocturnal (Night Blooming), painter-photographer's gesture Issue : Invention of the gesture that will lead from Black Paintings to combinating paints
Un étudiant jaloux demande à Tworkov pou: A jealous student asks Tworkov why he spends so much time with Bob, who never comes to class. Words: Tworkov: “Quand ils cessent de venir en cours, alors ça m'intéresse.” Atmosphere: Benevolent irony Issue: What the college does with students who don't go
Litz bondit sur scène en faisant flotter: Litz jumps on stage by floating the top of its tube dress; It disappears and reappears six times behind the panel, galloping, rotating, dragging, crawling; a mermaid becomes a tree, then a stone sculpture, then an animal; bells sound out of sync, piano notes drag after his disappearance. Atmosphere: mimic humour, precision, percussive variations Issue: Reinventing the body as a living glyph
Asawa explique le Paper Fold d'Albers ;: Asawa explains Albers Paper Fold; Renk performs the exercises, learns the rules of folding, then persists two days and two nights to draw and fold a shape of eggboard. Words: Renk, remembering the school: “je n'ai trouvé ni enfant ni solutions”; after Asawa: “j'avais appris les règles de base du pliage”. Atmosphere: Joyful obsession, night of work. Issue: La transmission of Albers pedagogy from artist to artist.
Rauschenberg colle les feuilles de papie: Rauschenberg glues the sheets of paper into a long ribbon and spreads it on the floor of Fulton Street; coating a section of the carriageway with ink; Cage, at the wheel of its Ford model A, goes into ink and then rolls straight on the paper only making sure not to get out of it; the tire trace is printed throughout the length. Words: Rauschenberg in interview: Cage was there “parce qu'il était le seul à avoir une voiture”; “Il devait seulement rester sur le papier. Il a fait un travail excellent” Atmosphere: New York Street, Black Ink, Ford Model A Engine, Public Experience and Burlesque Issue: Making Organized Chance and Direct Trace Art Matter
Exposition accueillie froidement, aucune: Coldly received exhibition, no sale, cold and rare criticism; One visitor counts: John Cage, avant-garde composer Words: Stuart Preston (New York Times): “stylish doodles in black and white” (sleek black and white scribbles) Atmosphere: public failure, seed of decisive friendship Issue: failure as an encounter
Cage se trouve devant les toiles blanche: Cage stands in front of the white canvases of Rauschenberg and has a competitive injunction: he must write his silent piece, otherwise the music is late on the painting. Words: “Oh yes, I must—otherwise I'm lagging, otherwise music's lagging” — “Oh oui, il le faut, sinon je suis en retard, sinon la musique est en retard” Atmosphere: Friendly Emulation Frissoon Under Zen Calm Issue: Alleged Birth of 4'33"
Olson et le jeune neveu de la cuisinière: Olson and the young nephew of the cook fall on a local auction; the child exclaims “It's like a race”; captured by the echo of slave sales, Olson writes an immediate poem, dedicates it to Alvin and Shahn, offering it to Ben Shahn. Words: “It's like a race” Atmosphere: Soudaine, uncomfortable, revealing Issue: The word race, between race and racial category, in the segregated South
Les deux jeunes, debout sur le patio, re: The two young people, standing on the patio, look at a large canvas covered with tar; they throw in handles of stones; Motherwell, between them, gesture and says “More”; they throw again; “More”; they throw again; “More”. Words: Motherwell: “More.” — repeated three times Atmosphere: Educational ritual before the eyes of the older painter; gesture rather than speech Issue: Transmission of creative gesture — accident, material, action are doctrine
Doutant de ses forces, Goodman entre dan: Doubtful of his strength, Goodman enters a decade of purgatory (“a useless time”); he challenged himself to have “une once de force en plus” and finished the fourth volume of The Empire City without any hope of publisher; In the novel, his hero loses courage, becomes momentarily mad of conformity, then heals and ends “spoiling for a fight” — seeking a fight he does not know. Words: the hero “ne sait quel combat ni comment y entrer”; Goodman knew that his own duel would be with the Incarnate Organized System, out of Atmosphere fiction: dark then combative; lucidity about impotence Issue: the transition from Romanesque abstraction to real social confrontation
Un soir de printemps, l'autrice voit ven: One spring evening, the author sees a woman coming to her in black, lace shawl on red hair, walking fast, eyes lit by the destination, crossing the street without seeing her; the author, new in the middle, fixed; His friend identifies him. Words: Friend: “That must be Elaine de Kooning” — “Ce doit être Elaine de Kooning”. Atmosphere: Energy, haste, joyful greed; the city as an adventure (probably a party where to dance, drink, laugh). Issue: Mythification of Elaine: Even unknown, it radiates.
Un reporter du journal étudiant de Yale: A reporter of Yale's student newspaper notes that the majority of students produce non-objective abstractions, a dramatic change from the surrealist paintings two or three years ago, attributed to the reorganization of the courses by Albers.
Olson part au Yucatan avec sa femme Cons: Olson goes to Yucatan with his wife Constance, hoping to decipher the Mayan hieroglyphs; he wrote visionary letters to Creeley that became Mayan Letters. the title “Mayan Letters” is a word game on maya glyphs Consequences: The letters constitute his most complete statement on his draft
Dix-sept lettres adressées à Robert Cree: Seventeen letters to Robert Creeley, dated from February 18 to July 1, 1951, mixing lyrical anecdotes (the wounded seabird), reports from snake-infested fields, anthropological speculation and literary strategy. 17 letters; Creeley is only called “lad”; the letter of March 17 begins with “christamiexcited”; the “f” key on his typewriter breaks and triggers a series of swears leading to “fuck it” Consequences: Published by Various Press, Majorca, 1953
Depuis la fenêtre d'un bus de troisième: From the third-class bus window on the coastal road, Olson makes a discovery (“christamiexcited”); he and Constance come back with sacks of teeth, little heads and feet; The next day, alone, further south, he dug up his first hieroglyphic stone. Sherds & little heads & feet bags; Third class bus; letter of 20 March 1951

From the third-class bus window, Olson finds something; he and Constance come back with bags of tesses and small heads and feet; the next day, alone, growing further south, he dug up his first hieroglyphic stone; interrupting a letter to Creeley, he writes that his nerves are too tense towards the ruins. Words: “christamiexcited”; “I am wild for it”; “Christ, these hieroglyphs… Is, in fact, verse. Is their verse.” Atmosphere: Fever, excitement, dust from excavations Issue: The poet is archaeologist to prove that an imaginative jump can defeat where the academy fails
Au printemps 1951, les derniers membres: In the spring of 1951, the last members of the Conservative group withdrew; Duberman argues that the college then becomes for the first time a resolutely American and resolutely radical environment. Consequences: Transition to the American Radical Age of the College
Le matin, après le petit-déjeuner, Conni: In the morning, after breakfast, Connie shows visitors to the campus: rusty venom kits along the road, the library, the Studies Building with its individual work rooms, the sun terrace, the painting workshop and the studios. Never open snake kits, rust spots; “il y a des crotales et des copperheads, mais ils s'occupent de leurs affaires”; mist that dissipates from the peaks; increasing wet heat; ~100 work practices for a capacity of 99 students; three-level concrete building. Consequences: Rumaker is starting to feel good in college.
Grande salle blanche et fraîche au sol g: Large white and fresh room on the grey floor, without finished painting: canvases of various sizes serving pallets, barbulated with oil paint, turpentine essence and flax oil. Connie refers to a small canvas in a corner as a painting she loves; Rumaker takes it for a brush cloth. Phyllis Franklin enters through the back doors; fixes his canvas with an intensity that surprises Rumaker. Colour-stained canvases, dribblings, smudges; runoff of a mountain torrent against the windows on the shadow side; the Eye and the Stables, two long white buildings as painters' studios. Consequences: First lesson from Rumaker to Black Mountain: before what he does not understand, keep quiet and open his eyes; decision to come back at all costs.
Marche jusqu'au lodge Roadside sous les: Walks to the Roadside lodge under the pine trees: Roger and Rumaker on the first floor, Marge and Mary Ann on the second (gender separation for shape, ironic because Mary Ann is the only non-gay in the group). Presentation to students under the pine trees, including Mark Hedden, a Westport anthropology student, Connecticut, who later played a major role in the life of Rumaker. Unpainted pine rooms, sour-smell mattresses, old drawer chests, right-back canned chairs; smell of moisture and mould; Dry pine needle mats; wooden bridge on a deep ravine; Streamside cottage, faculty residence; college farm beyond the creek; Mary Fitton Fiore will later say that the area has the highest rainfall in the region and that the Seven Sisters deprive many of the sun's pieces.
Le samedi, Marge conduit le groupe à Ash: On Saturday, Marge led the group to Asheville to visit Thomas Wolfe's boarding house, set by Look Homeward, Angel, preserved as it was since his mother's death, then Riverside Cemetery where Wolfe has been buried since 1938. Rumaker and Mary Ann, Wolfe's devourers, are in secret fervency; Roger ricane; Marge's bored. Large porch, high-back rocking chairs, room where Ben died of pneumonia, writing Wolfe's father spider around the old phone; Registration: “Tom, son of W. O. and Julia E. Wolfe… A Beloved American Author… 'The last voyage, the longest, the best…'”; Pack Library where Wolfe child read everything; Marge in short sleeve sports shirt. Consequences: Strengthens the vocation of Rumaker writer.
Première apparition de Charles Olson, qu: First appearance of Charles Olson, which Rumaker was waiting for since the Ben Shahn conference in Philadelphia. Saturday evening roast chicken (traditional), prepared by Malrey and Cornelia cooks with the help of students. Olson and Harrison dominate the conversation of conspiracies; Olson makes Rumaker and Mary Ann feel that they are very special people. A dozen tables on the long porch; Dressing evening: Lou Harrison in glittering vanilla-colored ice suit with thick dark brown taste; Connie in sober blue blouse, denim skirt, loose knit shawl, Greek sandals with fine straps; Olson: almost 2m10, long brown searsucker jacket, blue loose work shirt, deformed tie, chino work pants, high-stem work boots, horn-ringed glasses. Consequences: Rumaker is conquered; Olson awakens in him the desire to be there and to be near him.
Après le dîner, Olson emmène Mary Ann et: After dinner, Olson takes Mary Ann and Rumaker to his old blue convertible Ford, probably looking for something in a pharmacy for their daughter Kate (born eight months earlier) and maybe an ice cream in a drive-in he loves. Olson drives fast, a large hand placed on the steering wheel, speaking over his shoulder; Rumaker, silent, is bewitched by the full moon on the valley. Leather driver seat pushed away from the steering wheel by the weight of Olson; down condom; wind in the ears; huge moon and close as ever seen; 12 miles to Asheville. Consequences: La “reddition” from Rumaker to college is complete.
Samedi après-midi, mal à l'aise ou décid: Saturday afternoon, uncomfortable or deciding that the place is not for them, Marge and Roger leave in the Chevy de Marge to see local curiosities and only return on Sunday, the day of the scheduled departure. Consequences: They leave college after the weekend; Roger to Rider for graduation.
Elle avait conclu depuis longtemps qu'el: She had long concluded that she could not be both a serious artist and a mother; her son Jeff is raised by her grandparents, she only sees him on emotional weekends (a recent bestseller of the New York Times). weekends only; silver to buy materials Consequences: Illustration of the “terrible dichotomie” (Alice Neel)
Tout le monde est revenu des vacances de: Everyone came back from the spring holidays, classes resumed that morning; Dawson moved stones, which removed fat and muscled his back. A book ordered arrived the same day. rock chore, reinforced back
Marche le long de la route bordée de lam: Walk along the road lined with rusty streetlights and high vegetation; Rumaker worried in front of the antivenim kits but dares not ask; Connie, guessing, makes sure no one's ever been bitten. Words: “Il y a des crotales et des copperheads, mais ils s'occupent de leurs affaires.” Atmosphere: Brume rising, burning sun starting, unease quickly calmed by the calm of Connie Issue: First confidence in the place
Connie désigne une petite toile dans un: Connie designates a small canvas in a corner as a work with dynamic and interesting shapes; the group is politely fixed by whispering; Phyllis enters, responds “oh”, then absorbs its eye web; Rumaker looks at her a second time and sees muscle energy under chaos. Words: Connie: don't you think it has reached dynamic and interesting forms? Phyllis : “oh.” Atmosphere : Fresh, torrent rumbling, polished malaise mixed with glare Issue : Rumaker aesthetic conversion ; decision to return
Première apparition d'Olson, géant en se: First appearance of Olson, giant in brown searsucker, which throws itself on the chicken dish while being all courtesy; “in” piles between Olson and Harrison that make nearby tables laugh; Rumaker and Mary Ann only dare to respond by monosyllables; Olson makes them feel like they're counting. Words: Inside plaits not included; Olson and Harrison laughs that dominate the Atmosphere room: Human warmth, excitement, reassuring strangeness; laughs that shake beams Issue: Rumaker falls under charm; hope of a queer enclave
Après le dîner, départ pour Asheville (c: After dinner, departure for Asheville (baby races Kate, maybe an ice cream); Olson drives with one hand, speaks over his shoulder; Rumaker, hypnotized, watch the full moon flood the valley. Words: Words of Olson carried away by the wind, inaudible for Rumaker Atmosphere: Wind, low hood, lunar clarity of a quality never seen Issue: Full Rumaker rectification instead
Traversée de Pack Square, visite de la p: Crossing of Pack Square, visit of the intact board (room of Ben, writings of the father around the phone), then cemetery where Mary Ann and Rumaker read the stone piously; Roger jokes, Marge gets bored. Atmosphere: Juvenile romanticism, secret fervency hidden from Roger Issue: Confirmation of the vocation of writer of Rumaker
Cage écrit à Boulez qu'il a beaucoup lu: Cage writes to Boulez that he read Artaud a lot, thanks to him and Tudor, who read Artaud because of Boulez. English translations were rare.
Une de leurs blueprints est montrée dans: One of their blueprints is shown in the “Abstraction in Photography” exhibition, under the title “Blueprint: Photogram for Mural Decoration”. MoMA, May-July 1951 (German version: May-June)
L'un de leurs blueprints est montré dans: One of their blueprints is shown in the “Abstraction in Photography” exhibition, under the title Blueprint: Photogram for Mural Decoration. Catalogue title : Blueprint: Photogram for Mural Decoration
Première édition composée, mise en page,: First edition composed, layout, printed and linked by the author himself to the college's printing shop, under cover of cream paper. 12mo, cream cover
Williams rend visite à Miller un mois av: Williams visits Miller a month before entering Black Mountain: Avuncular Miller, funny, enthusiastic, encouraging; Williams sometimes beats him in ping-pong. Ping-pong (“comme battre Protée”) Consequences: Miller will later meet Harry Party and Williams (probably)
Avant de rejoindre Black Mountain, Willi: Before joining Black Mountain, Williams goes to San Francisco to see Rexroth, Duncan and Henry Miller and produces his first Jargon Press book: a small Broadside of one of his poems with an engraving by David Ruff. Broadside, engraving by David Ruff Consequences: birth of Jargon Press (Jargon #1)
Le collège publie une revue entièrement: The College publishes a magazine entirely composed of students' and professors' works. Summary: Nick Cernovich's Noh, Natasha Goldowski's “High Speed Computing Machines”, poems by Russell Edson and Joel Oppenheimer, Fielding Dawson's “Father”. Only one number appears; A second is composed but for lack of money to print it. Editorial shared by Richards, Oppenheimer, Fitton, Kemeny, Larsen. Consequences: Homonymy with the 1954 review, of which Olson and Creeley apparently did not exist.
De retour de ses mois au Yucatan, Olson: De back from his months in Yucatan, Olson presents a version of his essay “Human Universe” in conference before fifty members of the summer session 1951; The essay appeared the following winter in the fourth edition of Origin, then in 1954 in the Mayan Letters by Robert Creeley. Fifty Listeners Consequences: Published in Origin n°4 (Winter 1951-52) and then in Mayan Letters (1954)
Pendant la session d'été 1951, animée pa: During the summer session 1951, animated by the enthusiasm of Olson for the glyphs, Katherine Litz dances The Glyph on a score of Lou Harrison of the same name; Ben Shahn paints A Glyph for Charles (heavy letterrist strokes projected on a human torso like a musculature); the “Glyph Exchange” multimedia brings together Olson, Litz, Harrison and Shahn, which designs decorations and pattern for the Nicholas Cernovich student dance. the photo of Litz dancing The Glyph is taken by Teri Helen Dick
Outre The Glyph, Harrison et Litz collab: In addition to The Glyph, Harrison and Litz collaborate in the summer of 1951 on Chorales for Spring; the Adjustable Choir composition was flexible enough to allow the development of choreography.
Lou Harrison est recommandé à Black Moun: Lou Harrison is recommended to Black Mountain by John Cage for the summer session 1951. Consequences: presence of Harrison at BMC, summer 1951
Gablik fréquente Black Mountain College: Gablik frequented Black Mountain College in the summer of 1951, where she met Rauschenberg. Consequences: Beginning of a friendship of nearly two decades.
Session d'été 1951 avec Ben Shahn et Rob: Summer session 1951 with Ben Shahn and Robert Motherwell; Olson knew Shahn of their days at the Office of War Information at Washington. Consequences: Dawson describes this summer as strange and difficult, as the previous year.
De retour du Yucatan, Olson lit « Human: De Return of Yucatan, Olson reads “Human Universe” in front of fifty members of the summer session: the West of Socrates in the camps, the interrupted experience, the common flesh of the Mayans in the buses. Words: The “absolutely interfered with” action; the touch like “the natural law of flesh” Atmosphere: Prophetic urgency, limited but captured audience Issue: The college itself as politely dying and reborn
Durant la session d'été 1951, Gablik, je: Durant the summer session 1951, Gablik, young student, met Rauschenberg, back in college for the summer. Issue: the beginning of a twenty-year-old New York friendship through the avant-garde world
Un mois après avoir rendu visite à Henry: One month after visiting Henry Miller at Big Sur in June 1951, Williams goes to Black Mountain College. Visit to Miller in June 1951, departure for BMC in July Consequences: Start of the link of Williams with the college and with Olson
Callahan enseigne juillet-août aux côtés: Callahan teaches July-August alongside Siskind, invited by Hazel Larsen Archer; He found music and dance particularly stimulating and judged the college more free and democratic than the ID, despite a disorganized administration. Nicknamed memory: “ils ne nous payaient presque rien et ne nous nourrissaient presque pas… les étudiants avaient mangé toute la nourriture pendant l'hiver”. Consequences: First extensive joint work of Callahan and Siskind; Siskind accepts the position at the ID for the fall.
Invité par Olson, qu'il avait connu à l': Invited by Olson, whom he had known at the Office of War Information in the 1940s, Shahn arrived at the end of July 1951 to teach painting and lecture; he remains four weeks and participates fully in the life of the college, collaborating with the dancers. four-week stay; the other visual arts teacher that summer is Robert Motherwell; the same year appeared his biography Portrait of the Artist as an American Consequences: Invitation to represent the United States at the Biennale of Venice 1954; turning “palimpseste” in his painting
Olson, accompagné d'Alvin, neveu du cuis: Olson, accompanied by Alvin, nephew of the African-American cook at Jack Lipsey College, attends an auction where a black boy says “Like a race” — Olson draws a poem meditating on the word “race” as a word, image and event. silver coin passed from hand to hand; “the whites' eyes”; “the seats / theatre soft”; “feel / the weight” Consequences: poem “Glyph (For Alvin, & the Shahns)”
Olson achève deux pièces dansées cet été: Olson finished two dance pieces that summer, Apollonius of Tyanna and The Born Dancer, demonstrating his interest in the integration of music, dance and poetry.
Olson se tient à côté d'Alvin dans l'enc: Olson stands next to Alvin in the door frame; the boy's foot crosses the threshold and his voice draws white eyes; New Yorkers pass a silver coin along the ranks to feel the weight of it; The people of the South, idle by a summer evening, bid dollar per dollar; Alvin says “Like a race” and Olson is not sure if he heard. Words: “Like a race, the Negro boy said / And I wasn't sure I heard, what / Race, he said it clear” Atmosphere: too illuminated piece, soft seats, palpable racial tension, weight of silver Issue: the word “race” as abstraction applied to a living body; subject of the poem Glyph
Harrison arrive au bord du lac Eden quat: Harrison arrives on Lake Eden four years after a depression that led him to psychiatry at Presbyterian Hospital in New York; His distress is still alive. Consequences: Two months later he finished the song-piano score of Rapunzel.
Cunningham propose qu'Asawa et Lanier tr: Cunningham proposes that Asawa and Lanier work on her Greene Street home (where she has lived since 1947) — painting two rooms, bathroom and hallway — in exchange for a three-year photographic cover of their two toddlers; She buys all the paint and the photo material. Proposed contract: two rooms (bathroom and hallway) against three years of photographic coverage; painting and supplies paid by Cunningham. Consequences: Cunningham will continue to photograph Asawa-Lanier children well after three years, with dozens of photographs.
À l'automne 1951, Olson offre un cours i: In the fall of 1951, Olson offered a course entitled Hieroglyphic Writing and Ovid's Metamorphoses.
En septembre 1951, Laverne s'enquit de q: In September 1951, Laverne inquired about someone who could design his new exhibition space in San Francisco; He also inquired about the textile creations of Asawa. Consequences: Subsequent collaboration with Lanier and Asawa
Poème en broadside plié de 2 pages, écri: 2 pages folded Broadside poem, written to be read in absence of Olson at the centenary of Moby-Dick celebrated by the Melville Society at Williams College, Labour Day weekend, 2-4 September 1951; Sliding into a paper wallet; Special edition with an abstract hand-coloured drawing by Charles Oscar. Broadside folded, 2 pages, weekend of 2-4 September 1951
Dan présente Fielding à Franz le deuxièm: Dan presents Fielding to Franz on the second night; the warmth of the handshake and eyes establishes immediate reciprocity between two unknowns. Fielding had previously avoided Franz to observe it remotely. warm handshake, look Consequences: beginning of a very close friendship until the death of Franz
Au Cedar, Franz appelle Black Mountain «: At Cedar, Franz calls Black Mountain “downtown Manhattan”, including the college in its experience; Fielding laughs at pride. Consequences: Fielding feels proud to be part of the Franz experience
Franz demande son âge à Charley : « Quar: Franz asks Charley for his age: “Quarante et un”. Franz, condescending and sufficient: “Je suis plus vieux que toi.” Charley, injured, stares at him as if to say that's not what he expected. steps, tree, bench, millstone (millstone) Consequences: Charley rejected by Franz, price of including Black Mountain in Franz world
Après un éloge du charme de Roosevelt pa: After a praise of the charm of Roosevelt by Charley, Fielding launches : “C'est ça qui l'a tué.” Charley, astonished : “By God, that's right!”
Fielding avait écrit une belle histoire: Fielding had written a beautiful one-page story, had it framed and offered to Franz for Christmas; years later he found it among the antiques at the bottom of the Franz closet. one page, frame, Christmas, bottom of closet Consequences: durable injury
Une fille mince, rose et blanche, aux ch: A thin, pink and white girl with red hair arrives six weeks late in autumn 1951. M.C. presents her to Fielding who makes her visit; She's tense, defensive, smokes filter cigarettes with a Ronson lighter. shirt with small red and freshly starched white tiles, button neck, three open buttons, white pants, white sneakers, copper hair brushed back, lighter Ronson Consequences: it will change the lives of two students; Fielding will fall in love and sleep with her
Elle se dit écrivain, travaille sur un r: She calls herself a writer, works on a novel “à propos d'une fille que je connaissais”; “Elle est morte.” Walk in silence, then “C'est trop tôt, je t'en reparlerai un jour.”
M.C. prend un thé en lisant Ulysses avan: M.C. has tea reading Ulysses before his class; She questions Fielding about the new girl with a voice of “lady lawyer”, guesses her trouble; Fielding thinks the news is “gay”; Then she'll prepare “espresso”. Class with Alex and Cicely (Pat and Russell perhaps). unique college clock on the Dining Hall stove, coffee in a cup, cigarette roll, espresso
Dîner ensemble, choix d'une study, démén: Dinner together, choice of a study, moving; beer brought by someone, records; Tim knocks with three cans of beer; Victor exclaims “Behold! ... a lady!” by tripping; We read poems, we steal wine, we drink the lees of homemade beer, peanut butter sandwiches at Dining Hall.
Elle recommande Nightwood de Djuna Barne: She recommends Nightwood by Djuna Barnes as her favourite book; wears a heavy ID bracelet that it slides along the forearm; read Williams only Tennessee; Fielding quotes Charley, Pound, Frobenius. heavy ID bracelet
Une fille joufflue fan d'Eddie Fisher et: A young girl fan of Eddie Fisher and Ted Williams becomes a hardened Miami cop, armed, crossed in a gay bar in the Village; The other, shy and dug, becomes icy and bitter, sneezing at the mention of Black Mountain. Dark gay bar, farewell karate blow, “first class bastard” on Ted Williams
Assis en tailleur dans le couloir de nui: Sitting in a tailor in the night corridor; Fielding sterilizes a razor blade to the flame of a match, incise each thumb, suck, join their thumbs in the air bleeding and swearing “I, Fee, will never forget”; They kiss and then split up to go to class. razor blade, match, incision to the thumb, blood Consequences: the five then disperse (Kitty, Hitler, Dancer left; Farmboy comes back and leaves for good)
À vingt et un ans Fielding ouvre une his: At the age of twenty-one Fielding opens a story by “Monday is a metaphor” (the alliteration the amuse); At Black Mountain, naming a metaphor was a natural act, “une métaphore était aussi claire qu'une patate”.
Speedy, étudiant d'âge mûr (nullement ra: Speedy, a mature student (nully fast), writes a poem about the lake and spells “mirror” in “mirrow”; the fault is accepted, becomes done; Charley screams “LOOK AT THAT GODDAMNED WORD!” for lack of spelling become word
Fielding vérifie : le scarabée cornu de: Fielding checks: the horny beetle of the valley is a lucane (Stag Beetle), but different — older, bossy, longer and wider body — proving Charley's belief that the valley was original. hump, elongated and enlarged body
Des années plus tard, Franz présente Fie: Years later, Franz presented Fielding to Ornette Coleman in exactly the same warm way as Dan presented Franz to him; Fielding is seized and seized with admiration.
Adamic meurt à cinquante-deux ans d'une: Adamic died at fifty-two years of a bullet received on his farm in New Jersey; officially killed. Rice, who knew him too well, remains convinced of a violent crime: no note, no clear motive, the farm burned about at the time of death while Stella was absent. Adamic had been investigated in 1948 by HUAC for left-wing associations. Stella out of town; firm on fire; NYT of 5 September 1951 Consequences: Rice, devastated, loses his closest friend.
Franz demande l'âge de Charley, apprend: Franz asks Charley's age, learns that he is forty-one years old, responds condescendingly that he is older; Charley stares at him, wounded, as if to say that was not what he wanted Words: Franz: “I'm older than you are.”; Charley's look: “But Franz, this isn't what I — this isn't IT!” Atmosphere: sudden tension, mute injury under trees Issue: failure of the encounter between the great poet and the painter, two men with similar values
Debout au bar dans la lumière de la fenê: Standing at the bar in the light of the window, the glass of beer becomes a crystal flint; Franz drinks, rests the glass, whispers, sucks the foam, turns around, blinks the eye and speaks; around, Louie in white apron, bottles, taps Words: “Boy! The first one's always the best.” Atmosphere: crystalline light, sensitive fullness, revelation Issue: Franz as initiator: the world of things speaks through it
Visite guidée ; pause sur la courbe mont: Guided tour; pause on the rising curve; She contemplates the lake and the valley, throws her cigarette into the high grasses in an impatient gesture; Duration dialog (“Two years” / “It'll be longer”); Visit of the Studies Building, the farm, back to the lodges; conversation about her novel and the dead girl Words : “Gee, it's beautiful.” / “Been here long?” / “I love it.” / “She's dead.” / “It's too soon. I'll tell you about it again. Some time.” Atmosphere : tension, mistrust of the news, hand shaking while smoking, final smile Issue : erotic and literary encounter ; a mystery (death) planted for later
Fielding prend un café, s'assoit en face: Fielding takes a coffee, sits in front of M.C. who reads Ulysses, bows his chair, rolls a cigarette; M.C. in a low and serious voice guesses that he wants to talk, plays the lawyer, asks the question he expects; he admits to finding the new “gay” and interesting; it returns the question, it defends itself; She prepares an espresso and goes to the Words class: “Well, Fielding. It's clear you want to talk.” / “What do you think of the new girl?” / “Don't you think it's because she's so new?” Atmosphere: complicity, serious humour, tea and espresso, secret tremor of Fielding's hand Issue: M.C. reads in Fielding's heart; He discovers himself in love
Après le dîner commun, installation de l: After the joint dinner, install the new one in his study; common beers, discs; Tim knocks, three cans in hand, scratching his head; Victor stumbles back: “a lady!”; We read poems, we tell stories, we miss beer; Theft of wine, homebrew dregs, sandwiches at Dining Hall, then reads Words: Tim: “I've brought three cans of beer.”; Victor : “Behold! ... a lady!” Atmosphere : smoke, open window, gaiety defaced, depressive end without beer Issue : integration of the new ; small bohemian ceremonies of dying college
Assis en tailleur devant la study ; Fiel: Sitting as a tailor in front of the study; Fielding sterilizes the blade with the match, chokes his thumb, sucks; everyone does the same; inches joined in the air, bloody, nominative oath; kisses, then separation: there is class Words: “I, Fee, will never forget.” Atmosphere: solemn and childish ritual, night, urgency of classes Issue: conjuring the inevitable dispersion of the community
Speedy lit ou écrit son poème sur le lac: Speedy reads or writes his poem on the lake with “mirrow” for “mirror”; the whole community, and especially Charley, is seized; the fault is adopted as a fact Words: “LOOK AT THAT! LOOK AT THAT GODDAMNED WORD!” Atmosphere: collective wonder, sacred laughter burst Issue: error becomes poetry: essence of the pedagogy Olson
Souvent, le lampadaire est éteint ; Fiel: Often the floor lamp is turned off; Fielding stops in the dark, bare feet, hands stretched, smelling possible snakes; He gives in to the darkness, receives at night, listens to the slow rock under his feet and the moisture on his skin half naked Atmosphere: dense darkness “derrière la vision”, frightening and wonderful immobility, threshold of the universe at his fingertips Issue: Mystical union of the body and the archaic valley
Adamic, 52 ans, est trouvé mort d'une ba: Adamic, 52, was found dead with a bullet while Stella is out of town; the farm burns at about the time of death; no note, uncertain mobile; official suicide verdict challenged by Rice and number of friends. Atmosphere: Mystery, violence, fire. Issue: Loss of Rice's most expensive friend; Suspect plot after HUAC investigation.
Conscients des difficultés financières,: Aware of the financial difficulties, Robertson and Carl Kent ask Doyle (farmer) and Wes Huss if there is an alternative to the farm; Doyle proposes to cut the pines on a clear plot; the Council provides capital, they buy two double-edged axes and sell the pulpwood to a local factory; After two weeks they get a chainsaw that multiplies the production two sharp axes, a chainsaw bought after two weeks, pines cut for a pulp mill Consequences: production and sales increasing but insufficient in the face of the growing deficit; the two students leave for New York feeling the end of the nearby college
Naissance du fils du couple Harding, alo: Birth of the son of the Harding couple, while the temperature on the mountain often falls below zero mid-October, temperature often below 0°C on the mountain
Automne et hiver 1951-1952 : la faculté: Autumn and winter 1951-1952: Faculty reserves time to discuss its educational goals, echo of the thirties; official minutes keep the lively exchanges between Olson and the two new “sciences sociales” backups. Consequences: Progressive clarification of the Olson project
Excavation, aboutissement du style abstr: Excavation, the culmination of Bill's abstract-surrealist style, appeared at the Sixth Annual American Exhibition and received the Logan Medal and the acquisition prize. Logan medal, purchase prize Consequences: Infant institutional consecration.
Deux mois après son arrivée, Harrison ac: Two months after his arrival, Harrison finished the song-piano score of a fifty-five minute opera, put into almost verbatim music of the poem by William Morris (1858) according to the tale of Grimm “Rapunzel”. Dodecaphonic opera, three voices, two characters, six brief acts. Consequences: Act III will win a prize in Rome in 1954.
Rauschenberg écrit à la galeriste Betty: Rauschenberg writes to gallerist Betty Parsons to promote her White Paintings, in a language qualified as “édénique”, on Black Mountain College header paper — year of her meeting with John Cage in college. College Header Paper; formulas such as “presented with the innocence of a virgin” and “Today is their creater” (sic, for creator) Consequences: The text suggests that this language of the “blanc” anticipated the rhetoric of the white page of Cage/“Meyer” at the beginning of the next decade
Dawson écrit Mother en octobre 1951, res: Dawson wrote Mother in October 1951, remained unpublished until this book; with At The Farm, the only one of his news dedicated to the daily life of the college. Consequences: Played in Olson class.
En lisant Mother à voix haute, Olson but: By reading Mother aloud, Olson stops on the passage HO HO HEY DROP, stunned by discomfort; Dawson says embarrassed that it has false rhythms; Mary suggests that Fee (Dawson) read. La new flows from hand to hand up to Dawson, which reads it as it is written; Then each reads his own text, then Olson reads his new poems and exposes his teaching formula in construction. Order of circulation: Olson to Nick, Joel, Mary, Duck, Victor, Cynthia, then Dawson. Consequences: Change of pedagogy: each student reads his work and the discussion follows; Olson and students learn to listen together.
Consciencs du déficit, les deux étudiant: Conscientcs of the deficit, the two students offer a business to farmer Doyle and Wes Huss; on his suggestion they cut down and plug pines with the axe for two weeks, sell the pulpwood, get from the Council a chainsaw that multiply the production, then give up for lack of sufficient results Atmosphere: extremely hard and slow work, exaltation of the company, sadness of the start Issue: save the college in bankruptcy — failure
Olson lit les travaux des étudiants à vo: Olson reads students' work out loud; arriving at Mother's HO HEY DROP passage, he interrupts, tries, troubles to the point of stuttering; Dawson, embarrassed, tells him he has the wrong rhythms; Olson still tries, fails; Mary proposes to let Fee read; the new hand-to-hand pass to Dawson that reads it as it is written; So everyone reads their own text, talks, then Olson reads their new poems and builds their teaching formula under the group's questions. Words: Dawson: The rhythms are wrong. Mary: Why not let Fee read? Atmosphere: Manages, stutters, then releases when Dawson reads; mutual attention, olson on the quiver. Issue: The reversal of the master-pupil ratio: Olson ceases to be the only player, the class becomes a listening community.
Série de réunions (25 octobre, 2, 9, 21,: Series of meetings (25 October, 2, 9, 21, 28, 30 November 1951) to discuss the study reform; On November 2, Olson states that it believes “à la liberté absolue de l'étudiant, la liberté même de se concentrer sur une seule matière”. Minutes kept at Raleigh Archives Consequences: preparing the reorganization into institutes
Pendant une vague de froid record avec n: During a record cold wave with snow and ice, Elaine slides on the ice and breaks his right leg by visiting the Empire State Building. Convalescent in Denby's apartment (parted in Italy), it is chewed by Kaldis in plaster, skirt raised to show the height of plaster on the thigh, right foot on a pillow, another pillow tight in the arms, expression “comment-me-suis-je-retrouvée-dans-cette-galère”; Kaldis insists on his nails of hands and feet as suggesting a bright red varnish. plaster high on the thigh; pointed nails in pencil; record cold wave with snow and ice Consequences: weeks in wheelchair and crutches; She hires a lawyer (who writes speeches for Adlai Stevenson's campaign); first vote of his life for Stevenson
Elaine se fracture le tibia et le péroné: Elaine fractures the tibia and peronea in early November 1951; in an undated letter to Josef Albers, she said she had finished with wheelchairs, crutches and canes. La Albers response, dated April 18, 1952, celebrates its recovery. “wheelchair, crutches, canes, etc.”; letters stored at the Josef and Anni Albers Foundation Consequences: Evidence of a lasting epistolar link between Elaine and Albers after BMC
Document Olson dédié à Cy Twombly, novem: Olson document dedicated to Cy Twombly, November 1951.
Convalescente, jupe relevée pour montrer: Convalescent, skirt raised to show the height of the plaster, foot on a pillow, another tight against it, it lays ; Kaldis insists on his nails as a red varnish Atmosphere: self-deteriation of an invalid in the middle of a worldly life Issue: the fall (in a clean sense) at the top of the artistic scene
Réunions consacrées aux « fins éducative: “fins éducatives” meetings: Adams asks why so few academic courses and pleads for a disciplinary boss the first two years, denouncing aberrant students and the risk of chaos; Olson answers that the right term is “historique”, that BM works on living knowledge and not on the history of knowledge, that there has never been any other pattern than the passionate interest of the teacher; Two weeks later Sprague tries “coincer” Olson on its “pitch spécial d'éducation”, Adams ends up doubting that anyone understands Olson; Olson says we win not to plan a course. Words: Adams: Many students are aberrant personalities, too focused on themselves, there is a considerable lack of historical knowledge. Olson: This place goes blind, and it is as legitimate to go blind in education as elsewhere. Olson: The individual is more complex than any curriculum. Adams: He doubts anyone here knows what Olson is talking about. Atmosphere: Plays good child but background, Olson style torrential against methodical questioning Issue: Two conceptions of education face each other: the survival of the “nouveau” Black Mountain depends on it
Correspondance avec Erwine Laverne (show: Correspondence with Erwine Laverne (New York showroom): Lanier talks about Ruth's “wire stuff” (wire work); undated draft letter from Ruth around 1952. terms : “wire stuff”
En proie à une crise sentimentale, River: In the midst of a sentimental crisis, Rivers cut his wrists one afternoon; it recovers from Fairfield Porter who paints it with symmetrical bandages and a hebate air; Elaine, in his letter, sweeps his fear of nervous breakdown like a lack of vitamin B, judging him “tellement vivace et exhibitionniste” symmetrical bandages; fantasy diagnosis: vitamin B deficiency
Toujours en convalescence au printemps 1: Still recovering in spring 1952, Elaine accepts the invitation of Porter: “partie pour deux jours, restée deux semaines”, making only “peindre, manger, parler, lire et dormir”; Porter to write her articles, she takes an “plaisir malicieux” to work in her workshop and grab “de gros paquets” from her painting that she usually cannot afford. large packages of borrowed paint
En voiture avec Mercedes Matter et sa fa: By car with Mercedes Matter and her family: she finds the subjects of the great Renoir “vulgairement beaux”, jokes about the humor of Barnes which makes Picasso “un second coute fiable mais médiocre”, and notes that the great Seurat and the Great Bathers of Cézanne seem to him “des reproductions agrandies”, so much so we know too closely a painting never seen. Renoir “vulgairement beaux”; Picasso “second coute” Consequences: anticipation (translated only in 1968) of the problem of Benjamin on mechanical reproduction
Quatre voitures pour convoyer les invité: Four cars to transport the guests. The artists, for whom a party rhymes with drunkenness, arrive with bottles of Scotch, gin and vodka; the host, who planned a special dinner watered with a German moselle, preventively locks up their alcohol. When he monitors the kitchen, Kline forces the cabinet and circulates the bottles. 4 cars; Scotch, gin, vodka; German muselle planned; Cabinet forced by Kline Consequences: after drinking the fort, artists... (continued off-road)
Rosenberg et Bill deviennent amis après: Rosenberg and Bill became friends after seeing each other a lot in the summer of 1952; Rosenberg plays the provocative, Bill launches enigmatic remarks to decode; The two couples are bound by a common antipathy for Lee Krasner, then in a fierce and tearing crusade to promote her husband and crush any rival. Bill, in private, mocked Rosenberg's theories.
Dîner raffiné chez l'intellectuel allema: Fine dinner at the German intellectual Fritz Hensler; it locks the alcohol brought by the guests, Kline forces the cabinet and redistributes the bottles; the leg is consumed in a vacarm worthy of the Cedar Tavern; At dawn, the question of the unsettled beds, Elaine states that she will return to New York on foot and walk away with her plaster, forcing Bill to catch her. four cars to transport guests; bottles of Scotch, gin and vodka; Moselle wine German (sold in plants or spilled on land according to the versions); Leg; Elaine leg plaster; martinis Consequences : Out of the world meal desired by Hensler; Elaine will later say to be ashamed of artists' behavior
Rencontrée au Cedar Tavern, artiste comm: Met at Cedar Tavern, a commercial artist, Joan Ward became Bill's mistress, who moved to the top floor of 88 East 10th Street between 3rd and 4th Avenues; She lives next door. Consequences: De facto separation of the couple during the Woman's year
Elaine se rend avec des amis artistes au: Elaine goes with friends artists to the four-day festival: Cunningham choreography Stravinsky's wedding and Symphony for a single man by Pierre Schaeffer; Bernstein directs Blitzstein's adaptation of the Quat's Opera and creates his own opera Trouble in Tahiti; Elaine will later enigmatically evoke this Quat's Opera as an explanation of certain beliefs of her mother.
À l'automne 1952, Bill déménage au 88 Ea: In the fall of 1952 Bill moved to 88 East 10th Street, which became the heart of a colony of informal artists and attracted bold galleries. Consequences: New pole of the artistic scene.
Soirée chez Fritz Hensler (décrit comme: Evening at Fritz Hensler (described as professor of philosophy by Lionel Abel, sociologist by Edvard Lieber) where Elaine's leg was still plastered; Lieber the date of July 1951 according to the memories of Elaine, but the accident of November 1951, the author proposes spring 1952. A subsequent visit to Hensler took place in February 1954. Cast on the leg; diverging accounts of Abel (Intellectual Follies, 215-16) and Lieber
Anni suit le cours de Kubler sur l'art p: Anni follows the course of Kubler on pre-Columbian art and chooses as a search for the reconstruction of the techniques of the Andean weavers for the very wide pieces of the ancient Nazca; She trains the expert Junius Bird in a debate (letter of 21 April 1952). The essay will appear as “A Structural Process in Weaving” in On Designing (1959). Letter to Bird, 21 April 1952 Consequences: Publication in On Designing
La démission polémique de Cruz permet à: La Cruz's polemic resignation allowed Piwonka to assume Composición Pura (called Plástica), closer to the Bauhaus model, then normalized by the work of Albers in Chile since 1953. Piwonka will lead him until 1967, replaced by the Taller of Arquitectura d'Octavio Sotomayor. Consequences: The model of the Preliminary Course is transmitted to the art and design schools of the PUC
Au début du decanat de Sergio Larraín (1: At the beginning of Sergio Larraín's (1952-1967), he commissioned Emilio Duhart to contact an international professor of prestige to temporarily direct the course of Composition Pre-Arquitectónica given by Piwonka. Consequences: Arrival of Albers in Chile in June 1953
Anni suit la classe d'art précolombien d: Anni follows George Kubler's pre-Columbian art class; his research focuses on the reconstruction of Andean weaver techniques for the very large fabrics of ancient Nazca; She discusses in letters with textile expert Junius Bird of the Museum of Natural History of New York. Letter to Bird of 21 April 1952: his speculations may seem “far-fetched to non-weavers” Consequences: Research published as “A Structural Process in Weaving” in On Designing (1959)
La démission contestée de Cruz permet à: La disputed resignation of Cruz allows Piwonka to take over the Pure Composition, renamed Art Plastic, closer to the Bauhaus model; Piwonka will teach him until 1967, when Octavio Sotomayor's Architecture Workshop replaces him. Consequences: The course was standardized after 1953 under the influence of Albers work in Chile.
Devenu doyen de la faculté d'architectur: As Dean of the Faculty of Architecture and Fine Arts of the PUC (1952-67), Sergio Larrain entrusted Emilio Duhart, one of Chile's most important modern architects, with the task of finding an international teacher of prestige for the Pure Composition course then taught by Piwonka. Consequences: Duhart solicits Josef Albers.
Josef enseigne à l'Université de La Hava: Josef teaches at the University of Havana (9-17 February); summer in Mexico, Mayan ruins of Yucatán; Anni starts designing for Knoll.
Visite à Nell en fuyant la chaleur d'Arl: Visit Nell fleeing heat from Arlington, Virginia; Summer Institute in session: Olson giant, Cage lecture on Zen Buddhism, Kline paintings, Weinrib sandstone; Always polluted lake, daily swimming at the water hole in North Fork where they meet Rauschenberg and Thiel, all admiring the smooth pebbles on the bank. Consequences: Last view of the working college.
Max Dehn meurt pendant le service milita: Max Dehn dies during Dawson military service. He's buried in the rhododendrons under the tank. Burial: rhododendrons below the tank. Consequences: Flash-forward of Dawson, then to the army.
Un matin d'automne frais et doucement br: On a cool and gently misty autumn morning, Dawson, sitting on the top rocks, hears a stifled friction: Max Dehn appears on the trail near the barbed wire that Dawson had helped to tender. Dough but pink cheeks, deep eyes and very shiny, white hair in the wind, collar half raised, slightly vaulted. They exchange a smile and a whispered hello; The little curved body passes and disappears in the fog. Consequences: Shortly before conscription of Dawson, Dehn “s'effaçait” visibly.
Après avoir demandé poliment à emmener B: After politely asking to take Branwen, two and a half years old, promising to show her the wild flowers, Dehn walked hand in hand with her, bright white hair in the sun, an hour on the wooded slope; They came back delighted with each other and he greeted her ceremonially. A few days later, a hearse came early in the morning to load his body in the clearing. 2.5 years; white hair in the sun; one hour's walk; Fog in the early morning Consequences: Death of Dehn
Le doyen académique Worth Howard les int: Academic Dean Worth Howard questioned them; They gave him a tour of the college and enjoyed it with exaggerated stories about the school. Fearing that they had ruined their chances, they were hired: Howard would have told the administrators that having survived BMC and could laugh at it, they were tough enough for Egypt. quote from Howard to the trustees Consequences: Departure of the couple to Cairo
Revenus comme Olson le lui avait ordonné: As Olson had ordered her, she showed her diary; A few days of glory when she was the winner of the workshop, reduced to six students. La first week, Olson hovers over them, slipping behind his big glasses, finger placed on a clean line of the newspaper: “I pointed westward, towards his grave” (about his father). six students; thick glasses; line on Father's grave Consequences: “Si, si, girl! That's space!” — Olson triumphant
Trois récits très autobiographiques sur: Three very autobiographical stories about her childhood, following the precept of Olson (“écrire depuis le centre”), earned her the annual Creative Writing Award awarded to a senior student at Barnard. 500 dollars, round sum for the time Consequences: Jalousie/impulsion of Olson towards New York publishing firm jurors
Furieux devant les prix new-yorkais, Ols: Furious in the face of the New York awards, Olson splintered her with a new tutoring by shouting that she still writes conservative junk, that she must stick to a newspaper, and above all not attempt to publish for ten years. The “morse géant” rises from its chair, its six feet seven deployed. six feet seven (2m); Cree; forbidden to publish for ten years Consequences: Second censor; She obeys and keeps her diary for years.
Kline succède à Jack Tworkov, artiste in: Kline succeeds Jack Tworkov, a guest artist of the month of June, whose intellectual and scholarly approach to contemporary art contrasted with the smiling generosity of Kline, which was in no way “le professeur” and had no idea of teaching. Tworkov invited in June; Scientific/generous contrast Consequences: Very positive impact on the community
Fin d'été, Olson suggère à McGee de rest: In late summer, Olson suggests that McGee stay for autumn and winter; McGee, already a graduate at Indiana University, would accept if the college could get her a master's degree. Olson rubs its chin, looks at it with its gigantic eyes: “Okay”, it summons the Board of Fellows. The council deliberates the best part of a morning and concludes that even with all its imagination, the college cannot achieve this feat. a morning of deliberation; Master's impossible despite the BA possible Consequences: The effort and goodwill remain memorable for McGee
L'atelier en plein air de McGee est just: McGee's outdoor workshop is just under the Wolpe apartment in the Studies Building; The badly isolated floors make him suffer the moods and angers of the composer. Wolpe, a strong and boiling European personality, becomes for many “notre Far-out Beethoven”: warm to Lou Harrison, distant to John Cage, the most moody and volatile faculty this summer. non-insulated floors; nickname “Far-out Beethoven”
Rauschenberg est la première personne qu: Rauschenberg is the first person that McGee and his wife Marty meet upon arrival; large, imposing, he immediately offered them a hand to unload the old Ford 39. He spotted a pack of small canvases whose compositions were covered with zinc white — still vaguely visible below — and became enthusiastic: “This is really an interesting painting.” Ford 1939; small format; zinc white; gestures at the end of the arm Consequences: McGee, destabilized, no longer knows what to paint on these canvases
Adams, anthropologue amateur d'art en di: Adams, an amateur art anthropologist in trouble on a canvas, will hit at night Rauschenberg; the light on the porch, he discovers with horror that he walked on a spread canvas to dry; The prints get into the paint. porch without lighting; canvas spread on the floor of the porch Consequences: For the witness, this incident summarizes the avant-garde nature of academic life at BMC
Schème d'Olson pour remplacer le cursus: Olson Schème to replace the basic curriculum with institutes: interaction of leading professionals, as in summer sessions. Five eight-week institutes planned: crafts; theatre bringing together actors, dancers, writers, musicians and painters (Boris Aronson anticipated to direct him); “nouvelles sciences de l'homme” (Christopher Hawkes approached from England); natural sciences with emphasis on ecology; arts in summer. The remaining “académiques” (except Fiola Shepard) lose all hope; Sprague denounces an “semblable à un sac de haricots sauteurs” community in intellectual, moral and physical disintegration. 5 institutes, 8 weeks each Consequences: Departure of the last academics, Sprague included
De retour de son année congée, elle mépr: De back from her year off, she despises Olson and quickly finds it impossible to dislodge it; The catalogue nevertheless credits it with nine courses, from introductory chemistry to atomic physics. 9 courses listed in his name
Séminaire tronqué de trois semaines sur: Three-week Truncated Seminar on Archaeology and Mythology: Olson, Braidwood (Jarmo Searcher) and Maria von Franz, Jung Associate. Jung himself had been invited and had proposed von Franz, already on a conference tour.
L'anthropologue anglais serait venu, mai: The English anthropologist would have come, but as a prerequisite the college also paid for his girlfriend's trip, which the community could not afford.
Quelques mois avant l'institut, ils acce: A few months before the Institute, they accepted the position that all Alfred University students had refused, indignant by the $80 a month. They discover the workshop built by Bob Turner, unused since his departure but in perfect condition. Salary: $80/month; workshop in a flat field near the Studies Building, large windows on the valley, “le meilleur four dont on puisse rêver”, fully equipped studio. Consequences: Compromise: “potters-in-residence” but not faculty members in the first year; oven autonomy (purchases and recipes kept).
Karnes a peu d'élèves ; Mary Caroline Ri: Karnes has few students; Mary Caroline Richards works intensively with the couple. Some despise her pots, not enough “rugueux, réels, naturels”, because she sells in Asheville and New York stores. After Thanksgiving dinner, people stack turkey bones in Karnes dishes to mark their contempt (Remy Charlip story).
Déjà venu en 1948-1949 pour suivre Sue W: Already came in 1948-1949 to follow Sue Weil, then considered painter more serious than he; Albers found him frivolous and told him he didn't have “rien à lui apprendre”. In 1952, married to Sue, he returned after the shock of his white canvases at Betty Parsons Gallery. In 1948-1949: imaginative costumes, dye baths cooking on the stove of the kitchen, purple underwear that came out. Consequences: With Cage and Cunningham, and the help of David Tudor, he conducts form explorations that will mark the theatre of mixed media.
Des voies sexuelles explorées cet été-là: Sexual routes explored that summer disconcert Olson, Fiore, and Rice, men sharing a stereotypical, almost trucker, vision of the “masculinité”.
Lou Harrison, boursier Guggenheim 1952-1: Lou Harrison, Guggenheim Fellow 1952-1953, convinced Wolpe, tired of teaching, replacing him. Wolpe, 50, teaches composition; his wife, poet Hilda Morley, literature and Hebrew. Wolpe and Olson, both dynamic, immediately sympathize; the climate suits the new direction of its music. Wolpe knew Jalowetz in Germany, studied with Webern, taught at the Philadelphia Musical Academy (where he had David Tudor as a student). Consequences: Wolpe decides to stay after 1953, to the great regret of Harrison; Cage sees an “usurpation”.
Invité à enseigner la composition (ce qu: Invited to teach composition (which flatters him, no other school would have “rêvé” to do), Cage announces that he will not teach the students' work but his, as apprentice manufacturer the “Williams Mix”. Not a student enrols; he renounces all organized teaching and becomes simply a friend of music students. Long discussion and strippoker sessions with music students. Consequences: No formal courses; reading the Huang Po night as the unique “cours”.
Lecture intégrale de la première édition: Full reading of the first edition of the Huang Po Doctrine of Universal Mind (notes, preface, everything), in front of 20 to 30 people of a community swollen at about 70 for the summer. Several assistants play the dialogue where the master insults the student. Consequences: A profound effect, especially on a veteran of Korea “au bout du rouleau” and another student at a perplexity point in his life.
Cage utilise « exclusivement » les opéra: Cage uses “exclusivement” random operations and composes “Williams Mix” on magnetic tape, funded by Paul and Vera Williams, college benefactors. Paul Williams also supported early David Tudor and Living Theater, still “sans conditions. Magnifiquement.”
Cage lit à voix haute le texte zen du Hu: Cage reads aloud the Zen text of the Huang Po, which he considers as “le texte essentiel”, in front of twenty to thirty people; several listeners help him, notably by playing the dialogue section where the master insults the student. 20 to 30 listeners on a community of about 70 people for the summer session Consequences: Deep effect on a veteran of the Corsican War “au bout du rouleau” and on a student at a confusing turn of his life
Cage, avec Tudor, conçoit un événement t: Cage, with Tudor, designs a 45-minute theatrical event (duration of the time bands it tracks on paper) where each guest freely fills his niche: poetry readings (Olson, M.C. Richards), paintings and discs (Rauschenberg), piano (Tudor), dance (Cunningham). The audience, sitting in the center in four sections separated by diagonals, finds an empty white cup on each chair; coffee is served in cups at the end — including those used as ashtrays. 45 minutes of working hours; empty white cups on the seats; coffee paid at the end; children who scream; barking dogs Consequences: The event will be considered the “préhistorique” precursor of the 1960s happenings (Allan Kaprow)
Le compositeur Stefan Wolpe, furieux con: The composer Stefan Wolpe, furious about the event, gets up and goes in full performance.
Selon Weinrib, Mrs. Jalowetz, femme bell: According to Weinrib, Mrs. Jalowetz, a beautiful woman from German radical tradition (Schönberg), repeats as a “Deep in the middle ages” (“Au plus profond du Moyen Âge”) incantation; Olson, sitting next to her, remains non-committal, “joue la coolitude” facing the poem distributed at the hearing he had written in advance. Olson had written the poem in fragments and distributed the replicas to spectators who rose in turn
Spectacle simultané aux éléments mal rec: Simultaneous spectacle with poorly reconstituted elements: a escapeau or desk (M.C. Richards was on horseback or in a basket, so probably Rauschenberg or Olson on top; Olson may be taken down to the public after reading); Rauschenberg expounded something of his hand (black or white stars) as background or foreground; a gramophone with records from the 1920s-30s or Edith Piaf; audience in the center (triangles, squares or undivided) with alleys where Merce danced followed by a barking or silent dog; Cage read something (an account says: Emerson and Thoreau); Tudor played something (perhaps Cunningham itself played); projections (diapositive, films, montages, painted glass). Everyone loved it, except Wolpe and Johanna Jalowetz (who loved at least the participants). Considered possibly the very first event “multimédia”. escabeau/pupitre, horse, basket, gramophone, records 1920-30 or Piaf, dog, slides or painted glass, black or white canvases by Rauschenberg Consequences: Considered retrospectively as the first multimedia event; founding material for Cunningham, Cage, Rauschenberg, Tudor.
Kline passa la plupart de l'été au collè: Kline spent most of the summer in college; Everyone loved him and he loved Black Mountain, but he was worried that young people would learn nothing that would help them make a living by becoming painters or writers. In front of an exhibition of paintings, he said they had to be large canvases because he absolutely felt “helpless” or “hopeless” (Cage no longer remembers the word). notice before an exhibition of paintings
Cunningham situe cet épisode peut-être l: Cunningham places this episode perhaps the previous summer: Olson decided to study dance, came regularly, worked hard, at the cost of considerable physical risks; He told Cunningham he didn't have to look at him if he didn't want to. Cunningham grimmed with incomprehension at first — it was actually concentrated — and ended up with “comprendre” that physical experience. Cunningham compares it to “un morse léger” (light walrus)
Trop occupé pour se faire opérer, il fit: Too busy to get surgery, he made a diet and ran by pressing a bag of ice on his stomach with every pain. In 1953, he was in excellent physical fitness. bag of ice on the belly
Tentative (échouée) de ranimer l'intérêt: Attempted (failed) to revive the interest of Forbes: Huss describes two impulses — rigidity of control in those who feared the dominant irrationality, and impulse towards the abolition of any limit in a group blindly responding to the philosophy of sensation; On both sides, incurable romantics reacting rather than acting.
Ferme en bon état après le départ de Ray: Farm in good condition after the departure of Ray Trayer, land extension plans under Doyle Jones; $5,000 borrowed from Paul Williams for the beef herd, an additional $5,000 for scholarships and operations; the new scientific building ($6,000 donated by Forbes) remains unfinished — “les étudiants n'avaient pas su construire aussi bien qu'ils concevaient” — Dan Rice came back with a small team to finish it; five acres sold to a neighbour; new accreditation attempt (registration 1952 at 35, low level); always about a rector or “chef administrateur”; the Community Council (flowering under Wallen) is relaunched. $5,000 (troupeau) + $5,000 (bourse/function), $6,000 (Forbes, science), 35 students, 5 acres sold Consequences: Almost all of these projects will fail; late 1953 the community narrowed.
Beaucoup sentaient dès 1952 que la décad: Many felt as early as 1952 that physical (non-spiritual) decadence was advanced, but cared little about it: Olson argued that this mood poverty is the only conducive to living and working, and that “la seconde poussée du lieu est maintenant en plein mouvement”.
Un ancien des années trente revient supe: An elder from the thirties comes back to oversee a reorganized work programme; nine special work grants are created allowing some students to provide up to 30 hours of work per week.
