Pour ses treize ans, Hermine reçoit des: For her thirteen years, Hermine receives gifts made by Rauschenberg and Rockburne; Rauschenberg assembles thorny branches, grass strands, petals, sand and a figure on sensitive paper, exposes to light, removes everything: the shapes remain in white silhouettes on blue background. Atmosphere: Intimate, summer, childhood in the middle of the avant-garde Issue: The private gesture that condenses the sensory revelations of the summer 1952
Rauschenberg installe les filles Tworkov: Rauschenberg installs the girls Tworkov blotties in a mass of ferns, then photograph Hermine profile, collapsed body, negligently tied hair, natural light and low depth of field that flattens the space between foliage and it. Atmosphere: Monkey, vegetal, net contours Issue: Equality of figure and background — the very perception taught by the college
Au printemps 1952, Cernovich imprime le: In spring 1952, Cernovich printed the poem of Duncan in red ink on verged paper; Twombly, probably with the help of Rauschenberg, performs the cover linogravures within months of Rauschenberg breaking with Susan Weil. Words: First verse of the poem printed on the sheet. Atmosphere: Coral red ink on green paper, intimate and risky. Issue: A poem of love queer printed in the segregationist South at the heart of the cold war.
Une sculpture en fil de fer de près de d: An iron wire sculpture of nearly ten feet swings like a pendulum to visitors, fascinated and confused. Atmosphere: Perplexed fascination Issue: The work refuses categories: neither sculpture nor craft
Cage est hors de la ville et prête son a: Cage is out of town and lends its apartment to Rauschenberg; Rauschenberg is working on his Black Paintings series there; To thank him, he painted a Black Painting over the No. 1 rose and sand that Cage had bought from Betty Parsons in 1951 — a painting itself painted on a canvas of Sue Weil. Issue: The work as palimpsest: three layers of authors and affections.
Rauschenberg se pose nonchalamment devan: Rauschenberg poses nonchalantly in front of the White Painting with four panels, camera or look of a third party capturing the artist and his work Atmosphere: Assumed break, posture of dandy Issue: The artist becomes the subject of his own work
Rauschenberg agrandit et dry-mounte les: Rauschenberg enlarges and dry-mountes the photographs of Twombly's paintings for his application for the scholarship, then imagines that Albers would have approved this treatment Words: He claims to have made large, carefully mounted enlargements, before concluding: “Albers would have liked that” Atmosphere: Handicrafted pride, echo of the rigorism of Vorkurs Issue: The legacy of Albers persists until the administrative steps of the former student
Twombly, en blue jeans, un carnet de cro: Twombly, in blue jeans, a sketch book in hand, stands in profile next to the colossal fragment of the hand of Emperor Constantine, absorbed in his contemplation; Rauschenberg tight frame Atmosphere: Crushing in front of the missing grandeur, like Fuseli's despair in front of the same fragments Issue: The young American facing the weight of European antiquity
Autour du couple en crise et du bébé Chr: Around the couple in crisis and the baby Christopher, Rauschenberg hangs its modular white canvases as background, projects its slides, while Cage reads, Cunningham dances, Tudor plays and Olsen recites — the first American theatrical synthesis of the arts. Atmosphere: summer warmth, college hospitality, joyful eclecticism Issue: the rejection of Albers and the birth of an art of openness; prototype of Happenings
Olson lit des poèmes du haut d'une échel: Olson reads poems from the top of a scale; behind him the white paintings of Rauschenberg; Edith Piaf accelerated skewer; Cunningham dances with a wandering dog on the chaotic scene. Atmosphere: Burlesque Chaos, Ritual Derision Issue: exact denial of GLYPH: chance and zen replace myth and rite
Dans un dispositif de chaises en quatre: In a four-triangle chair system and White Paintings on the Cross, the performers occupy overlapping time ranges: poetry readings, dance, piano, discs, Zen talk, reverse slides — without anything being causally linked, but in a strict cut. Atmosphere: Bath of light, images, movements and noises (Artaud) Issue: La birth of happening
Un carton calligraphié arrive : lavis no: A calligraphic board arrives: black wash in which are cut out of strong graphic panels, sketch of pots, lists of discussions, demonstrations and faculty; on the programme, two weeks on form, mass production, master and apprentice, the craft/art relationship. Atmosphere: Japonizing aesthetic, ink and paper, promise of East-West encounter. Issue: Gather Bauhaus, England and Japan in a single room of rural America.
À son arrivée, Leach annonce que les mat: Upon his arrival, Leach announces that the materials at hand are unknown to him, he will not demonstrate and will only speak; Under pressure from the audience, he gives in. Hamada, on the other hand, claims to be able to manage itself: it picks up clays and enamels on the hillside in front of the workshop, binds weed stems in a beam to make brushes, and works in turn in front of potters and students, using the piece turned not as an end but as a starting point for other manipulations. Words: Hamada: he could “make do” — manage — with the materials on site. Atmosphere: Emulation between two masters, public potters and students taking the measure of American academicism. Issue: Two conceptions of the craftsman facing the unknown: the prudence of the expertise against improvised adaptation.
Bouteille de gin remplie d'eau, deux ver: Bottle of gin filled with water, two glasses, feigned and real mixed intoxication; sun, dust in suspension; from the open door through the corridor to the light on the mountain; exchange of bluejeans; dinner gong from the lake; slow walk, separate, head that bursts Atmosphere : Luminous, suspended, melancholic Issue : The idyllus at its top, already closed
Salut civil obligé ; Doyle demande du ha: Forced civilian greeting; Doyle asks for the hangar, offers nails, bursts of laughter, slams the back of Dawson; his eyes flash to the word “teach”; Dan frowns the eyebrows away Words : “How's that Tobacco Barn coming?” / “Slow.” / “You're damned RIGHT you will” / “That's OAK!” / “That oak is gonna teach you.” / Dan : “He sure has it bad.” Atmosphere : Repeated Southern Rires, Warm Frontage, Underlying Threat Issue : Friendship of Work Broken by College Policy
Face à face sur la planche, chacun sur s: Face to face on board, each on its nail; Dawson notes the strange color (lead and purple) of its nail, understands that it is black Words: “The Goddamned thing's changed color!” / “Hey! Let's quit! For Christ's sake — it's NIGHT!” / “Well by God, so it is.” / “Beautiful.” / “It is.” Atmosphere: Sudden obscurity, dizziness of work, peaceful complicity Issue: Total absorption in gesture until time is wasted
Querelle sur l'endroit de la scie hier ;: Quaerelle on the saw spot yesterday; Dan blushes, short, brandishes the saw Words: “Here — HERE is your saw!” Atmosphere: Exasperation, resentment, shame Issue: La stress of exhaustion
Pianiste au travail sur la Deuxième Sona: A pianist working on the Second Boulez Sonata, Tudor admits to her partner Richards that the score is not her real problem. Words: He says the sonata is complicated but he doesn't have “pas de problèmes avec les notes, mais avec la musique”. Atmosphere: Intimacy of the couple at work, intellectual confidence. Issue: This confidence leads Richards to Artaud and, from there, to the theatre matrix and its Double in English.
Exposition « New Work by Josef Albers —: Exhibition “New Work by Josef Albers — Homage to the Square et Transformation of a Scheme” Gallery Press release, 7-26 January 1952
Huss sollicite à nouveau Forbes, qui ref: Huss again requests Forbes, which refuses: it feels no closer to Black Mountain “ni en esprit ni dans la connaissance du lieu”. He estimated that he had given more than $20,000 in total and had done his part. more than $20,000 in total; letters of 20 January and 12 March 1952 Consequences: loss of a major lessor
Elaine et Mercedes Matter, seules femmes: Elaine and Mercedes Matter, the only women on the Club's voting committee; January 25, panel “Abstract Expressionism II” with Gottlieb, Holtzman, Diller and Busa; in April, only woman on “Integration of Art and Architecture” (with Denby, Hendler, Kiesler) and “Problems of the Engaged Artist” (with Newman, Navaretta, Abel, Hendler); on May 14, she organizes the “New Poets” panel introduced by O'Hara with Ashbery, Guest, Schuyler, Rivers moderator
Invité à donner un cours d'une semaine a: Invited to give a one-week course to the students and professors of architecture, Albers is received as a celebrity: housed at the best hotel, celebrated by architects, academics and the American cultural attaché; he writes four letters to Anni during the week; all presentations are recorded; He's doing more Spanish than in Mexico. La city has grown enormously since its first visit in 1934-12; the questions do not stop Consequences: Illustrating his intact love of teaching after thirty years
Photographie d'Albers enseignant à La Ha: Photograph of Albers teaching in Havana in February 1952, during its Yale period.
Laverne suggéra d'introduire de la coule: Laverne suggested introducing color; Asawa apparently did so by painting the pieces and probably incorporating coloured yarn (letters Lanier–Laverne of 4 and 12 February 1952; letter from Laverne to Asawa of 18 September 1953).
Seize entretiens d'une heure sur l'histo: Sixteen one-hour interviews on the history of Surrealism, broadcast February-June 1952 and published in the same year under the title Entreprises 1913–1952 ; Breton defended the “phénomène lyrique” in poetry and the example of Lautréamont. 16 one-hour interviews
A la reunion de faculte ou chaque etudia: At the faculty meeting where each student is reviewed, Fee is warmly praised by all; The Dr Dehn, professor at Heidelberg, highlights the contrast between the previous Fee and today's citizen; Fiore confirms the acuite lift seen by Olson in December. Consequences: letter from Olson to Mrs Dawson of February 28, 1952 reassuring her and Cara
« 6 Students Talk with Mies » : entretie: “6 Students Talk with Mies”: Mies interview by students from the School of Design at North Carolina State College, published in LINE magazine, vol. 2, No. 1, February 1952 — same state and same period as Black Mountain College. LINE magazine, vol. 2, No. 1 (February 1952)
Reçu comme une célébrité, logé au meille: Received as a celebrity, housed at the best hotel, celebrated by architects, academics and American cultural attaché; overflowing classes, morning to evening classes, endless questions, all recorded; he writes to Anni four times, feeling every day the freshness of the profession after thirty years Words: “Tout ce que je dis est une surprise absolue”; “j'utilise plus d'espagnol qu'au Mexique” Atmosphere: Tropical effervescence, student greed, learning happiness Issue: The old master rediscovers the pure joy of the class
Albers sollicite l'archéologue Junius Bi: Albers asked the archaeologist Junius Bird (conversation on 11 March 1952, letter of 23 April 1952), who alerted him: the length of the fabric was also limited by the amount of rollable fabric on the lower bar of the trade. Paracas Necropolis specimen 14 feet 7 inches wide by 47 feet 4 inches long. Consequences: Albers responds by proposing weaving through both ends towards the middle, with insertion of the last wefts to the needle.
De Kooning, prêt à considérer Woman I co: De Kooning, ready to consider Woman I a failure, removed the canvas from his chassis when Schapiro visited him and encouraged him to rework and complete the image. Consequences: La canvas was completed and exhibited at Sidney Janis in 1953.
De Kooning a jugé Woman I ratée, l'a ret: De Kooning judged Woman I missed, removed it from its chassis; Schapiro visits the workshop, convinces him to rework the image and finish it. Atmosphere: Moment of discouragement transformed into decisive revival Issue: The salvation of the work that will make the world renowned of the painter
Anni Albers date et signe à New Haven so: Anni Albers dates and signs to New Haven his technical study proposing that the wide Peruvian fabrics have been woven in several layers folded in accordion on narrow dorsal-banded looms. Date “May, 1952”; conversation of 11 March 1952; visit of Isabel Guernsey on 14 March 1952; letter from Junius Bird of 23 April 1952. Consequences: The essay appeared in On Designing (1961).
Tudor crée Water Music à la New School a: Tudor creates Water Music at New School before returning to Black Mountain; It's probably the work he plays during Theater Piece No. 1. hybrid partition: steam whistle in linear wave, “verser l'eau d'un récipient dans un autre” instruction in calligraphic capitals
Seule avec ses diagrammes, échantillons: Alone with his diagrams, described samples and reading notes, Albers unfolds the argument: yarn counts, layer calculations, Bird objections, response by weaving by both ends towards the middle, last frames placed at the needle at the meeting point. Words: Quotes of O'Neale (“the wefts lie in straight lines such as can be explained only by a wide batten”) and Bird (“length is also limited by the amount of cloth which can be rolled and supported on the lower bar”), discussed point by point. Atmosphere: Workshop-domestic concentration, millimetre paper, scholarly correspondence crosses. Issue: Relive by thought a technical gesture that has disappeared for two millennia.
Réponse à sa lettre mentionnant sa pauvr: Answer to her letter mentioning her poverty: she mentions work scholarships and invites her to a three-day visit. College brochure, 600 acres Consequences: Organization of the journey
Quatre jeunes — deux gays de Rider Colle: Four young people — two gays from Rider College, Roger and Marge (lesbian taciturne at the wheel of his new green Chevy), and Mary Ann Fretz, student of Mary Reed — leave early June 1952; Almost non-stop journey, night spent in the car near the sleeping village of Black Mountain (altitude 2,400 feet), hysterical laughter in front of imaginary ghosts. Green Chevy, insect-splattered windshield, left arm of Brown Marge and white straight, manuscript panel BLACK MOUNTAIN COLLEGE Consequences: Arrival at college in the morning
Arrivée vers 9h : lieu désert entre deux: Arrival around 9am: deserted place between two sessions, only a famelic orange dog crosses the road; Initial disappointment, the college resembles a delapidated summer camp, a former recreational site acquired during the 1940-41 move from the other side of the valley. 9am in the morning, flat wheel near the entrance, vermoulu bench under an apple tree, creosote buildings, insect and bird noises Consequences: First doubt on choice
Une femme en blanc, pieds nus, chemise d: A woman in white, bare feet, man's shirt tied, Mexican pants cream, cigarette at the edge of her lips and empty Mason jar, crosses the road; It's Connie, who says “Nous vous attendions”, invites the group to the coffee on the grilled veranda of the dining room and admits that there was a party the day before. too large man's shirt, dark blond horse tail, Mason jar, thick white cups Consequences: First warm contact; hope felt by Rumaker
Visite : gong rond de dîner, Dinner Bell: Visit: Round Gong Dinner, Dinner Bell Circle, Hazel Frieda Larsen house covered with glycine, Eden Lake, Quiet House stone built by a teacher and student, and the scientific glass building completed but unused because Natasha Goldowski considered it dangerous on its thin metal legs — sometimes used for language or writing lessons. Kudzu imported from Japan against landslides, anti-color kits nailed to rusty streetlights, Mount Mitchell snowed at nearly 7,000 feet Consequences: Rumaker “sent son cœur s'échauffer” for the place
La physicienne, cheffe des programmes sc: La physicist, head of scientific programs, refuses to set foot in the finished structure laid on two posts, and forbids its students to use it, considering it promised to degrease the slope; She briefly taught at Princeton after her post-war immigration. Two metal poles, all-glass tri-level structure Consequences: The building remains almost unused, except for language or writing courses
Rumaker passe l'été chez la famille de R: Rumaker spends the summer with the Roger family: packing lupines and peonies cut at dawn by the father in baskets of peaches shipped by train to Manhattan wholesale markets; then at the Automatic Voting Machine Company; dinners in the huge wood stove kitchen with coffee always simmering. Ice vegetable cellar, old newspapers, peach baskets, afternoon train to New York (over 400 miles), cherry wood ancestor bed of 1860s
Pendant que Roger travaille au drive-in: While Roger is working on the ice cream drive-in, Rumaker is doing auto-stops to the Bemis Point cable ferry and the Chotauqua concerts; he spot a young blond in marine blue blazer always alone at the same ramp of the Amphitheatre and develops a desperate, too fearful crush to approach. Cable ferry on Lake Chautauqua, about 20 miles, Beethoven and Tchaikovsky from the orchestra pit
Rumaker travaille dans l'immense salle d: Rumaker works in the huge galvanoplasty room, facing an old man bulge, soaking dozens of metal straps in boiling acid baths, thousands a day. First week: two pairs of gloves, canvas pants and new working shoes gnawed with acid; acid-resistant wire loop Consequences: Good salary to replace clothes and shoes, pay part of his farm pension and save for Black Mountain
Cinéma en voiture (African Queen, entrée: Cinema by car (African Queen, free entrance thanks to the land rented by the mother of Roger), Genessee beer at Mayville Inn, nude night swims in Chautauqua Lake with friends including two gays, excursions to Chautauqua Gorge and Niagara Falls with Roger parents. Beer Genessee; almost fall in the gorge and on the rocks of the falls
Dans son rapport au président Griswold p: In his report to President Griswold for the year 1951-52 (undated, probably June 1952), Albers judges the program of invited critics “hautement réussi”, proposes to extend it to second and third year students to expose them to various perspectives, and affirms that these critics encourage freedom to learn as important as freedom to teach. typed report, JA Papers
Asawa et Cunningham conçoivent ensemble: Asawa and Cunningham together design the cover of Arts and Architecture magazine with untitled photographs (S.535). Asawa is credited “Ruth Lanier”: she has not yet taken up her maiden name despite Cunningham's advice. June 1952 issue; “Ruth Lanier” credit; pasted photomontage Consequences: Illustrating the time of Asawa to follow the advice of Cunningham on its artist name.
Après près de 600 miles non-stop, les qu: After nearly 600 non-stop miles, the four stopped in the dark near the college's manuscript panel, raised windows and locked doors, scared of imaginary ghosts and laughed to hysteria before sleeping in the car. Atmosphere: thick black, woody, tired, nervous laughter, a few hours of restless sleep Issue: Threshold: the long-awaited arrival begins in fear and exhaustion
Personne en vue ; un chien orange faméli: Person in sight; a famelic orange dog slowly crosses the road and disappears behind the pines; Rumaker tries to justify the vacuum (“c'est entre les sessions”); Others seem to believe in a crazy race; They tacitly decide to wait, embarrassed. Words: “There's hope” (“Il y a de l'espoir”), says Rumaker in view of the dog; “Peut-être que c'est parce qu'on est entre les sessions” Atmosphere: Chirring and rumbling insects, bird screaming, dust, soporous place, disappointment Issue: Doubt: Is college worth 600 miles?
Une femme en blanc pieds nus, cigarette: A woman in barefoot white, giant cigarette, jar in her hand, crosses the road avoiding stones; Marge orders Rumaker to catch it; it rushes, apologizes for the number of visitors; Connie smiles with her deep smile and invites them to coffee. Words : Margin : “Grab her… the last live one we catch all day” (“Attrape-la… la dernière créature vivante qu'on attrapera de la journée”) ; Connie: “I'm Connie. We've been expecting you”; “We had a party last night” (“Nous avons fait la fête cette nuit”) Atmosphere: Sun, dust, warm smile contrasting with desolation Issue: First human contact: the place opens
Pendant que Connie dépose son bocal de l: While Connie puts down his milk jar, the group drinks coffee in large white cups and discovers the lake, white Studies Building and snowy Mount Mitchell; Rumaker is still waiting to meet Connie's giant husband. Words: Connie learns the lake's name is Lake Eden Atmosphere: An opening perspective, fogs rising, first appeasement Issue: The landscape buys up dilapidated buildings
Connie montre la maison de Hazel Larsen,: Connie shows Hazel Larsen's house, Quiet House, unused science building and tells of Natasha Goldowski's refusal; Rumaker is silently worried about rusty collar kits; Connie reassures him on the snakes that “s'occupent de leurs affaires”. Words : “There are rattlesnakes and copperheads… but they mind their own business” (“Il y a des cascabels et des mocassins… mais ils s'occupent de leurs affaires”) Atmosphere : Rising heat and humidity, thick Kudzu, smiling anxiety Issue : Rumaker goes from doubt to attachment : “mon cœur s'échauffe pour ce lieu”
Chaque soir, Rumaker, à quelques rampes: Every evening, Rumaker, at a few distance ramps, steals eyes from the young blond in navy blue blazer with golden buttons, always alone in the same place; Too terrified to approach. Atmosphere: Beethoven and Tchaikovsky in the night, feverish and hopeless crush, security of fantasy Issue: Desire under terror, sexual loneliness before BMC
En juillet, la famille Tworkov (les deux: In July, the Tworkov family (the two girls Hermine and Helen) brings new vitality; in August arrives Franz Kline, “lui-même un cristal”. M.C. Richards writes the words of an “French Farce Based on a Wagnerian Opera” in which almost the whole school participates. The late August farewells are sad but the school is ready for the fall and a new contingent of students. play: A French Farce Based on Wagnerian Opera, lyrics by M.C. Richards Consequences: secret end of a phase; the school is redefined
Soir de côtelettes de porc en session d': Soir of pork chops in summer session. Helen asks Hermine to keep a share; Connie secretly asks Charles to put aside a rib for Kate. Hermine, arriving slightly late, finds nothing to keep, goes to the kitchen, discovers the plate covered on the shelf above the stove and takes the riblet — Kate's. Connie arrives with Kate on the hip, whispers to Charles; Olson gets up, grabs Kate with a gesture, the laying on the palm of her right hand, arm stretched — the child nearly eleven feet from the ground — and beugles like an Ahab/Melville: WHO VOLATED THE PORC COAST OF HIS CITY? Silence of grave on the porch. plate covered with another inverted on the metal shelf above the stove; baby at ~11 feet from the ground, near the beams; grilled porch view on lake and mountains Consequences: Hermine will ask Dawson for silence seven years later; Olson apparently never knew
Jack Tworkov, sa femme Wally et leurs fi: Jack Tworkov, his wife Wally and their daughters Hermine (~11 years) and Helen (~9 years) come a month in July 1952; Franz Kline is expected in August. girls about 11 and 9 years old
Incident au dîner que « toute l'école a: Incident at dinner that “toute l'école a vu”; That night Olson and Connie, alone in their South Lodge apartment, exchanged a hilarity contained — she knew the Dahlberg variation of 1940 and Dahlberg had thus taken his revenge, twelve years later, because of the impractical food honor system of Black Mountain. Olson still angry, laughing while cursed “that son of a bitch”; reference to the last line of Maximus' Letter 16 Consequences: Olson will never talk about it: the incident evoked Connie, their daughter Kate, his departure with Betty and Charles Peter, and then the death of Betty
Le lendemain d'une fête où Elaine de Koo: The day after a party where Elaine Kooning soaked hundreds of pennies in gold paint and sowed them on the lawn, and where Nancy and Joan attached balloons to the trees, Elaine painted two white grapefruits with seams and the Spaulding brand. The next day, Vicente (Elaine? — pitcher) on the mountain, Franz on the stick... Franz slides a grapefruit to the pitcher on the pretext of a mound conference. Everyone knows except Pavia; it strikes — burst. After cleaning: “All right, let's play.” Franz: “Just a second, I want to talk to Vincente.” Gold pennies, balloons, painted grapefruits with brand Spaulding
Années plus tard, buts chargés, Dawson a: Years later, goals loaded, Dawson on the stick, Franz launches. He yells at the voltigators to step back, they don't listen: he strikes over the left voltigator, triple from the inside. Next handle, the voltigators retreat; Franz : “Aw hit the fuckin' ball.” Dawson holds the hand at breast height in the centre of the marble; Franz places the ball exactly there, Dawson hits it over the center and marks by looking at Franz, which pretends to have enough.
Repas de côtelettes, joie générale. Conn: Chop dinner, general joy. Connie enters with Kate on the hip, whispers in the ear of Charles. Olson rises, pulls Kate out of Connie with a gesture, sits on her right palm, arm stretched vertically — eleven feet from the ground — and beautifies her Melvillian question. Silence of grave. Words: “WHO HAD STOLEN HIS DAUGHTER'S PORK CHOP?” — “Tu ne peux le dire à personne, il l'entendra, il sera encore fâché !” (Hermine, 1959) Atmosphere: summer evening, mountains far away, smell of chops, then vertigo and silence Issue: the community's honor against a child's lie; the anger of a giant
Après le dîner et l'incident public, le: After dinner and public incident, the couple alone; exchange of eyes, each keeping a straight face laughing; it knows the 1940 version; Olson still angry laughs by cursed Dahlberg. Words: Olson breathe “that son of a bitch” laughing Atmosphere: Hilarity gone after the blow Issue: Twelve years after Gloucester, Dahlberg is avenged; the incident will seal the silence of Olson for life
Elaine et des amis artistes vont se baig: Elaine and friends artists will bathe naked in the moonlight; She writes to Ernestine Lassaw that her hair has not been as clear and her skin as brown for years. letter to Ernestine Lassaw; buying a refrigerator for her mother replacing the cooler, leaving her “dans son état naturel — fauchée”
Elaine achève un article sur Buckminster: Elaine completes an article on Buckminster Fuller; After a drink party with Burgoyne Diller while she had to watch her paintings for an ARTnews article, she only has “que des plumes dans la tête, dont (elle s'est servie) pour épousseter Bucky” left. article ARTnews on Diller reported in drinking
De 20 h 30 à 22 h 30, Cage, juché sur un: De 8:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m., Cage, strewn on a staircase, spoke about the relationship of music to Zen Buddhism while a film was being projected, that dogs barked through the scene, that twelve people danced without rehearsal, with prepared piano, whistles, baby screams, and Edith Piaf's records passed at double speed on a turn of the century machine. 8.30-10.30 p.m.; escapeau; 12 dancers; prepared piano; Edith Piaf Double Speed Discs Consequences: Considered the First American Happening
Après le concert de clôture (Neuvième de: After the closing concert (Beethoven's Ninth), Rumaker does auto-stop; A young man sexually assaults him, pushes him back, then by revenge accelerates to 90 and then 100 miles/hour on the country road. 100 miles/hour; rolling tires on the gravel of the farm driveway Consequences: Terror; immense relief by finding the gravel of the farm
Vers la mi-août, par le frais automne pr: Towards mid-August, by the early autumn cool of the New York West (leaves already blushing), letter from Connie Olson: the application for a scholarship is accepted, arrival expected in early September for the fall quarter. Mid-August, sharp chill in the air Consequences: Joy: leave the clothes with acid and go south
Un soir d'août 1952, Cage conduit le The: One evening in August 1952, Cage led Theater Piece No. 1, widely regarded as the first Happening, bringing together almost all performing arts: dance, music, poetry. The author recalls that this event was only one of hundreds of performances in college. appeared “comme un champignon” in historiography Consequences: Becomes the iconic event by which we reduce performance to BMC
Un soir d'août 1952, performance sans no: One evening in August 1952, unnamed performance designed by Cage in the day and performed the same evening: poetry readings (Olson, Richards), dance (Cunningham), piano music prepared (Tudor), paintings of Rauschenberg suspended from the ceiling, discs played, film projection. No script, rehearsal or costumes; each activity started and ended according to time schedules set by Cage. It would gain a reputation as the first Happening by the end of the decade. projectionist score: “Begin at 16 min. play freely until 23 min.”; College calendar simply notes “a 'concert' by John Cage” on August 16, 1952, possible date Consequences: considered retroactively as the first Happening; established by Michael Kirby in 1965, rather via Cage courses at the New School (Kaprow, Brecht, Hansen, Higgins)
Aucune photo de l'événement n'existe ; u: No photo of the event exists; A single score of Cage remains. Francine's Plessix diary: Cage on a scale talked about Zen music and Buddhism as a movie passed, dogs barked, Merce danced, a prepared piano played, whistles blew, babies shouted, coffee was served by four boys in white, Edith Piaf's records were fast-paced on a turn-of-the-century machine. Weinrib : Cunningham pursued by a dog, Rauschenberg playing popular records of the 1920-30s, Olson distributing a poem written in parts and making the audience read up, Richards reciting Edna St. Vincent Millay from the top of a ladder. Litz: all evening in French, Richards arriving “à cheval… une structure mobile”. Williams: projection of hand painted 35 mm slides and coloured glued gelatins. Cernovich: projection of fragments of a silent film in black and white. Challenged projection surface: Rauschenberg screen, ceiling, or White Painting (Four Panel). start time noted 20:30 in the Plessix log; Cage speaks until 4:30 pm according to the same newspaper Consequences: mythical status of the event due to the documentary vacuum
L'été 1952 est retenu pour la première d: The summer of 1952 was selected for the premiere of Theater Piece No. 1 by Cage and for its recognition, assisted by the White Paintings of Rauschenberg, of silence as a key to 4'33''. Mr. C. Richards drew in 1989 a plan of the play for William Fetterman, including what is believed to be the Painting of Kline; Most memories instead place the White Painting (Four Panel) suspended from the ceiling
Franz Kline est invité à enseigner la pe: Franz Kline was invited to teach painting in August 1952; Dawson tells him a very emotional farewell to the station with Nancy.
Wolpe, ancien étudiant du Bauhaus enseig: Wolpe, former student of the Bauhaus college teacher, “proteste” against chaos and exit; Others find this “assez ennuyeux”, “une expérience intéressante”, or admit that we weren't supposed to understand literally. no photographs or films of performance exist; the records contradict each other because the arrangement of the seats prohibits a single point of view Consequences: the contradictory accounts circulate
Cage, sur un escabeau, parle deux heures: Cage, on a escapeau, speaks two hours of music and Zen while film, barking dogs, twelve improvising dancers, prepared piano, whistles, screaming babies and Edith Piaf accelerated doubles. Atmosphere: Jubilatory and Simultaneous Chaos Issue: Official Birth of American Happening
Après la Neuvième de Beethoven, un jeune: After Beethoven's Ninth, a young man stops him and pelates him immediately; Rumaker refuses dryly; Crazy with rage, the driver crushes the accelerator up to 100 miles/hour to scare and punish it; He finally puts it at the gravel of the farm. Atmosphere: Night Terror, Screaming Tires, Black Road to Jamestown Issue: Award of Desire Denied in 50s America

Dans « An Open Letter to Bernard Leach »: In “An Open Letter to Bernard Leach”, published in Craft Horizons in May 1953, Wildenhain challenges the notion of pivot root: it no longer exists in our time and probably never existed; American potters cannot take root by imitating Sung pottery or copying the Japanese rural way of life — the conscious imitation of works alien to the spirit of their generation would produce only questionable expeditions and turn potters into dilettants or fakes. Craft Horizons, May 1953, pp. 43-44. Consequences: Public riposte with Leach credo, rooted in Wildenhain Bauhaus experience.
Carolyn Brown danse huit heures ou plus: Carolyn Brown dances eight hours or more a day with Cunningham; the intensity art/life/process experienced with Merce to Black Mountain has redirected his life. dancing “from morning into the night” appeared “right”; choreographic notes by Untitled Solo taken at the college in 1953
Dawson écrit à Franz pour demander à ven: Dawson writes to Franz to ask to come during the spring holidays and sleep on a camp bed at the bottom of his loft; Franz answers to come; Dawson announces the news to her mother; He leaves but must shorten the stay. Camp bed requested, loft background Consequences: Early return for interview with judge at Asheville
En déménageant vers un nouveau logement,: By moving to a new home, his friends come together to paint his apartment; wall paintings are originals offered by friends. original paintings offered by friends; painting the apartment by friends
Janis expose les toiles Women ; l'articl: Janis exposes Women's paintings; Hess's article in ARTnews, illustrated with Rudy Burckhardt's photos, appears in coincidence with the exhibition. Woman I enters MoMA before the end of the year. Photos of Burckhardt taken in 1950-1952 documenting six states of Woman I. Consequences: La series and the debate it triggers make Kooning internationally known in a few years.
La photo montre Elaine assise en arrière: La photo shows Elaine sitting in the background and Willem standing in the foreground, sure of it; She poses as an appendix to the husband, as to attest her heterosexuality, in a context of presses accusing contemporary art of homosexuality. Woman I was largely executed in this East Hampton residence. Consequences: This type of image shapes the public image of the couple and contrasts with photos of Elaine alone in his studio.
L'exposition confirme de Kooning comme r: The exhibition confirms Kooning as renegade in the eyes of the abstract scene; violent reactions of the critic (Crehan, Geist, Fitzsimmons). A painter claims to be unable to paint after seeing the paintings; a dozen others call them “profondément troublants”, The Woman “horreur” and “muse maléfique” Consequences: Woman I purchased by the Museum of Modern Art
Dix jours après la clôture de l'expositi: Ten days after the closing of the Janis exhibition, Kooning's first retrospective opens in Boston. Ten days after the Janis show closed
Elaine dit à Josef Albers vouloir écrire: Elaine tells Josef Albers to write about him for Art News in the “The Artist Paints a Picture” series and cover his color theories. Albers replied: “I will make some paintings that express my color philosophy. I will call you when I have some work for you to see.” Two weeks later he invited him to his home: he did not have a workshop and worked in his living room, where he made a large number of small paintings on one square paper in a square of another color: “I will call this series 'Homage to the Square'”. Come with her to photograph, Rudy Burckhardt remembers that Albers pursued her around the table to kiss her, at Rudy's great amusement. Small formats on paper, square in square of different color; no studio, living room work; two weeks of waiting; chase around the table. Consequences: Public birth of the Homage to the Square series and article “Albers Paints a Picture” (1950 according to table, 1953 according to preface).
Le MoMA présente « 15 Americans », inclu: The MoMA presents “15 Americans”, including Kiesler and Dickinson, two major artists approaching 60, more or less unknown to the art audience. Consequences: Kiesler shows his largest Galaxy on irregular axes.
Arrivé en Amérique en 1926, Kiesler expo: Arrived in America in 1926, Kiesler exhibited his painting and sculpture for the first time; known vaguely as an architect especially for the “Floating City” at the Paris 1925 International Exhibition of Decorative Arts, he never received a building order in the United States and rarely exhibited his extraordinary models (Space-House 1933, Endless House 1950).
Kiesler, arrivé en Amérique en 1926 et j: Kiesler, who arrived in America in 1926 and was never commissioned to build in the United States, showed his painting and sculpture for the first time, including two large galaxies. Two monumental galaxies exhibited Consequences: public revelation of previously unpublished works
Wes Huss distribue à Rumaker le rôle du: Wes Huss distributes to Rumaker the role of the Married in Lorca's Blood Wedding — far from his only previous role, Oogie Pringle in the high school graduation play, A Date with Judy, where he even sang. Consequences: Rumaker feels it is progressing
Dawson rencontre « sa plus belle fille »: Dawson meets “sa plus belle fille” in January; His little knocks on his door, sign of his desire, almost breaks his heart; nights of love and sleep on her dirty sheets and her little mattress, stunned with pride, guilt, tenderness, fear and exaltation. Small mattress, dirty sheets
Pour son article de janvier 1953, Elaine: For his January 1953 article, Elaine interviewed Diller while Rudy Burckhardt photographed; They accompany her to a charming neighborhood bar where we eat smoked eels and where Diller chain the boilermakers. At the end, she proposes to correct the article; he reports that his merchant Rose Fried warned him: “Watch out for that Elaine de Kooning. She's one smart cookie and she's out to cut your throat” — Elaine laughs, rather flattered to be “one smart cookie”. Diller, highly respected artists for her important position at WPA, suggests some minor relevant corrections that she incorporates. Last conversation: he constantly turns away his face to hide his abdominal pain grimaces; Soon after, he died of cirrhosis of the liver. Smoked eel, boilermakers served one after the other, couch full of burnt cigarette holes, Diller couple compared to a couple of Scott Fitzgerald, beautiful and tall, both drinking excessively but in perfect manners.
Trois architectes chiliens posent aux cô: Three Chilean architects pose alongside Josef Albers who came to give his Curso Preliminar to the PUC; the photo is kept by the Josef and Anni Albers Foundation. Issue: La meets between master Bauhaus and young Chilean modernity.
Un jour, trois détails retiennent l'atte: One day, three details attract the attention of Albers: a sweeper collecting leaves with a long branch of harmonious palm; interlaced metal rings preventing walking on the lawn; a mason carefully installing a glass box against a rough stone wall — a contrast that makes him enthusiastic. Words: He exclaims on the richness of the contrast of materials: “la fragilité et la translucidité du verre avec la rugosité et la masse de la pierre”. Atmosphere: Daily walk between residence and university; Albers curiosity for ordinary design rather than its Bauhaus past. Issue: The eye of Albers transforms the street into perception.
Le gong du repas retentit ; cinq minutes: The meal gong sounds; five minutes later there is nothing; Around the poker tables, we used to crochet the cold locker to find a steak; Olson, 2.01 m, sometimes participating, excused by its intense hunger Atmosphere: Joyous Famine and Complicit Delinquency Issue: The giant body of the hungry rector facing the material collapse of the college
Le pianiste attitré, sans virtuosité, a: The dedicated pianist, without virtuosity, disgusted the dancers of the play; Cunningham presses Tudor — busy preparing a Wolpe concert — to come once to play “Banjo”; Tudor executes and electrifies support. Words: Cunningham to Tudor: “because they don't know what I'm doing” — “I don't know myself” Atmosphere: sudden revelation, electricity (“quelque chose d'électrique, fantastique”) Issue: converting company to Cunningham vision
Après des jours de lutte sur la musique: After days of struggle on Christian Wolff's music, physically and musically impossible, Cunningham drops to the ground as a sign of abandonment; Tudor smiles kindly and proposes to continue still; They can do it. Words: Tudor: “Well, it's clearly impossible. But we're going right ahead and do it anyway.” Atmosphere: despair and serene complicity Issue: the birth of a work against the impossible
Danse plus longue que la partition : Tud: Dance longer than the score: Tudor replays the piece from the beginning, only advances by a sentence and a half when the dance ends — it stops net. Words : Cunningham : “he stopped. That was the end . . . and the result was the result.” Atmosphere : serenity of chance assumed Issue : independence of music and dance
Pendant le grand nettoyage des écuries,: During the great cleaning of the stables, the herd escapes through the fences; Olson and almost the entire community run into pastures by grinding to gather it. Atmosphere: pastoral farce, both hideous and hilarious Issue: The collapse of the college's agricultural dreams
Wolpe, mis en rapport par Irma Jurist, i: Wolpe, reported by Irma Jurist, interviews in the Automat a young man without experience who has just obtained his B.A.; they like each other; Schram, who dreamed of seeing Black Mountain, goes down to visit two days, discovers the monumental figure of Olson and the fervor of all, but does not follow. Words: Schram: “I guess they were seizing at straws”; “a company convent” Atmosphere: New York brewery, lucid despair of college looking for a savior Issue: the ultimate search for a magic administrator and its failure
Il crée sa première danse : se tenir deb: He creates his first dance: standing, the moment after falling; rehearsals contusion its basins; He realizes he's trying to destroy himself and must stop. Words: “je me souviens d'avoir des os du bassin meurtris... j'essayais juste de me tuer.” Atmosphere: physical violence, sudden lucidity Issue: art at risk of the body
Un soir délicieusement parfumé, Rumaker: A deliciously scented evening, Rumaker asks Ellen if a connection is possible; she only replies that she will be in her room later; When night comes, he knocks at his window, gently calls, discovers the empty room; It feels mistaken, pride hurt, and slowly goes up the road to his study Words: Ellen, eyes slipping in such a dark night: “elle serait dans sa chambre plus tard” Atmosphere: Scented evening, black night, smile of Ellen where you can read everything Issue: Sexual ambiguity of Rumaker, protective malice of Ellen
Wes lit à voix haute toute l'adaptation: Wes reads aloud all the adaptation of the “Grand Inquisiteur”; Duck frankly demolishes it: transcribing is not enough, the drama remains at Dostoevski; Wes confirms with a flat and passive politeness; the rest of the class maintains a pitiful tolerance towards the novice. Words: Duck: no advance, no variation; Where are you in all this? Atmosphere: Polished shine, intimate burn. Issue: First rite of passage: the literary vanity of Rumaker sprayed.
Rumaker ouvre la porte pour lire au sole: Rumaker opens the door to read in the sun and discovers a giant black snake curly on the ramp, in full motion, shiny new scales, dead skin falling to the ground several floors below. Atmosphere: graceful ritual, spring light, quiet fascination. Issue: Image of renewal when Olson returns — moulted and rebirth.
Olson lit les Pisan Cantos, se moque de: Olson reads the Pisan Cantos, mocks “the moon is my pinup”, brandishes the page to the black ideogram LING, asks who can read it; Rumaker random “harmony”, Olson asks again, then “Sensibility” — “Bingo!” Words: Olson: “Bingo!”; On Pound: Ez' plays hip with the GI slang, he doesn't buy. Atmosphere : Sudden game, victory of the shy. Issue: First recognition of Rumaker by the master.
Coupe du kudzu et du bambou aux bolo kni: Cut of kudzu and bamboo with bolo knives; during a break, Olson asks what Rumaker reads; on the Carson McCullers answer, it removes it from an “Saturday night” and returns to tall grasses; Rumaker blushes, says he agrees, but will continue in secret. Words: Olson: McCullers is “Saturday night”. Atmosphere: Sweat, manual complicity, brief judgment. Issue: Conflict between the master's law and the student's secret affinities.
Après le lavage du déjeuner, Rumaker bal: After breakfast washing, Rumaker sweeps, serpilles, puts the tables playing the classics at full volume; he sometimes gives up everything to dance in free form; Outside, in the grass in front of wild roses, Connie and Kate, then Mary Fiore, Bea with David, Dorothea with her baby, listen and chat, like an informal concert; Connie thanked him several times. Words: Connie warmly thanks for the music; Olson then mocks the choice of discs. Atmosphere: Warm kitchen, music overflowing on the lake and the road, bright afternoon, little joy in routine. Issue: Simple happiness immediately bitten by the jealousy of Olson.
Par un crépuscule agréable après souper,: By a pleasant twilight after supper, Rumaker descends from the Studies and hears by far the laughter of Olson on the water; Olson, avachi in a canned chair, legs apart, shouts instructions to Connie who clumsily pushes at the pole the rowless boat where Kate, solemn, looks at her mother; Rumaker wants to help but something stops it; exasperated, red throat, Connie turns back her skirts and jumps in muddy water to the knees to pull the boat through the reeds; Olson continues to laugh and slide apart to its neighbor behind the rusty grilling. Words: Instructions shouted by Olson to Connie (not reported textually). Atmosphere: Summer dusk, thundering laughter, muddy water, thick reeds. Issue: La mocking domination of Charles on Connie, in public, in front of the paralyzed narrator.
Jorge pose le disque rapporté de Detroit: Jorge poses Detroit's reported record; Olson vaulted on the phonograph, still, glued ear, face of child or deaf discovering recorded music; at the end of the furrow he demands the name, then rejoining it; then dance cut after cut with Arlene Franklin, crouch high and soft, small steps near the phonograph. Words: “Who is that? Who is that?” — “Qui est-ce ?” Atmosphere: Wonder of a giant; It's a pinched trumpet sound, brand new. Issue: The man of the verb seized by an incredible sound.
Discussion sur la party ; Rumaker lâche: Discussion on the party; Rumaker loose that Charles danced “comme une baleine”; the hard look of Olson piercing it; then a little smile half-amused half-against, a dry punch at the biceps, “Oh you!”, and Olson goes to his mailboxes. Words: “Charles, you danced last night like... like a whale!” Atmosphere: Instant panic, then painful relief; Ego hurt stronger than the arm. Issue: Language care — even in conversation.
Après-midi gris et froid ; café au poêle: Grey and cold afternoon; coffee in the pan; Kline threads discrete and narquoise stories around the table at the metal tray; everyone hangs on his lips; Guston, the Roman senator, stays back. The next day they leave — forever. Atmosphere: Heat stove, cult of the teller, already legend of BMC. Issue: The disappointed hope of a return of Kline teaching.
Après-midi pluvieux ; à court de textes,: Rainy afternoon; Short of texts, Olson makes read Rumaker, which reads in a shy voice his news of South Philly (the innkeeper and egg yolk); Olson explodes, rips the warmer, shouts that he is not his psychologist; Rumaker shrinks, without skin, reading pity and contempt in eyes; he thinks of his mother, the priest, the “Michel Pange” of Madame; Olson concludes coldly. Words: “I'm not here to be a psychologist to you!”; “Quit bein' so much on the side of the angels, Rumaker”; “I can't help you because I don't love you.” Atmosphere: Rain on windows, pines, valley away, throat tied, feeling choking. Issue: Birth of a writer by burning; conflict between father and son queer.
Olson arrête Rumaker sur la route, décla: Olson stops Rumaker on the road, says the text on Bartleby turns it on to the point of wanting to return to Melville; draft ideas: flyer, brochure, printing workshop, contributions; “Mike, you must stop hiding your talents under a bushel basket!”; Rumaker baldly, stunned by so much enthusiasm for what the text is worth Words: “Bartleby is Melville!”; “That story is talking about Melville's soul!”; “il fallait cesser de cacher ses talents sous le boisseau” Atmosphere: Magic of Recognition; Rumaker walks on a cloud for days Issue: the transition from shadow to light for Rumaker, start of mentoring
Enthronée sur une chaise cannée dans son: Enthroned on a canned chair in her purple regiment, she tells the separate rooms (white cover, black cover), the oblivion of children on the park bench (“Herman! Where are the children?”), and the ritournelle in front of the painting of the bay of Naples, cane brandie Words: “See how the little boats swing to and fro, to and fro...”; “Herman! Where are the children?” Atmosphere: intimate, malicious; Olson gallant and proud; Rumaker presenting to the visitor, blushing to the root of the hair when Olson boasts its essay Issue: the great Melville made alive by the blood of his blood, in front of his college readers
Un matin d'été, Rumaker ose monter sans: One summer morning, Rumaker dares to go up without an invitation to talk about his graduation project; through the mosquito net he sees Olson barely awake, cloth in the thighs, hand walked on his belly and pubis; his fists freeze in the air; The memory of his own father naked at the dawn of Philadelphia seized him Atmosphere: silence of the house, heart in the throat, embarrassed fascination, vertigo of the intimate Issue: the master seen as a father; no look
Un matin d'hiver, le père a dormi trop t: One winter morning, the father slept too late; Repeated horns in the dirt road; The father pops up in underwear, leans on his son who sticks his stockings, throws up the broken window, the iced air on the child's back, shouts that he arrives; Joe Harper launches an acute valve from the car; the child has seen, once, his father's black pubic Words: Joe Harper's sharp and mocking valve Atmosphere: icy cold, gray dawn, hangover, shame and tenderness mixed Issue: root of the paternal figure that Rumaker projects on Olson
Après Niagara vu à Asheville, Olson, plu: After Niagara saw at Asheville, Olson, more animated than usual, admiring and lubricated glow in the eyes, speaks of Monroe with verva to the boys who saw the film; later he will comment that she had only has-beens Words: “What did she ever get but has-beens?… Nobody up to her.” Atmosphere: hot male connivance Issue: reveals the ordinary sexism of progressive genius
Eric conduit Rumaker et Merrill du collè: Eric leads Rumaker and Merrill from college to farm. Natasha radiant makes visit the house (summer cottage look) ; Madame stays in her room, moaning through the thin walls. Natasha shouts “C'est l'heure de la traite !”, sends Eric to search for the bucket in French, walks the guests on the ground, designates the red browned cow grazing in thick grass, exclaims “Rouge-ah !”, rushes onto the grass, kneels and binds the animal's neck, whispers softness in Russian in the freting ear. Words: “Rouge-ah ! Rouge-ah !”; “Elle est jeune mais c'est une bonne laitière. Nous avons assez de lait pour nous, pour le fromage et le fromage blanc, et je vais faire du beurre — et du petit-lait pour les poules. Et nous l'avons eue à bon prix. Ô ma chérie Rougea, tu es si précieuse pour moi.”; “Vous voyez que je ne pouvais l'appeler que Rougea, 'rouge' en russe.” Atmosphere: thick sunset, full sun on the west hills, already dark slopes, bright autumn air; voice of Natasha breaking with emotion, rauque, resilient like that of Simone Signoret; Natasha in robust peasant figure, unbridled energy; patient and perplexed look at the cow. Issue: The happiness recovered from Natasha out of the shadow of Olson, mixed with sadness: her energy is lacking in college.
Natasha demande aux deux étudiants s'ils: Natasha asks the two students if they have already dealt; No — in college, the milking was mechanical with Mantovani music on agricultural radio. It shows the gesture in its quick and clever way, demands that everyone try; Rumaker squats, massages silky teats, hears hot jets hitting the bucket, smells the cow's velvet against her forehead, smells of alfalfa and animal heat in cold air. Words: “D'abord il faut traire la vache”; She would show, all had to try in turn. Atmosphere: Cold grass, twilight, animal warmth, sensual pleasure and wonder of the neophyte. Issue: Passage of sensual initiation, contrasts with the mechanization of the college.
Dîner simple et copieux de produits de R: Simple and hearty dinner of Rougea products; Madame daigne appears at the table, more kind to Rumaker only to remove the last gossip from the school; she questions him in French with the Russian accent, your falsely indifferent; he responds as best in his French to the Russian accent learned from her, alone to understand it; Natasha, amused, dominates the table of her flow of projects and knowledge of the earth, as she dominated her evenings at Meadows Inn. Words: Madam questioning the college's actions in an innocent and greedy way. Atmosphere: Warm, cheerful cuisine of Natasha overflowing, hidden melancholy of Madame, evil of the country of Black Mountain. Issue: La nostalgia of Madame reveals what the college was for its inhabitants; Natasha energy is missing in school.
Tocs à la porte à l'aube ; Merrill ignor: Tocs at the door at dawn; Merrill ignores; mute Rumaker; Jack pushes the door, discovers the two men tied on the mattress near the stove; barks the order, insists, fixes the swelling of the duvet, sharp look at Rumaker, exits by slamming the door; Rumaker gently pleads Merrill to get up, in vain — Merrill renders sleepi Words: “Gillespie, you know you're on a work crew this morning?” / “You coming?” / “Yeah, yeah, in a few minutes” Atmosphere: morning cold, fear, gay tension/military maschaism Issue: the upcoming expulsion of Merrill, fear of unveiling
Merrill, perfectionniste, planifie des j: Merrill, perfectionist, plan days, buys from Asheville, kitchen, sets the table; baby David lying; we sit down; Wes enters without a word, falls into an armchair, opens a book on Brecht and bed, cross leg; small talk about dishes; Rumaker cannot swallow; no one names Wes; departure without comment; Rumaker imagines the continuation after their departure Words: chatter about the taste and success of dishes; Theatrical silence of Wes Atmosphere: painful social comedy, medusa mute in the armchair Issue: lesson in passive resistance Quaker, silent sorting of Wes, blinding of Merrill
Après le souper, tous trois entassés par: After supper, all three piled among the jars and yeast; jar after brew jar; Bert's knee presses that of Rumaker; playful caresses begin, Virginia immobilizes behind her cross glasses observing them with perplexed fun; She goes away by titubling; Bert slams the foot door; They fall on each other. Atmosphere: heat, rising intoxication, smallness, annoying third-party look Issue: The hope of a love Rumaker, immediately disappointed by Bert's avoidance
La classe entière vient laver les fenêtr: La whole class comes to wash the farm windows in thank you for the McCarthy audience views at Doyle and Claire; Rumaker at the top of a ladder that oscupates, wipes the row of windows, laughing; Olson down, raising your head, delighted, smiling. Atmosphere: light, complicit, precarious height Issue: Ambiguous gesture of gratitude in the hierarchy that despises Doyle
Après le dîner de poulet, la danseuse gr: After the chicken dinner, the big, skinny, turquoise dancer, facing the public, performs micro-movements of hands and feet on a music of sounds; the audience applauds timidly; Olson applauds strongly, red face, grinning with pleasure, enthusiastically commenting on the modesty and accuracy of gestures. Words: enthusiastic comments by Olson on the sharp and precise smallness of the movements Atmosphere: concentration, motionless face to read in all senses, revision Issue: Olson recognizes in this tenuous dance something of itself
Après Pool of Sacrifice monté par Wes, O: After Pool of Sacrifice mounted by Wes, Olson climbs to the distribution, slapping Rumaker playfully by mocking him on his priestly role; Rumaker pique dreamed that he had no other models, including Olson. Words: “And you—you played it like a Catholic priest!” Atmosphere: public ironic picnic, intimate injury Issue: The authority of Olson over those he loves; the need for Rumaker approval
Heure après heure, la danseuse en justau: Hour after hour, the justaucorp dancer rubs her back to the pillar like a pussy folding and turning, the air ecstasy, while Rumaker sweeps and pushes the cart around her; Sometimes a weak smile of excuse; Mary Fiore tries to talk to her, she's only responding to dance. Words: Mary speculates with sympathy that there is something else in her home: an impossible dream, a edge of madness perhaps Atmosphere: fascination worried, concentrated loneliness Issue: The price of vocation without talent
Après la fête surprise à Streamside, Mer: After the surprise party in Streamside, Merce arrives late, gray face, hungover eyes; no breakfast granted by the Malrey cooker; penaud smile, immediate apology, and he immediately blows the room in exercises; Paul, a little grey too, gets there with so much energy. Atmosphere: the day after the party, good mood tired Issue: Professionalism despite everything from the great choreographer
Après le souper et la vaisselle, chacun: After supper and dishes, each comes back in costume; Pat and Michael are waiting for the dramatic moment to enter; they dance together in circles, then the men pass Pat from arm to arm on the 78 turns; Malrey as a witch grabs Michael for a foxtrot, its cone nose stinging his cheeks, its slippery glasses; Rumaker supports a toge to pose in Bacchus; Karen Karnes Amazonian and naked in Ophelia closes the paintings on the raft; Wes, stiff and agitated, shuns Pat through the kitchen door Atmosphere: candle shadow, sizzling discs, sacrilegious excitement and giddiness Issue: Liberation of ex-Catholics; desire (Pat/Wes, David/Mary Ann); only black-white couple from the South
Réveil anxieux avant l'heure, à peine dé: Anxiety awakening before the hour, barely lunch, cafés and Home Run in chain, the usual soothing landscape (lake, hills, snowy Mt Mitchell) does no effect; Dorothea sits in front, reassures and refocuss on the concrete: shave; He goes up to the large bath of the dormitory of the attic of South Lodge, walks long in the hills; Mary meets him on his way to lunch and booster Words: “Que dois-tu faire maintenant ? — Me raser. — Eh bien, fais-le.” Atmosphere: nerves, loneliness in the early morning, self-care found Issue: passage from the apprentice sweeper to the writer who appears
Fee lit avec assurance dans sa voix fort: Fee reads confidently in his slightly stuttering loud voice; Rumaker crosses its part; relief rather than echoes; in a corner, Wolpe chats with Charles, looks at Rumaker in front and launches his diagnosis; Charles fixes it with an exorbity grin of delicious perception, then looks at Rumaker Words: “The trouble with Rumaker is he doesn't know how to lie yet” (The problem with Rumaker is that it doesn't know how to lie yet) Atmosphere: corner of the room, loud voice with strong German accent Issue: the paradoxical key that will release Rumaker to fiction
Pendant le panel, Wolpe mentionne son at: During the panel, Wolpe mentions his atheism; the woman screams her unbelief; Wolpe, bored, pleated basset face, “No, of course not!” slice; fun laughs of the regulars; the woman, mouthless, turns to her neighbors and keeps a frown worried until the end. Words: “You mine ta' tell me you don't believe in Gawd” / “No, of course not!” Atmosphere: Saturday evening, cultural shock Bible Belt vs. college paganism Issue: Frontal confrontation between European atheism and Southern piety.
Le groupe s'attable ; Ma Peak surgit, dé: The group is stable; My Peak arises, designates the Indian, refuses to serve her; Dan Rice objects that it comes from India; My Peak crosses arms, stubbornly; Olson takes it apart, deploys its persuasion, fails; We order takeaway beers and go back to college. Words: “I kin serve evahbody but you” / “But she's from India” / “Look at 'er, black as a nigger” / “Git 'er outa here!” Atmosphere: warmth, bliss of the group, impotence against the law Issue: La college bubble bursts: even the charm of Olson can't fight legal racism.
Après deux sets au Blue Note, argent épu: After two sets at the Blue Note, the group left for the Mercedes; by the glass, Holiday caught a break, garenia with hair, gin and Slim Jim; They come in, women shy in Booth; Rumaker goes to the bar, beating heart; she tease (“college boy?”), regrets not knowing the words of “My Funny Valentine”; quarter in the jukebox; She sits behind him, says “Sing”, he starts, she takes over and sings in her right ear; It remains petrified. Words: “You a college boy?”; “I've had heartburn all day and haven't eaten a thing—Gimme one of them Slim Jims”; “You know the words?”; “Sing” Atmosphere: snow outdoors, empty and dull bar, gin, gin and spicy jerky, stealthy and magical intimacy Issue: The humanized idol in an ordinary place — echo the previously failed poem, revenge of the coming writing.
Cornelia en tenue de dimanche attend dev: Cornelia in Sunday uniform awaits in front of the dining hall; Rumaker invites her to the front; she refuses laughing, “Naw, naw, naw”, climbs to the back; Rumaker joke without understanding; Mary silent, she understood; Cornelia dropped off in its black quarter. Words : “Don't be silly, Cornelia… there's plenty room” / “Naw, naw, naw… I'll be perfectly fine back here” Atmosphere : sunny Sunday, naïve good mood on one side, caution on the other Issue : La segregation comes to benevolence — Rumaker understands too late.
Après des jours d'approche (visites au s: After days of approach (visits to the study), they win the Quiet House; Bill's eyes shameful of desire; closed door, total black, mutual hunger; wet bench; Then return to the Quiet House or study; Bill's leaving, Rumaker regrets it. Atmosphere: humidity, mouldy, total black, body heat in the cold Issue: Desire and guilt in a deacralized memorial — Merrill still at Houston in the background.
Rumaker sort de South Lodge vers son stu: Rumaker exits from South Lodge to his study, spot the squatting silhouette of the illuminated bathroom; recognizes Alvin; pass in silence, both in the shadow, towards the Studies. Atmosphere: night, shadows accomplices Issue: Two hidden sexualityes come close without seeing each other — mirror of the homosexuality of Rumaker.
Arrivés de Stuttgart, les grands volumes: Arrived from Stuttgart, large pale blue volumes with large black O brush; Olson, calm, looks at the copy he holds, then the students, without a word — his visible joy; the poorest scrape the three dollars by saving on food and beer. Letter from Olson to Forbes Consequences: Forbes, nourished by stories of decadence and immorality by Nell Rice and others, feels only one: close clean.
